title: Safety and immunogenicity of a first-generation modified vaccinia virus Ankara-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine candidate with mRNA-based booster vaccination: A phase 1 trial
abstract: The rapid development of effective COVID-19 vaccines was enabled by the parallel assessment of multiple candidates early in the pandemic, including candidates based on the Modified Vaccinia virus Ankara (MVA) vector platform. This Phase 1 trial (NCT04569383) evaluated the MVA-based vaccine candidate MVA-SARS-2-S, expressing the full-length native SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (Wuhan-HU-1). Between October 2020 and May 2021, 30 healthy, SARS-CoV-2–naive adults received two doses of either 107 or 108 international units (IU) of MVA-SARS-2-S 28 days apart, with 6-month follow-up. A subgroup (n = 12) received two BNT162b2 booster vaccinations. Safety and reactogenicity were primary objectives; secondary and exploratory objectives included S1 seroconversion rates, S-domain-specific antibodies, SARS-CoV-2-neutralizing antibodies, and spike-specific T cell responses. MVA-SARS-2-S demonstrated a good safety profile. No severe or serious adverse events occurred. Immunogenicity was poor: S1-specific seroconversion occurred in 0/15 (107 IU group) and 3/15 (108 IU group) participants. Binding antibodies were predominantly directed against the S2 subunit, with peak median anti-S2 fold changes of 6.0 and 5.2 in the 107 IU and 108 IU groups, respectively. Neutralizing antibodies were detected in one participant (108 IU group); spike-specific T cell responses were observed in 5/15 (107 IU group) and 2/13 (108 IU group) participants. Heterologous BNT162b2 vaccination induced S1 seroconversion and detectable neutralizing antibody and T cell responses in all boosted participants, without safety concerns. In conclusion, while MVA-SARS-2-S was well tolerated and did not adversely affect subsequent BNT162b2 boosting, the vaccine candidate elicited insufficient immunogenicity, underscoring the need for optimized antigen design.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估带有 mRNA 加强剂的第一代基于 MVA 的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗 候选药物的安全性和免疫原性,解决早期大流行期间对 疫苗 有效的 疫苗 的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项 1 期试验 (NCT04569383) 在 30 名健康、未接受过 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 治疗的成年人中评估了 MVA-SARS-2-S 疫苗 候选药物,这些成年人间隔 28 天接受两剂 107 或 108 IU 的 疫苗,随后进行 6 个月的随访。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究以安全性和反应原性为主要目标,次要目标是测量 S1 血清转化率、S 结构域特异性抗体、严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 中和抗体和尖峰特异性 T 细胞反应。
elements_zh.main_results: MVA-SARS-2-S 显示出良好的安全性,没有报告严重或严重的不良事件。然而,免疫原性较差,107 IU 和 108 IU 组中分别有 0/15 和 3/15 的参与者发生 S1 特异性血清转化。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,虽然 疫苗 具有良好的耐受性,但它引起的免疫原性不足,强调需要优化抗原设计以提高其有效性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,为了使 MVA-SARS-2-S 疫苗 有效,需要进一步优化抗原设计,这可以为未来的 疫苗 开发策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究样本量小且随访有限,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。由于这些限制,证据的强度中等。

title: The impact of COVID-19 vaccination on long COVID prevention in the Omicron era: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on the prevention of long COVID (LC) in the Omicron era through an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods We performed an update of our previously published systematic review and meta-analysis of vaccination and LC risk (searches between 1 January 2022 and 1 March 2024). Databases (Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, Europe PMC, LILACS, Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register) were searched for studies published between 1 March 2024 and 13 July 2026. Observational studies assessing the impact of vaccination on the risk of LC four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection were included. Vaccines were restricted to those centrally authorised in the European Union. Random-effects meta-analyses, restricted to adults, were performed to calculate pooled odds ratios (OR) of LC in three comparisons: vaccinated (any dose) versus unvaccinated; booster vaccination versus unvaccinated; and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination only. Results Nineteen new studies were identified, of which ten were included in the updated meta-analyses alongside eight studies from the original review. The pooled OR of LC in vaccinated adults (any dose) versus unvaccinated was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67–0.84; 13 studies). ORs were also lower for booster vaccination versus unvaccinated (0.73; 95% CI 0.65–0.82; 6 studies), and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination (0.63; 95% CI 0.53–0.75; 6 studies). Significant associations between vaccination and lower LC odds were observed in subgroup analyses of mRNA-only vaccination and LC outcomes three or more months after infection. Conclusions This updated review and meta-analysis reinforces our previous finding that vaccination may reduce the burden of LC in the Omicron era, with booster doses potentially providing additional protection. Although evidence in high-risk groups now prioritised for vaccination in most countries remains limited, these findings clearly demonstrate the benefits of vaccination and support current seasonal vaccination strategies.

title_zh: The impact of COVID-19 vaccination on long COVID prevention in the Omicron era: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis
source_body_en: Abstract Objectives To evaluate the impact of COVID-19 vaccination on the prevention of long COVID (LC) in the Omicron era through an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods We performed an update of our previously published systematic review and meta-analysis of vaccination and LC risk (searches between 1 January 2022 and 1 March 2024). Databases (Embase, MEDLINE, PubMed, Europe PMC, LILACS, Cochrane COVID-19 Study Register) were searched for studies published between 1 March 2024 and 13 July 2026. Observational studies assessing the impact of vaccination on the risk of LC four or more weeks after SARS-CoV-2 infection were included. Vaccines were restricted to those centrally authorised in the European Union. Random-effects meta-analyses, restricted to adults, were performed to calculate pooled odds ratios (OR) of LC in three comparisons: vaccinated (any dose) versus unvaccinated; booster vaccination versus unvaccinated; and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination only. Results Nineteen new studies were identified, of which ten were included in the updated meta-analyses alongside eight studies from the original review. The pooled OR of LC in vaccinated adults (any dose) versus unvaccinated was 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67–0.84; 13 studies). ORs were also lower for booster vaccination versus unvaccinated (0.73; 95% CI 0.65–0.82; 6 studies), and booster vaccination versus primary course vaccination (0.63; 95% CI 0.53–0.75; 6 studies). Significant associations between vaccination and lower LC odds were observed in subgroup analyses of mRNA-only vaccination and LC outcomes three or more months after infection. Conclusions This updated review and meta-analysis reinforces our previous finding that vaccination may reduce the burden of LC in the Omicron era, with booster doses potentially providing additional protection. Although evidence in high-risk groups now prioritised for vaccination in most countries remains limited, these findings clearly demonstrate the benefits of vaccination and support current seasonal vaccination strategies.

title: Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality. We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Papers were required to list specific program content or learning objectives for any educational level or type of health professional. Two authors independently extracted data. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Quantitative data was summarised and reported using frequencies and percentages, learning objectives were mapped across the six Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) telehealth competency domains, and qualitative categories were thematically synthesised. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication. Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. This review highlights that telehealth education and training has expanded since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, however, current curricula are lacking experiential learning. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required. For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines the development of telehealth-related education and training programs since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. Standardized training across disciplines with specialized modules is recommended to optimize resource use.

title_zh: Telehealth-related education and training: a systematic review of recent developments since the COVID-19 pandemic
source_body_en: The pandemic showed the potential of existing telehealth to increase healthcare access but also the need for healthcare workers to be competent and skilled in delivering care through this modality. We undertook a systematic literature review to identify telehealth-related courses developed since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and summarised study characteristics, learning objectives, and course content. Articles describing telehealth-related training and education programs implemented between 2020 and 2024 were included. Papers were required to list specific program content or learning objectives for any educational level or type of health professional. Two authors independently extracted data. Quality of articles was assessed against the SQUIRE 2.0 guidelines. Quantitative data was summarised and reported using frequencies and percentages, learning objectives were mapped across the six Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) telehealth competency domains, and qualitative categories were thematically synthesised. Of 7547 articles identified, 51 were included. Most courses were implemented in the USA (82%), mostly targeted to undergraduate students (51%), and the number of articles per year increased over time. Most courses were developed by universities (53%), sometimes in collaboration with health services, and content was primarily applicable across multiple specialties. Participants nearly always evaluated the courses (90%). Content included basic knowledge and skills in telehealth, patient safety, and ethics, with learning objectives often on technology and communication. Only four programs included all AAMC telehealth competencies. This review highlights that telehealth education and training has expanded since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, however, current curricula are lacking experiential learning. Courses generally covered telehealth communication competencies in detail, but more content on the ethical and legal requirements, billing, physical examination, patient education, and eligibility for telehealth is required. For efficient resource use, standardised training can be applied across disciplines with addition of site or speciality-specific modules.

title: Evaluation of pre-Omicron population immunity for SARS-CoV-2 in the Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation (HIVE) cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: Continued serosurvey for SARS-CoV-2 population immunity is critical for vaccine strain selection and identification of susceptible groups such as young children. We aim to evaluate the use of a high-throughput, low-volume assay to describe strain-specific IgG measurement in a longitudinally followed community based cohort. METHODS: The longitudinal Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation study has observed around 300 households annually for acute respiratory illness. SARS-CoV-2 variant-specific IgG (including original, Delta, Beta, and Omicron variants) concentrations were measured using multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL), pseudoviral neutralization (PN), and ACE2 inhibition assays in participants who had serum samples drawn between July 1 and December 31, 2021. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient assessed correlation within and between ECL, ACE2, and PN assays. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the performance of ECL and ACE2 assays. Generalized additive mixed models estimated population immunity by age against SARS-CoV-2 variants. RESULTS: A total of 156 serum samples from 117 participants were selected for this study. Most (65.8%) were from adults and a majority (77.8%) received vaccination during the analysis period. High correlations were observed within ECL IgG assays (0.95-1.00), within ACE2 inhibition assays (0.70-0.99), and between assay platforms, including ECL versus PN (0.81-0.83) and ACE2 versus PN (0.88-0.95). SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations generally increased with age and appeared to plateau in early adulthood, although estimates were imprecise in younger age groups because of small sample sizes. CONCLUSION: We found a high correlation between ECL, ACE2, and PN across variants. Age-specific IgG quantities reflected behavior and infection histories collected by active surveillance.

title_zh: 家庭流感中 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的前 Omicron 群体免疫力评估 疫苗 评估 (HIVE) 队列研究
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Continued serosurvey for SARS-CoV-2 population immunity is critical for vaccine strain selection and identification of susceptible groups such as young children. We aim to evaluate the use of a high-throughput, low-volume assay to describe strain-specific IgG measurement in a longitudinally followed community based cohort. METHODS: The longitudinal Household Influenza Vaccine Evaluation study has observed around 300 households annually for acute respiratory illness. SARS-CoV-2 variant-specific IgG (including original, Delta, Beta, and Omicron variants) concentrations were measured using multiplex electrochemiluminescence (ECL), pseudoviral neutralization (PN), and ACE2 inhibition assays in participants who had serum samples drawn between July 1 and December 31, 2021. Spearman's rank correlation coefficient assessed correlation within and between ECL, ACE2, and PN assays. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated the performance of ECL and ACE2 assays. Generalized additive mixed models estimated population immunity by age against SARS-CoV-2 variants. RESULTS: A total of 156 serum samples from 117 participants were selected for this study. Most (65.8%) were from adults and a majority (77.8%) received vaccination during the analysis period. High correlations were observed within ECL IgG assays (0.95-1.00), within ACE2 inhibition assays (0.70-0.99), and between assay platforms, including ECL versus PN (0.81-0.83) and ACE2 versus PN (0.88-0.95). SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations generally increased with age and appeared to plateau in early adulthood, although estimates were imprecise in younger age groups because of small sample sizes. CONCLUSION: We found a high correlation between ECL, ACE2, and PN across variants. Age-specific IgG quantities reflected behavior and infection histories collected by active surveillance.

title: Longitudinal BCR repertoire dynamics reveal the evolution of broadly binding antibodies following heterologous SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and breakthrough infection: a single-donor case study
abstract: Continued SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift and the persistent risk of zoonotic sarbecovirus spillover highlight the need for broadly protective countermeasures. Here, we longitudinally profiled the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire of a single volunteer who received heterologous booster vaccination followed by Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection, integrating bulk BCR sequencing with single B-cell culture and antibody binding analysis. Breakthrough infection was associated with broadened serum neutralization across SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses, consistent with recall of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes. Repertoire analysis revealed stage-specific remodeling, with high-affinity binding antibodies shifting from an IGHV1-46-enriched profile after vaccination to preferential representation of IGHV3-30-3 after infection. Isolated monoclonal antibodies exhibited nanomolar-to-picomolar binding affinities to diverse animal-derived sarbecovirus spikes, with broad binding commonly, but not universally, associated with CDRH3 lengths of 14-16 amino acids. Phylogenetic and sequence analyses defined divergent evolutionary trajectories for IGHV1-46 and IGHV3-30-3 lineages, highlighting candidate genetic features that warrant validation in larger cohorts. Together, these findings describe how sequential heterologous antigen exposures can reshape the humoral repertoire in one individual and generate hypotheses for future pan-sarbecovirus antibody and vaccine studies.

title_zh: 纵向 BCR 库动态揭示了异源 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗接种 和突破性感染后广泛结合抗体的 进化:单一供体案例研究
source_body_en: Continued SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift and the persistent risk of zoonotic sarbecovirus spillover highlight the need for broadly protective countermeasures. Here, we longitudinally profiled the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire of a single volunteer who received heterologous booster vaccination followed by Omicron BF.7 breakthrough infection, integrating bulk BCR sequencing with single B-cell culture and antibody binding analysis. Breakthrough infection was associated with broadened serum neutralization across SARS-CoV-2 variants and related sarbecoviruses, consistent with recall of antibodies targeting conserved epitopes. Repertoire analysis revealed stage-specific remodeling, with high-affinity binding antibodies shifting from an IGHV1-46-enriched profile after vaccination to preferential representation of IGHV3-30-3 after infection. Isolated monoclonal antibodies exhibited nanomolar-to-picomolar binding affinities to diverse animal-derived sarbecovirus spikes, with broad binding commonly, but not universally, associated with CDRH3 lengths of 14-16 amino acids. Phylogenetic and sequence analyses defined divergent evolutionary trajectories for IGHV1-46 and IGHV3-30-3 lineages, highlighting candidate genetic features that warrant validation in larger cohorts. Together, these findings describe how sequential heterologous antigen exposures can reshape the humoral repertoire in one individual and generate hypotheses for future pan-sarbecovirus antibody and vaccine studies.

title: Genomic surveillance of COVID-19 in Hong Kong (2020-2023): Analysing SARS-CoV-2 variants, mutations, and their impact on viral entry.
abstract: Abstract We analysed 15,982 quality-controlled SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences from Hong Kong, obtained from NCBI and GISAID between 2020 and 2023, to characterize lineage dynamics, mutational profiles, demographic distributions, and variant-specific viral entry. Genomic surveillance identified 543 lineages and 5,982 unique mutations. Lineages A, B, and B.4 dominated the initial epidemic waves, whereas Delta and Omicron emerged and predominated in later waves. Omicron BA.1 and BA.2 exhibited distinct distributions across gender and age groups, while JN.1 harboured several novel mutations. Molecular simulations comparing spike receptor-binding domain (SRBD)–ACE2 interactions revealed significant differences in binding affinity among variants (F = 4.404, p = 9.12 × 10−7). JN.1 demonstrated enhanced ACE2-binding affinity, suggesting increased viral entry and potential transmissibility. By integrating genomic, demographic, and molecular evidence, this study provides a comprehensive account of SARS-CoV-2 evolution in Hong Kong and highlights the public health relevance of emerging variants. These findings support sustained genomic surveillance and demographic monitoring to strengthen pandemic preparedness. Future research should evaluate public health strategies and adopt holistic frameworks integrating population characteristics with genomic evidence to mitigate the effects of future variants.

title: Protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during Omicron KP.3 wave
abstract: BACKGROUND: Data are limited on the protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against Omicron KP.3 infection. METHODS: Among 1826 tertiary hospital staff in Tokyo who had received three or more doses of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and provided blood samples in June 2024, we prospectively examined the associations of XBB.1.5 vaccination and previous infection (classified by the timing of the last infection as pre-Omicron XBB, Omicron XBB, or Omicron JN.1 waves) with the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron KP.3 wave (June to September 2024). In a nested case-control analysis, we compared pre-infection live-virus KP.3.3-neutralizing antibody titers between cases and 1: 1 propensity-score matched controls. RESULTS: XBB.1.5 vaccination was not associated with measurable protection against symptomatic infection (4%, 95% CI, -88 to 51). Previous infection conferred protection that increased with its recency: 26% (95% CI, -26 to 56) for pre-Omicron XBB, 44% (95% CI, 2 to 68) for Omicron XBB, and 89% (95% CI, 52 to 97) for Omicron JN.1 waves. Pre-infection KP.3.3-neutralizing titers tended to be lower in cases than in matched controls (GMT ratio 0.68, 95% CI, 0.35 to 1.33); KP.3.3-neutralizing activity was only modestly elevated by XBB.1.5 vaccination but markedly higher after recent JN.1 infection. CONCLUSIONS: During the Omicron KP.3 wave, when an updated vaccine was unavailable, XBB.1.5 vaccination administered approximately 7 months earlier conferred no measurable neutralizing activity or protection against symptomatic KP.3 infection. Previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly recent JN.1-wave infection, affords substantial neutralizing titers and protection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the protective efficacy of the Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine and previous SARS-CoV-2 infection against symptomatic Omicron KP.3 infection during the KP.3 wave in Tokyo. Among 1826 tertiary hospital staff who had received three or more doses of mRNA vaccines, the study found that XBB.1.5 vaccination did not provide measurable protection against KP.3 infection. In contrast, previous infection conferred protection, with the highest level observed for recent JN.1-wave infections. The study used a nested case-control design, comparing neutralizing antibody titers between cases and matched controls. The findings suggest that natural immunity from recent infections may offer stronger protection than vaccination against emerging variants. However, the study's results are limited by the lack of an updated vaccine during the KP.3 wave, and the evidence for vaccine efficacy is weak. These results have implications for understanding the role of vaccination and natural immunity in protecting against new variants of SARS-CoV-2.

title_zh: 对 Omicron XBB.1.5 疫苗、既往感染及其在 Omicron KP.3 波期间针对症状性 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染诱导的中和抗体的保护
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Data are limited on the protection of Omicron XBB.1.5 vaccine, previous infection, and their induced neutralizing antibodies against Omicron KP.3 infection. METHODS: Among 1826 tertiary hospital staff in Tokyo who had received three or more doses of COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and provided blood samples in June 2024, we prospectively examined the associations of XBB.1.5 vaccination and previous infection (classified by the timing of the last infection as pre-Omicron XBB, Omicron XBB, or Omicron JN.1 waves) with the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron KP.3 wave (June to September 2024). In a nested case-control analysis, we compared pre-infection live-virus KP.3.3-neutralizing antibody titers between cases and 1: 1 propensity-score matched controls. RESULTS: XBB.1.5 vaccination was not associated with measurable protection against symptomatic infection (4%, 95% CI, -88 to 51). Previous infection conferred protection that increased with its recency: 26% (95% CI, -26 to 56) for pre-Omicron XBB, 44% (95% CI, 2 to 68) for Omicron XBB, and 89% (95% CI, 52 to 97) for Omicron JN.1 waves. Pre-infection KP.3.3-neutralizing titers tended to be lower in cases than in matched controls (GMT ratio 0.68, 95% CI, 0.35 to 1.33); KP.3.3-neutralizing activity was only modestly elevated by XBB.1.5 vaccination but markedly higher after recent JN.1 infection. CONCLUSIONS: During the Omicron KP.3 wave, when an updated vaccine was unavailable, XBB.1.5 vaccination administered approximately 7 months earlier conferred no measurable neutralizing activity or protection against symptomatic KP.3 infection. Previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly recent JN.1-wave infection, affords substantial neutralizing titers and protection.

title: SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein hijacks host transcription by targeting eEF1A1
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 variants display substantial genetic and phenotypic diversity, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects on host gene regulation need further investigation. We performed a transcriptomic analysis of host responses to multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron. Despite their divergence, all variants induced a conserved transcriptional program in human lung epithelial cells characterized by activation of interferon regulatory factors (IRFs), immediate–early genes, and downstream cytokines. We identify the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein as a central driver of this transcriptional reprogramming, as N expression alone partially recapitulated the host response to infection. Mechanistically, N promotes recruitment of interferon regulatory factors and AP-1 transcription factors, RNA polymerase II, and the elongation factor eEF1A1 to promoters of pro-inflammatory genes, revealing a previously unrecognized nuclear role for eEF1A1. Disruption of the N-eEF1A1 interaction, genetically or pharmacologically using the eEF1A interactant plitidepsin, abolished transcriptional complex formation and reversed host gene dysregulation, identifying a conserved host–virus regulatory axis and potential pan-variant therapeutic target.

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳蛋白通过靶向 eEF1A1 劫持 宿主 转录
source_body_en: SARS-CoV-2 variants display substantial genetic and phenotypic diversity, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects on host gene regulation need further investigation. We performed a transcriptomic analysis of host responses to multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta and Omicron. Despite their divergence, all variants induced a conserved transcriptional program in human lung epithelial cells characterized by activation of interferon regulatory factors (IRFs), immediate–early genes, and downstream cytokines. We identify the viral nucleocapsid (N) protein as a central driver of this transcriptional reprogramming, as N expression alone partially recapitulated the host response to infection. Mechanistically, N promotes recruitment of interferon regulatory factors and AP-1 transcription factors, RNA polymerase II, and the elongation factor eEF1A1 to promoters of pro-inflammatory genes, revealing a previously unrecognized nuclear role for eEF1A1. Disruption of the N-eEF1A1 interaction, genetically or pharmacologically using the eEF1A interactant plitidepsin, abolished transcriptional complex formation and reversed host gene dysregulation, identifying a conserved host–virus regulatory axis and potential pan-variant therapeutic target.

title: A Genome-Wide Association Study in the Chilean admixed population reveals four new loci for COVID-19 severity and susceptibility
abstract: ABSTRACT Background More than five years after the COVID-19 outbreak, the infection by the SARS-CoV-2 virus should still be considered as a global threat with highly heterogeneous clinical outcomes from asymptomatic to fatal depending on existing genetic and phenotypic inter-individual and inter-population variability. Our objective is to identify risk loci associated with COVID-19 in an admixed Latin American population. Methods We performed a genome-wide association study in the framework of the Chilean C19-GenoNet team, analyzing a cohort of 3,417 individuals recruited from the northernmost to the southernmost regions of the country, who presented variations in the severity of their COVID-19 clinical manifestations. Results Our investigation replicated the extensively reported association of several variants at the 3p21.31 locus with COVID-19 severity and found a suggestive association for a variant within the FOXP4 gene at 6p21.1 with COVID-19 hospitalization. Both associations appear to be shared with other populations. Importantly, our study identified three previously unreported loci associated with COVID-19 severity or hospitalization at 7q21.11, 16p13.12 and 6p25.3, and one additional locus at 4p13 associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity, a proxy for infection susceptibility. Conclusions these new risk loci may represent population-specific effects in Chilean and, potentially, other Latin American admixed groups. Our study highlights the importance of expanding efforts to study underrepresented and genetically different populations, which may provide new clues on the genetic basis of human diseases and may help to anticipate global responses to emerging viral infections and future pandemics.

title_zh: A Genome-Wide Association Study in the Chilean admixed population reveals four new loci for COVID-19 severity and susceptibility
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background More than five years after the COVID-19 outbreak, the infection by the SARS-CoV-2 virus should still be considered as a global threat with highly heterogeneous clinical outcomes from asymptomatic to fatal depending on existing genetic and phenotypic inter-individual and inter-population variability. Our objective is to identify risk loci associated with COVID-19 in an admixed Latin American population. Methods We performed a genome-wide association study in the framework of the Chilean C19-GenoNet team, analyzing a cohort of 3,417 individuals recruited from the northernmost to the southernmost regions of the country, who presented variations in the severity of their COVID-19 clinical manifestations. Results Our investigation replicated the extensively reported association of several variants at the 3p21.31 locus with COVID-19 severity and found a suggestive association for a variant within the FOXP4 gene at 6p21.1 with COVID-19 hospitalization. Both associations appear to be shared with other populations. Importantly, our study identified three previously unreported loci associated with COVID-19 severity or hospitalization at 7q21.11, 16p13.12 and 6p25.3, and one additional locus at 4p13 associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity, a proxy for infection susceptibility. Conclusions these new risk loci may represent population-specific effects in Chilean and, potentially, other Latin American admixed groups. Our study highlights the importance of expanding efforts to study underrepresented and genetically different populations, which may provide new clues on the genetic basis of human diseases and may help to anticipate global responses to emerging viral infections and future pandemics.

title: Germinal center dynamics in the mediastinal lymph node distinguish time-dependent and variant-specific immunity during SARS-CoV-2 secondary exposure
abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 secondary infections remain a persistent challenge even though individuals have previous immunity from natural infection or vaccination. Yet, the cellular mechanisms that determine whether a secondary exposure is rapidly controlled by pre-existing immunity and results in sterilizing protection or progresses to productive infection and disease remain poorly understood. Using homologous and heterologous secondary-challenge experimental strategies in C57BL/6J mice, we show that protection against a homologous SARS-CoV-2 Alpha secondary challenge in previously infected mice is time-limited, remaining durable through 56 days post-primary infection, with breakthrough infection on day 84 post-primary infection. This loss of protection was not associated with waning neutralizing antibody titers but instead correlated with progressive contraction of T follicular helper cells and germinal center B cells in the mediastinal lymph node. In contrast, heterologous Beta secondary exposure in Alpha-previously infected mice consistently failed to mount a robust germinal center response despite mobilizing comparable or greater numbers of immune cells than homologous re-challenge. Instead, RNA-seq and flow cytometry analyses revealed that this response was associated with an inflammatory extrafollicular B cell response characterized by reduced Bcl6 and Aicda expression and concomitant robust upregulation of Il6 . Taken together, these findings identify the germinal center recall response in the mediastinal lymph node as an important cellular correlate of SARS-CoV-2 secondary immunity and carry direct implications for the timing of booster immunization and the design of cross-variant vaccines.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用 C57BL/6J 小鼠进行同源和异源二次攻击实验,以研究 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 免疫。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究在 C57BL/6J 小鼠中采用同源和异源二次攻击实验策略,利用 RNA-seq 和流式细胞术分析来评估 免疫应答。

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 二次暴露期间纵隔淋巴结生发中心动态区分时间依赖性和变异特异性免疫
source_body_en: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 secondary infections remain a persistent challenge even though individuals have previous immunity from natural infection or vaccination. Yet, the cellular mechanisms that determine whether a secondary exposure is rapidly controlled by pre-existing immunity and results in sterilizing protection or progresses to productive infection and disease remain poorly understood. Using homologous and heterologous secondary-challenge experimental strategies in C57BL/6J mice, we show that protection against a homologous SARS-CoV-2 Alpha secondary challenge in previously infected mice is time-limited, remaining durable through 56 days post-primary infection, with breakthrough infection on day 84 post-primary infection. This loss of protection was not associated with waning neutralizing antibody titers but instead correlated with progressive contraction of T follicular helper cells and germinal center B cells in the mediastinal lymph node. In contrast, heterologous Beta secondary exposure in Alpha-previously infected mice consistently failed to mount a robust germinal center response despite mobilizing comparable or greater numbers of immune cells than homologous re-challenge. Instead, RNA-seq and flow cytometry analyses revealed that this response was associated with an inflammatory extrafollicular B cell response characterized by reduced Bcl6 and Aicda expression and concomitant robust upregulation of Il6 . Taken together, these findings identify the germinal center recall response in the mediastinal lymph node as an important cellular correlate of SARS-CoV-2 secondary immunity and carry direct implications for the timing of booster immunization and the design of cross-variant vaccines.
abstract_zh: 摘要:即使个体先前对自然感染或 疫苗接种 具有免疫力,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 继发感染仍然是一个持续的挑战。然而,对于决定二次暴露是否受到预先存在的免疫力快速控制并导致消毒保护或进展为生产性感染和疾病的细胞机制仍知之甚少。在 C57BL/6J 小鼠中使用同源和异源二次攻击实验策略,我们表明,对先前感染的小鼠的同源 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Alpha 二次攻击的保护是有时间限制的,在初次感染后 56 天保持持久,在初次感染后第 84 天突破感染。这种保护的丧失与中和抗体滴度的减弱无关,而是与纵隔淋巴结中滤泡辅助T细胞和生发中心B细胞的进行性收缩相关。相比之下,先前感染α的小鼠中的异源β二次暴露始终未能产生强有力的生发中心反应,尽管与同源再次攻击相比动员了相当或更多数量的免疫细胞。相反,RNA-seq 和流式细胞术分析表明,这种反应与滤泡外 B 细胞炎症反应相关,其特征是 Bcl6 和 Aicda 表达减少,同时 Il6 强烈上调。总而言之,这些发现确定纵隔淋巴结中的生发中心回忆反应是 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 二次免疫的重要细胞相关性,并对加强免疫的时机和交叉变体 疫苗 的设计具有直接影响。

title: Vaccination and Non-School NPIs Shaped Ontario's Pre-Omicron COVID-19 Hospital Burden
abstract: We develop an age- and immunity-structured COVID-19 model with setting-specific contacts, calibrated to Ontario incidence and hospital admissions before Omicron. We simulate counterfactual vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in schools, workplaces, and other community settings, evaluating projected severe-case demand against an illustrative healthcare-capacity benchmark. Vaccination combined with workplace and community contact restrictions keeps simulated demand within capacity. In contrast, relaxing restrictions in either setting produces large surges and repeated capacity threats, even when school restrictions remain. School-only changes produce smaller effects on severe disease. These findings highlight the value of vaccination and setting-specific contact restrictions that prioritize workplace and community settings for pathogens with adult-concentrated severe outcomes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate how vaccination and non-school non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) influenced the hospital burden of COVID-19 in Ontario before the Omicron variant emerged, addressing the need to understand the impact of these measures on severe disease outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a counterfactual simulation approach to model the effects of different vaccination strategies and contact restrictions in workplaces and community settings, alongside school restrictions, on the projected demand for hospital beds in Ontario during the pre-Omicron period.
analysis.methods: The researchers developed an age- and immunity-structured model calibrated to Ontario's incidence and hospital admission data, simulating various scenarios of vaccination and contact restrictions to assess their impact on severe-case demand.
analysis.main_results: Relaxing contact restrictions in workplaces or community settings led to large surges in severe-case demand, even when school restrictions remained in place. School-only changes had smaller effects on severe disease outcomes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that combining vaccination with targeted contact restrictions in adult-dominated settings is more effective in managing hospital demand than relying solely on school-based interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform public health strategies by emphasizing the importance of prioritizing workplace and community contact restrictions alongside vaccination to mitigate severe outcomes of SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on simulated data and does not account for real-world variability, which may limit the generalizability of its findings. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the model-based nature of the analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of vaccination and non-school non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) on the hospital burden of pre-Omicron SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario. Using a counterfactual simulation model, the researchers assess how varying levels of vaccination and contact restrictions in workplaces and community settings affect severe-case demand. They find that relaxing restrictions in these adult-concentrated environments leads to significant surges in hospital demand, even with school restrictions in place. In contrast, school-only changes have smaller effects on severe disease outcomes. The study highlights the importance of prioritizing workplace and community-based NPIs in conjunction with vaccination to manage hospital capacity. However, the reliance on simulated data introduces limitations, reducing the strength of the evidence to moderate.

title: Fitness flux in SARS-CoV-2 and influenza H3N2
abstract: The tempo of viral adaptation is usually read indirectly from the composition of mutations, through measures such as dN/dS. Here we measure it directly from the dynamics of variant frequencies, where we use multinomial logistic regression to estimate a fitness for each co-circulating variant. We aggregate these estimates to derive the rate of change of mean population fitness, referred to as fitness flux. Tracing SARS-CoV-2 from its emergence, we find that it initially adapted rapidly, doubling in fitness every 6 months from Jan 2021 to Jun 2022, but slowing to every 2.4 years from Jul 2022 to Dec 2025. Seasonal influenza H3N2 sustained a slower, steadier pace doubling in fitness every 10.0 years. In both, the rate of fitness gain closely tracks the variance in fitness, matching the 1:1 expectation of Fisher’s fundamental theorem. Phylogenetic contrasts between parent and child lineages localize most fitness gain to spike, and within spike to the receptor-binding domain, where a simple count of spike S1 substitutions predicts lineage fitness about as well as deep-learning escape and protein-language-model scores. Measuring fitness directly thus offers a transparent, frequency-based alternative to mutational proxies for tracking and anticipating viral adaptation. The website blab.github.io/fitness-flux/ is the intended reading experience of this paper, providing responsive layout and interactive figures.

title: Global burden of type 2 diabetes attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Objective We aimed to quantify the association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and the risk of incident diabetes. We also aimed to estimate the global burden of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D) attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL from inception to 29 January 2026. Adjusted relative risks (RRs) for incident T2D and type 1 diabetes (T1D) following SARS-CoV-2 infection were pooled using random-effects models. Population attributable fractions (PAFs) and attributable T2D cases were estimated by integrating pooled risk estimates with Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data on COVID-19 prevalence and T2D incidence. Results Fifteen cohort studies involving approximately 48.9 million participants were included. SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with an increased risk of incident T2D (13 studies; pooled RR, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.16–1.34]), although substantial heterogeneity was observed and the 95% prediction interval (PI) included the null (0.94–1.66). In subgroup analysis, the association was confined to mixed-variant studies (RR, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.23–1.36]; 95% PI, 1.09–1.54), whereas studies evaluating a single variant (Delta or Omicron) showed no excess risk (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.97–1.03]). The association with incident T1D did not reach conventional statistical significance (10 studies; pooled RR, 1.13 [95% CI, 0.99–1.30]). Globally, 24.53 million incident T2D cases occurred in 2023. The PAF attributable to COVID-19 of 1.12% (95% CI 0.90, 1.35), corresponding to 274,889 (95% CI 220,360, 331,698) incident T2D cases attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. The largest attributable burdens were observed in India, the USA, and China. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a modest increase in pooled T2D risk. This association was primarily observed in mixed-variant studies, for which the 95% PI excluded the null. However, the overall pooled estimated was accompanied by substantial between-study heterogeneity, and its 95% PI crossing the null, indicating uncertainty in the association across populations and settings. At the population level, this excess risk translated into an estimated 275,000 incident T2D cases attributable to COVID-19 worldwide in 2023, highlighting the need for ongoing metabolic surveillance following infection. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261307969 , identifier CRD420261307969.

analysis.summary_en: This review quantifies the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D). A systematic review and meta-analysis of 15 cohort studies involving 48.9 million participants found a modest increased risk of T2D following SARS-CoV-2 infection (pooled RR, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.16–1.34]), although heterogeneity and a 95% prediction interval that included the null suggest uncertainty. title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染导致 2 型糖尿病的全球负担
source_body_en: Objective We aimed to quantify the association between severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection and the risk of incident diabetes. We also aimed to estimate the global burden of incident type 2 diabetes (T2D) attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and CENTRAL from inception to 29 January 2026. Adjusted relative risks (RRs) for incident T2D and type 1 diabetes (T1D) following SARS-CoV-2 infection were pooled using random-effects models. Population attributable fractions (PAFs) and attributable T2D cases were estimated by integrating pooled risk estimates with Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 data on COVID-19 prevalence and T2D incidence. Results Fifteen cohort studies involving approximately 48.9 million participants were included. SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with an increased risk of incident T2D (13 studies; pooled RR, 1.25 [95% CI, 1.16–1.34]), although substantial heterogeneity was observed and the 95% prediction interval (PI) included the null (0.94–1.66). In subgroup analysis, the association was confined to mixed-variant studies (RR, 1.29 [95% CI, 1.23–1.36]; 95% PI, 1.09–1.54), whereas studies evaluating a single variant (Delta or Omicron) showed no excess risk (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.97–1.03]). The association with incident T1D did not reach conventional statistical significance (10 studies; pooled RR, 1.13 [95% CI, 0.99–1.30]). Globally, 24.53 million incident T2D cases occurred in 2023. The PAF attributable to COVID-19 of 1.12% (95% CI 0.90, 1.35), corresponding to 274,889 (95% CI 220,360, 331,698) incident T2D cases attributable to SARS-CoV-2 infection. The largest attributable burdens were observed in India, the USA, and China. Conclusions SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a modest increase in pooled T2D risk. This association was primarily observed in mixed-variant studies, for which the 95% PI excluded the null. However, the overall pooled estimated was accompanied by substantial between-study heterogeneity, and its 95% PI crossing the null, indicating uncertainty in the association across populations and settings. At the population level, this excess risk translated into an estimated 275,000 incident T2D cases attributable to COVID-19 worldwide in 2023, highlighting the need for ongoing metabolic surveillance following infection. title: Pathophysiology of Lung Cancer in the Context of SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern
abstract: Many retrospective cohort studies have revealed that patients with cancer are at increased risk of severe complications and mortality from COVID-19 due to a multitude of factors, including advanced age in this cohort, high incidence of underlying comorbidities, and immunosuppression caused by cancer and its treatments. It has been futher demonstrated that individuals with lung cancer face a disproportionately higher risk of mortality compared to other cancer types following SARS-SoV-2 infection. However, several questions remain unanswered regarding the understanding of the pathophysiology of lung cancer in the context of COVID-19, as well as the effects of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern on patient outcomes. The article aims to investigate the following gaps the clinical manifestation of SARS-CoV-2 infection in patients with lung cancer: the molecular characteristics of lung cancer driving the development of severe COVID-19, and the role of COVID-19-induced inflammation in accelerating the development and increasing the severity of lung cancer, particularly with respect to the Alpha (B.1.1.7), Beta (B.1.351), Gamma (P.1) and Delta (B.1.617.2) variants. Understanding the crosstalk between lung cancer and COVID-19, particularly concerning the early variants of concern, will reveal the unique mechanisms contributing to poor outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 in patients with lung cancer, including the maintenance of a hyperinflammatory state, TMPRSS2 expression patterns, and tumor-associated immune evasion, among others. This work will be valuable in the development of improved antivirals and vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 in the cancer population and will help provide insight into the pathogenesis of current and emerging variants of concern in this at-risk cohort. Additional studies and a high degree of caution are essential in understanding the impacts of newer and emerging variants of concern such as Omicron (B.1.1.529) and its subvariants on patients with lung cancer.

title: Informing risk stratification and vaccine policy via a predictive mathematical model of SARS-COV-2 infection
abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 human challenge studies enabled unprecedented high frequency temporal measurements of immune determinants of viral control. We integrated prior knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 replication, innate, cytotoxic T cell and antibody responses into a dynamic model which captured viral-load kinetics in seronegative volunteers challenged with wildtype virus. The model predicted measured innate and adaptive immune dynamics. Perturbation analyses indicated that innate immunity limits peak viral load, whereas antibodies principally mediate clearance while cytotoxic T cells become critical in antibody deficiency. Pre-existing antibodies suppressed both viral replication and subsequent immune activation- a prediction validated in a second challenge study of seropositive participants infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant. The model explains how specific immunodeficiencies may increase susceptibility to severe or persistent infection, supporting clinical risk stratification. It suggests that T cell-targeted vaccination strategies may provide limited protection without effective neutralising antibodies, and that attenuated boosting after low-dose exposure requires repeated vaccination to reduce breakthrough infections, informing public health policy. One Sentence Summary A mathematical model of SARS-COV-2 infection predicts innate and adaptive immunity, and informs risk stratification and vaccine policy.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to inform risk stratification and vaccine policy by understanding the role of immune responses in controlling SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A predictive mathematical model was developed using data from seronegative volunteers challenged with wildtype SARS-CoV-2, capturing viral-load kinetics and immune dynamics.
analysis.methods: The model integrated prior knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 replication, innate, cytotoxic T cell and antibody responses, and was validated through perturbation analyses and a second challenge study of seropositive participants.
analysis.main_results: Perturbation analyses indicated that innate immunity limits peak viral load, whereas antibodies primarily mediate clearance, and cytotoxic T cells become critical in antibody deficiency. Pre-existing antibodies suppressed both viral replication and immune activation, a finding validated in a second challenge study.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The model provides novel insights into how specific immunodeficiencies may increase susceptibility to severe or persistent infection, supporting clinical risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the development of clinical risk stratification tools and inform vaccine policy by highlighting the importance of neutralising antibodies in protection against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a mathematical model and challenge studies, which may have limited generalisability to real-world populations, but the evidence is supported by validation in a second challenge study.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a predictive mathematical model of SARS-CoV-2 infection that integrates prior knowledge of viral replication and immune responses. The model was validated using data from seronegative volunteers challenged with wildtype SARS-CoV-2 and a second challenge study of seropositive participants infected with the Delta variant. The results indicate that innate immunity limits peak viral load, while antibodies primarily mediate clearance, with cytotoxic T cells playing a critical role in antibody deficiency. The model suggests that pre-existing antibodies suppress viral replication and immune activation, offering insights into immunodeficiencies that may increase susceptibility to severe infection. These findings support clinical risk stratification and inform vaccine policy by emphasizing the need for neutralising antibodies. The study's reliance on challenge studies and mathematical modeling may limit its generalisability, but the evidence is strengthened by validation in a second study.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该模型提供了关于特定免疫缺陷如何增加对严重或持续感染的易感性的新见解,支持临床风险分层。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持临床风险分层工具的开发,并通过强调中和抗体在保护 against 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 中的重要性,为 疫苗 政策提供依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于数学模型和挑战研究,这可能对现实世界人群的普遍性有限,但证据得到了第二次挑战研究验证的支持。

abstract_zh: 摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 人类挑战研究实现了病毒控制免疫决定因素前所未有的高频时间测量。我们将 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 复制、先天细胞毒性 T 细胞和抗体反应的先验知识整合到一个动态模型中,该模型捕获了接受野生型病毒攻击的血清阴性志愿者的病毒载量动力学。该模型预测了测量到的先天和适应性免疫动态。扰动分析表明,先天免疫限制了病毒载量峰值,而抗体主要介导清除,而细胞毒性 T 细胞在抗体缺乏中变得至关重要。预先存在的抗体抑制了病毒复制和随后的免疫激活——这一预测在感染 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Delta 变体的血清阳性参与者的第二项挑战研究中得到了验证。该模型解释了特异性免疫缺陷如何增加对严重或持续感染的易感性,支持临床风险分层。这表明,在没有有效中和抗体的情况下,针对 T 细胞的 疫苗接种 策略可能提供有限的保护,并且低剂量暴露后减弱的增强作用需要重复 疫苗接种 来减少突破性感染,从而为公共卫生政策提供信息。一句话总结 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的数学模型可以预测先天性和适应性免疫,并为风险分层和 疫苗 策略提供信息。

title: Immune parameters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients during SARS-CoV2 delta and omicron waves.
abstract: Understanding immune mechanisms associated with COVID-19 severity remains important for interpreting clinical outcomes. We investigated virological and immunological profiles in 39-patients hospitalized with COVID-19 at InCor Hospital during the Delta and Omicron waves and included 28-non-hospitalized individuals with moderate COVID-19 as a comparator group for cytokine analyses. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed by RT-PCR from nasopharyngeal swabs, and viral variants were identified by next-generation sequencing. RNAemia was assessed by RT-PCR and analyzed as a binary variable. Serum cytokines were quantified by cytometric bead array, while humoral responses were evaluated by anti-Spike RBD IgG levels using CLIA and a Wuhan-Hu-1-based pseudovirus neutralization assay. RNAemia was more frequent in ICU-admitted patients than in non-ICU patients, supporting an association with disease severity. Cytokine profiling showed increased IL-6, IL-8, TNF, IL-17 A and IL-10 levels in hospitalized patients compared with moderate COVID-19 individuals, but did not distinguish recovered from deceased patients. Neutralizing antibody titers measured against a Wuhan-Hu-1 spike pseudovirus were significantly higher in recovered individuals than decease patients, underscoring the relevance of antibody functionality. These data emphasize the relevance of viral dissemination and functional humoral immunity as potential biomarkers for COVID-19 progression and outcome, with RNAemia and neutralizing antibody levels showing a stronger exploratory association in this cohort.

title: Impact of Community Factors on Mental and Physical Health During Successive Waves of COVID-19 Pandemic in China.
abstract: This study examined how community factors impacted well-being during the COVID-19 pandemic in China. Data were collected at two time points: Time 1 (T1) in September 2021 (N = 992) when COVID-19 cases stabilized, and Time 2 (T2) in January 2023 (N = 497) during a sudden outbreak of new infected cases. At T1, perceived community safety and sense of community directly affected depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms, with sense of community partially mediating these effects. At T2, community factors at T1 continued to impact depression, anxiety, and physical health symptoms. Sense of community at T1 partially mediated the link between community safety at T1 and mental health at T2. Higher income and older age were associated with a stronger sense of community, better perceived community safety, and improved health. Policymakers should consider the impact of community factors on well-being during health crises.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of community factors on mental and physical health during successive waves of the COVID-19 pandemic in China. Data were collected at two time points: September 2021 (N = 992) when cases stabilized and January 2023 (N = 497) during a sudden outbreak. The findings showed that community factors at the first time point continued to influence mental and physical health at the second time point. Specifically, sense of community at T1 partially mediated the relationship between community safety at T1 and mental health at T2. Higher income and older age were linked to better community safety and improved health outcomes. The study highlights the importance of community factors in shaping well-being during health crises and suggests that policymakers should consider these factors in their strategies. The evidence is based on data collected from two time points, and the study provides insights into the long-term effects of community dynamics on health outcomes.

title: Association between COVID-19 vaccination, SARS-CoV-2 infection, and oral lichen planus (OLP) flares: Results from a patient survey
abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic immune-mediated mucocutaneous disease. During the COVID-19 pandemic, new cases and flares of OLP were reported after SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination. Immune activation and cytokine release triggered by infection or vaccines are proposed mechanisms, although current evidence is limited. Clarifying this relationship is important for improving patient counseling and management during vaccination efforts. OBJECTIVES: The study aimed to explore the association with an increased occurrence of OLP flares following COVID-19 vaccination or infection. MATERIAL AND METHODS: An 11-question survey was distributed to OLP patients. The questionnaire aimed to inquire about the history of COVID-19 vaccination and infection as it related to subjective flares of OLP (oral redness, ulcerations, pain, or discomfort). Associations with complications were assessed with Fisher's exact or Wilcoxon tests. RESULTS: Seventy-six patients participated in the survey. Twenty percent of study participants reported experiencing a flare after COVID-19 vaccination (n = 13), and 33% after an infection (n = 13). Self-reported OLP flares were significantly associated with whether or not participants also reported vaccine side effects (p = 0.005). Among the 27 participants who reported experiencing systemic post-vaccination side effects (tiredness, headache, muscle pain, chills, fever, nausea), 37% (n = 10) also reported an OLP flare compared with 8% (n = 3) of the 38 who did not report systemic side effects from the COVID-19 vaccination. Of the 63 participants who received a 2nd vaccine dose, 21% (n = 13) reported experiencing an OLP flare. Experiencing systemic side effects following the 2nd vaccination was again significantly associated with reporting an OLP flare (p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, OLP flares were not reported at high rates with COVID-19 vaccination or infection. Within these limitations, the findings of the study suggest that participants who experience systemic side effects following a COVID-19 vaccine may be more susceptible to OLP flares. Experiencing an OLP flare following the 1st COVID-19 vaccination was significantly associated with experiencing a flare again after receiving the 2nd vaccination.

Experiencing an OLP flare following the 1st COVID-19 vaccination was significantly associated with experiencing a flare again after receiving the 2nd vaccination.

title: Severity-dependent and sex-biased dysregulation of A-to-I RNA editing in COVID-19 reveals CTSS as a key regulatory target
abstract: ABSTRACT SARS-CoV-2 infection causes diverse clinical outcomes, with men facing higher risks of severe disease. Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing mediated by ADAR enzymes governs innate antiviral immunity, yet its contribution to COVID-19 severity and sex-biased disease remains unclear. We performed epitranscriptomic profiling on 126 blood samples from non-COVID controls and COVID-19 patients spanning different disease severities. We detected 1,466 differentially RNA-edited sites in 514 genes linked to clinical outcomes. Although ADAR expression increased in COVID-19 patients overall, it was strongly reduced in ICU patients compared with non-ICU patients, and this shift was far more prominent in males. This severity-associated and sex-biased ADAR/ADARB1 downregulation coincided with decreased global RNA editing and perturbed expression of immune-related edited transcripts. Cathepsin S (CTSS) was identified as a central regulatory node: elevated A-to-I editing within its 3’ UTR in ICU patients stabilizes CTSS mRNA. Without stratifying by disease severity, ADAR expression and global editing showed no significant sex differences; the large sex divergence only appeared among ICU patients. This indicates severity-dependent, not infection-innate, disruption of A-to-I editing, disproportionately amplified in critically ill males. CTSS 3’UTR editing may serve as a biomarker for patient stratification, revealing a mechanistic connection between epitranscriptomic changes and male-biased severe COVID-19.

title: Administrative Primacy as an Interpretive Framework for Health System Governance: A Document-Based Analysis of Three Publicly Reported Episodes During the 2021 Fujian COVID-19 Outbreak Response
abstract: Abstract Background Public health emergencies can intensify ethical risks rather than suspend them. When emergency governance is structured primarily around administrative performance metrics, established clinical and occupational protection norms may face displacement pressure. This case study examines three publicly reported episodes from the 2021 Fujian Delta variant COVID-19 outbreak through the interpretive lens of Administrative Primacy, a descriptive framework for analysing governance patterns in which administrative performance objectives may structurally outweigh clinical judgment and ethical reasoning. Administrative Primacy is introduced here as a sensitising concept rather than a formal theory, analogous to interpretive constructs used in governance and organisational ethics research. Methods We conducted a document-based ethical case analysis using exclusively publicly available sources: official government communications, state-approved media reports, and peer-reviewed literature. All cited documentary sources are publicly accessible and independently retrievable. Ethical interpretation was informed, where applicable, by selected principles of the Declaration of Helsinki (2013), supplemented by WHO outbreak-ethics guidance, NHC pediatric imaging standards (WS 521–2017), and UV radiation safety regulations (GB 19258 − 2012). A Poisson incidence density model was applied as an auxiliary sensitivity analysis to examine the plausibility of a reported occupational outcome; full derivation and sensitivity analyses are in Supplementary Methods S1. Evidence is categorised by type throughout: official photographs, official regulatory text, official press conference records, and state-approved media reports are distinguished from interpretive inference. Results Three domains of concern were identified, each supported by publicly accessible documentary sources, including official documents and contemporaneous media reports. First, a state-media-documented pediatric CT episode involved the simultaneous co-occurrence of three concurrent ethical and regulatory concerns: an unaccompanied minor in a radiological environment (contrary to WS 521–2017), an apparently illuminated UV germicidal lamp during the child’s presence (which would be contrary to GB 19258 − 2012 if operating as depicted), and CT application to a cohort characterised by the NHC’s own lead expert as predominantly mild. Second, the overnight mobilisation of 320 pre-licensure medical students for 27 days of high-frequency nasopharyngeal sampling raised occupational safety and consent concerns; auxiliary Poisson analysis suggested the reported zero-infection outcome was lower than would be anticipated under the stated comparator assumptions, raising a question that warrants verification. Third, a ‘Green Channel’ administrative exception at the region’s designated tertiary hospital temporally associated with a sequence of events culminating in ICU closure, creating structural conditions that may have been associated with delayed critical care access; no mortality estimate is made. Conclusions The three episodes are consistent with, and may be interpreted through, the Administrative Primacy framework as illustrations of a governance pattern in which administrative performance metrics may, in some circumstances, come into tension with clinical ethics, occupational protection norms, and institutional transparency. The framework is offered as a replicable analytical tool for evaluating governance-ethics alignment in future emergency responses, and three domains are identified as candidate areas for further health-system governance review, framed as hypotheses generated by this single case rather than as established broader policy gaps.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的2021年福建三角洲变体暴发的治理,研究行政绩效指标如何影响突发公共卫生事件期间的临床判断和道德推理。核心问题是,行政至上是否可以被视为此类危机期间卫生系统治理的一种模式。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查采用基于文档的道德案例分析,使用公开来源:官方政府通讯、国家批准的媒体报道和同行评审的文献。使用泊松 发病率 密度模型作为辅助敏感性分析来评估报告的职业结果的合理性。所有引用的文献来源均可公开访问且可独立检索。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 确定了三个值得关注的领域,每个领域都有文献资料支持,包括官方文件和媒体报道。这些事件与行政首要框架一致,该框架表明,在某些情况下,行政绩效指标可能与临床伦理、职业保护规范和机构透明度相冲突。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 连夜动员 320 名预执照医学生进行高频鼻咽采样,引发了职业安全和同意方面的担忧。报告的零感染结果低于比较假设下的预期,因此需要进行验证。此外,该框架是作为假设而不是既定的政策差距提出的。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该框架作为可复制的分析工具提供,用于评估未来应急响应中的治理与道德一致性。三个领域被确定为进一步卫生系统治理审查的候选领域,并以此单一案例产生的假设为框架。

analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 确定了三个值得关注的领域,每个领域都有文献资料支持,包括官方文件和媒体报道。这些事件与行政首要框架一致,该框架表明,在某些情况下,行政绩效指标可能与临床伦理、职业保护规范和机构透明度相冲突。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 连夜动员 320 名预执照医学生进行高频鼻咽采样,引发了职业安全和同意方面的担忧。报告的零感染结果低于比较假设下的预期,因此需要进行验证。此外,该框架是作为假设而不是既定的政策差距提出的。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该框架作为可复制的分析工具提供,用于评估未来应急响应中的治理与道德一致性。三个领域被确定为进一步卫生系统治理审查的候选领域,并以此单一案例产生的假设为框架。

title: Efficacy and Safety of Live Attenuated COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Based on Omicron-like Temperature-Sensitive Mutant in Preclinical Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model. Methods: SARS-CoV-2 Dubrovka (Wuhan-like), Otradnoe (BA.1.1) and FEB2 (BA.5.2) strains and the ts F-F3 mutant derived from FEB2 were characterized by electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies used Vero CCL-81 cells; in vivo transmissibility and efficacy studies were assessed in female Syrian hamsters. Serum antibody titers were measured by ELISA and neutralization assays. Immunization efficacy was assessed by weight change; viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; and histological examination of the lungs at day 4 post-challenge. Safety criteria included evaluation of pathogenicity and transmissibility in hamsters and ts phenotype stability during prolonged in vitro cultivation. Results: The F-F3 strain displayed a stable ts phenotype in vitro, did not infect hamster lungs or brain, and showed no transmission from immunized to naïve co-housed animals. A single intranasal immunization by F-F3 induced seroconversion, reduced pneumonia severity by 76.2% and 79.5% in two independent experiments (p < 0.01), protected the lungs against productive infection while reducing viral load in the nasal passages, and resulted in no detectable viral transmission after homologous BA.5.2 challenge. Following heterologous Wuhan-like challenge, immunization prevented weight loss and significantly reduced viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; however, protection against pneumonia was only modest (18.6%; p < 0.05). Conclusions: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) candidate based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster model. The F-F3 strain was characterized using electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies were conducted on Vero CCL-81 cells, while in vivo studies assessed transmissibility and efficacy in female hamsters. The vaccine induced seroconversion and significantly reduced pneumonia severity (76.2% and 79.5% in two experiments, p < 0.01) and viral loads in the nasal passages. The study is limited to animal models and lacks human trials, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat.
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model.
elements_zh.methods: 通过电子显微镜、纳米孔测序、细胞病变效应滴定和 RT-PCR 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Dubrovka(武汉样)、Otradnoe(BA.1.1)和 FEB2(BA.5.2)菌株以及源自 FEB2 的 ts F-F3 突变体进行了表征。体外研究使用 Vero CCL-81 细胞;在雌性叙利亚仓鼠中评估了体内传播性和功效研究。通过ELISA和中和测定来测量血清抗体滴度。通过体重变化评估免疫效果;肺部、鼻道和大脑中的病毒载量;攻击后第 4 天进行肺部组织学检查。
elements_zh.main_results: F-F3菌株在体外表现出稳定的ts表型,不感染仓鼠肺或脑,并且未表现出来自免疫至首次共养动物的传播。F-F3 的单次鼻内免疫诱导了血清转化,在两个独立实验中将肺炎严重程度降低了 76.2% 和 79.5% (p < 0.01),保护肺部免受生产性感染,同时减少了鼻道中的病毒载量,并且在同源 BA.5.2 攻击后没有检测到病毒 传播。在经历类似武汉的异源攻击后,免疫接种阻止了体重减轻,并显着减少了肺部、鼻道和大脑中的病毒载量;然而,对肺炎的保护作用不大(18.6%;p < 0.05)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于 F-F3 的 LAV 可能是在新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体背景下进一步开发的有希望的候选者,特别是其安全性和针对同源挑战的功效。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于叙利亚仓鼠模型的临床前评估,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是温和的,因为它是基于体外和体内研究而没有进行人体试验。

title_zh: Efficacy and Safety of Live Attenuated COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Based on Omicron-like Temperature-Sensitive Mutant in Preclinical Study
source_body_en: Background/Objectives: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model. Methods: SARS-CoV-2 Dubrovka (Wuhan-like), Otradnoe (BA.1.1) and FEB2 (BA.5.2) strains and the ts F-F3 mutant derived from FEB2 were characterized by electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies used Vero CCL-81 cells; in vivo transmissibility and efficacy studies were assessed in female Syrian hamsters. Serum antibody titers were measured by ELISA and neutralization assays. Immunization efficacy was assessed by weight change; viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; and histological examination of the lungs at day 4 post-challenge. Safety criteria included evaluation of pathogenicity and transmissibility in hamsters and ts phenotype stability during prolonged in vitro cultivation. Results: The F-F3 strain displayed a stable ts phenotype in vitro, did not infect hamster lungs or brain, and showed no transmission from immunized to naïve co-housed animals. A single intranasal immunization by F-F3 induced seroconversion, reduced pneumonia severity by 76.2% and 79.5% in two independent experiments (p < 0.01), protected the lungs against productive infection while reducing viral load in the nasal passages, and resulted in no detectable viral transmission after homologous BA.5.2 challenge. Following heterologous Wuhan-like challenge, immunization prevented weight loss and significantly reduced viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; however, protection against pneumonia was only modest (18.6%; p < 0.05). Conclusions: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.

analysis_zh.methods: 通过电子显微镜、纳米孔测序、细胞病变效应滴定和 RT-PCR 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Dubrovka(武汉样)、Otradnoe(BA.1.1)和 FEB2(BA.5.2)菌株以及源自 FEB2 的 ts F-F3 突变体进行了表征。体外研究使用 Vero CCL-81 细胞;在雌性叙利亚仓鼠中评估了体内传播性和功效研究。通过ELISA和中和测定来测量血清抗体滴度。通过体重变化评估免疫效果;肺部、鼻道和大脑中的病毒载量;攻击后第 4 天进行肺部组织学检查。
analysis_zh.main_results: F-F3菌株在体外表现出稳定的ts表型,不感染仓鼠肺或脑,并且未表现出来自免疫至首次共养动物的传播。F-F3 的单次鼻内免疫诱导了血清转化,在两个独立实验中将肺炎严重程度降低了 76.2% 和 79.5% (p < 0.01),保护肺部免受生产性感染,同时减少了鼻道中的病毒载量,并且在同源 BA.5.2 攻击后没有检测到病毒 传播。在经历类似武汉的异源攻击后,免疫接种阻止了体重减轻,并显着减少了肺部、鼻道和大脑中的病毒载量;然而,对肺炎的保护作用不大(18.6%;p < 0.05)。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于 F-F3 的 LAV 可能是在新兴 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体背景下进一步开发的有希望的候选者,特别是其安全性和针对同源挑战的功效。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于叙利亚仓鼠模型的临床前评估,该模型可能无法完全代表人类 免疫应答。证据是温和的,因为它是基于体外和体内研究而没有进行人体试验。

title: Association of In-Hospital Antimalarial–Macrolide Therapy With 3–6-Month Cardiac Electrophysiological Outcomes in Survivors of Severe COVID-19: A Matched Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background: During the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, antimalarial agents and macrolide antibiotics were widely used because of their proposed antiviral and immunomodulatory effects. However, their potential to prolong ventricular repolarization and increase the risk of arrhythmias raised concerns about their cardiac electrophysiological effects. Available evidence has predominantly focused on electrophysiological effects during acute treatment, whereas post-recovery outcomes remain less well characterized. Objectives: To evaluate cardiac electrophysiological outcomes 3–6 months after hospitalization for severe COVID-19 pneumonia and compare these outcomes according to in-hospital exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy. Methods: We conducted a retrospective matched cohort study including adults hospitalized for severe COVID-19 pneumonia between March and June 2020. Patients exposed to hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine in combination with azithromycin or clarithromycin were matched 1:1 by sex and age (±3 years) with patients who did not receive either drug class. Cardiovascular assessment 3–6 months after hospitalization included a 12-lead electrocardiogram and 24-hour Holter monitoring. QTc interval, conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, and heart rate variability (HRV) were evaluated. Results: Eighty-six patients were included (43 exposed and 43 unexposed). Follow-up QTc intervals were similar between groups (420.0 vs. 423.1 ms; p =0.762), and QTc prolongation was uncommon. No malignant ventricular arrhythmias or clinically significant conduction abnormalities were identified. Exposed patients had a higher prevalence of sinus bradycardia, a lower resting heart rate on electrocardiography, and higher HRV as assessed by the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN). However, unexposed patients exhibited a greater inflammatory burden during hospitalization, more frequent intensive care unit admissions, and longer hospital stays. Conclusion: In this cohort of survivors of severe COVID-19, short-term in-hospital exposure to combined antimalarial–macrolide therapy was not associated with persistent QTc prolongation or clinically significant electrophysiological abnormalities at 3–6 months. Differences in heart rate and HRV should be interpreted with caution, given potential residual confounding due to acute disease severity.
