Data extraction and analysis will be performed according to the guidelines of the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis Protocols. The entire process will be carried out by two independent reviewers, with any discrepancies resolved by a third reviewer. The eligibility criteria followed the PECO strategy. To be included, articles will have to be: i) original published, ii) studies with educators, and iii) studies that analyzed executive functions. Conversely, exclusion criteria will be: i) duplicates, ii) literature reviews, and iii) studies with retractions. If the search strategy yields a sufficient number of methodologically comparable studies, meta-analytic statistical methods will be applied, including meta-analysis or meta-regression, sensitivity, consistency, precision, and certainty of evidence analyses. CONCLUSION: This systematic review is expected to deepen understanding of COVID-19's impact on educator's health, with a focus on analyzing executive functions.

title: Slow vaccination and immunity profile homogeny as a cause of SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift
abstract: Delays in vaccine production for severe respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), have resulted in countries dependent on foreign biomanufacturing capabilities to underperform in terms of their population immunization rates. The implications of slow vaccination and a comprehensive strategy to combat it have yet to be devised. Of particular concern is the exposure of SARS-CoV-2 to pressures created by vaccinated individuals which could promote antigenic drift negating vaccination efforts. Uncertainty also remains around the usage of the novel mRNA vaccines due to limited characterization of vaccinated host immunity profiles. If unable to induce lymphocytes of high diversity and longevity, mRNA vaccination could further accelerate the development of vaccine escape. This paper outlines the potential consequences of a slow vaccination with mRNA-based vaccines and recommends counteracting measures. It discusses (i) the mutable rate of key SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) protein sites that when altered, could lead to a loss of immunity; (ii) the potential of slow vaccination and mRNA vaccines causing antigenic drift; and (iii) methods of improving immunization rates through production-based means. Comparisons to previous pathogen cases suggest high risk of SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift in response to slow vaccination and novel vaccines. These mutations are predicted to occur at several S protein epitopes. The results call for genomic surveillance initiatives to track development of immune evasion and longitudinal research of vaccinated host immunity profiles to measure durability and diversity of the induced humoral response. Recommendations for improving vaccination rate include the construction of production facilities and improvement of already existing distribution networks, while maintaining communication channels and transparency with the public.

title: Hand–Washing Hygiene Knowledge, Attitude and Practice among University Students in the Post-COVID-19 Era: A Case of KCMC University, Moshi, Tanzania
abstract: BackgroundHand hygiene is a key public health intervention for preventing infectious diseases, including respiratory and gastrointestinal infections. Although the COVID-19 pandemic improved awareness and compliance, sustained adherence remains a challenge, with evidence showing a decline in practice after outbreaks, particularly among young adults in high-contact settings such as universities. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of handwashing hygiene among university students at KCMC University, Moshi, Tanzania, in the post-COVID-19 era. MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 380 students at KCMC University. Data were collected using a pretested structured questionnaire, which captured information on socio-demographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding handwashing hygiene. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Associations between variables were assessed using logistic regression and multivariable analysis, and a p-value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant. ResultsA total of 380 students participated in the study, with a mean age of 23.5 {+/-} 3.5 years. More than half 209 (55.0%) were aged 18-23 years, while 203 (53.4%) were female. Most participants had access to hand hygiene facilities 338 (88.9%). 338 (88.9%) participants had good knowledge of hand hygiene but attitudes were mostly negative 193 (50.8%), and practices were suboptimal, with 201 (52.9%) showing poor hand hygiene practices. Good hand hygiene knowledge was associated with access to hand hygiene facilities (AOR=2.84, 95% CI: 1.25- 6.42, p=0.012) and formal training on hand hygiene (AOR=3.48, 95% CI: 1.24-9.76, p=0.018). Positive attitudes were associated with being in the fourth year or above (AOR=2.12, 95% CI: 1.16-3.89, p=0.015). Good hand hygiene practices were associated with access to hand hygiene facilities (AOR=2.67, 95% CI: 1.18-6.01, p=0.018) and formal training on hand hygiene (AOR=2.98, 95% CI: 1.19-7.48, p=0.020). ConclusionAlthough knowledge and awareness of handwashing hygiene were generally high among university students, inconsistencies between knowledge and actual practices were observed in the post-COVID-19 era. Strengthening health education programs and ensuring continuous access to handwashing facilities may improve adherence to proper hand hygiene practices among university students.

title: The Current State and Future Directions of Therapeutics for SARS-CoV-2 Variants of Concern
abstract: Since March 11th 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic was declared, new SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VoCs) have gained prominent immune evasion and potential for enhanced transmissibility, compromising vaccines as tools for pandemic control. Despite the unprecedented speed for the development and approval of vaccines SARS-CoV-2 after the onset of the pandemic, therapeutic avenues are still limited. Within Canada, there are only two currently approved antiviral treatments for COVID-19 in addition to 5 monoclonal antibodies. As the risk of resistance to these therapeutics continues to rise and infection rates persist, there is an urgent need for effective therapeutics to treat infected individuals. In this article, we explore the effectiveness and accessibility of currently available therapeutics within Canada against new VoCs for SARS-CoV-2. Furthermore, we will look at the use of combination antiviral therapies as a possible strategy for treating SARS-CoV-2 infections. We will also investigate possible therapeutic targets to be used in combination with current antivirals to inhibit pathogenesis and spread. Understanding the limitations of current therapeutics against new VoCs highlights the importance of the implementation of new strategies and targets to treat infections. With additional therapeutic options, we may strive to inhibit the negative impacts of the pandemic on our society as well as increase accessibility to those around the world.

title: Medical and non-medical out-of-pocket cost and time burden of COVID-19 illness in U.S. children and adults: a cross-sectional survey study
abstract: Background: While health system costs of COVID-19 are well documented, evidence on out-of-pocket costs to patients and families, including non-medical and time burden, is limited. This study aimed to estimate out-of-pocket medical, non-medical, and time burden of COVID-19 illness directly from patients and caregivers. Methods: Two cross-sectional surveys were fielded to national nonprobability samples of U.S. adults in Fall 2023: a personal burden survey (adult sample) and a caregiver burden survey (child sample). Surveys collected data on care setting, visit duration including travel and wait time, and medical and non-medical out-of-pocket costs. After applying quality-based exclusion criteria, 409 adult sample and 52 child sample responses were analyzed. Results: Over 87% of respondents were insured. Median out-of-pocket medical costs per visit were low, ranging from $5 (emergency department) to $10 (urgent care) in the adult sample, and from $0 (emergency department) to $75 (hospitalization) in the child sample. Median non-medical costs were $28 or less across care settings. Median time spent receiving care ranged from 90 minutes (primary care, child sample) to 300 minutes (emergency department, adult sample). Despite the relatively low reported out-of-pocket costs, COVID-related financial challenges were reported by 34% of the adult sample and 29% of the child sample, with the most common difficulty being paying non-medical bills (11% and 15%, respectively). Twelve percent in both groups reported problems paying COVID-19-related medical bills. Conclusions: In this post-pandemic non-probability sample, individual out-of-pocket costs for COVID-19 illness were relatively modest. However, time burden was substantial and one-third of respondents reported financial hardship. These estimates, including non-medical and time burden not captured in administrative data, can support more robust economic evaluations of COVID-19 prevention and treatment interventions.

title: Lipid droplets: A hallmark of SARS-CoV-2 infection and a potential target for novel antiviral therapeutics
abstract: Since its emergence, severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has infected over 110.7 million people and killed over 2.4 million people worldwide. Currently, Remdesivir is the only antiviral approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat the disease caused by SARS-CoV-2, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). With millions of new COVID-19 cases reported weekly, efficient, and broad-acting antiviral treatments are urgently needed. Host lipid metabolic reprograming and the formation of lipid droplets (LDs) may play a role in SARS-CoV-2 replication and pathogenesis—opening new perspectives for therapeutic strategies against COVID-19. This paper will review the current knowledge on LDs in the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle and its potential functions in viral replication, assembly, and pro-inflammatory cell moderation. This paper will also highlight key research areas in the field that remain to be understood, including, (i) the possible moonlighting activities of LD-associated viral proteins in the host-cell nucleus of SARS-CoV-2 infected cells, (ii) the potential ability for SARS-CoV-2 to escape or exploit autophagic machinery to enhance viral fitness and survival, and (iii) the impact of diet on one’s susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Overall, a better understanding of the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle and host cell interactions will clarify mechanisms of infection at various levels, inform the design of novel and effective therapeutics and vaccines, and reduce the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on public health.

title: Single-cell-resolved dynamic immune remodeling following Omicron infection and recovery in vaccinated individuals
abstract: Breakthrough SARS-CoV-2 Omicron infections occur despite vaccination, yet post-infection immune recovery remains incompletely understood. Here, we performed longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and targeted proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy individuals and vaccinated patients during infection, early recovery, and 3-month post-recovery. Omicron infection induced coordinated immune remodeling with contraction of T and B cell compartments; expansion of plasma, regulatory T, and dendritic cells; and suppression of inflammatory and metabolic pathways, including TNFα-NF-κB and mTORC1 signaling. Innate populations rebounded rapidly, whereas adaptive compartments recovered slowly with sustained suppression of IL-2 , IL-12 , and IL-15 modules. Chemokine surges ( CXCL1 , CXCL5 , and CXCL8 ) resolved during convalescence, whereas selective cytokines ( CCL5 and CCL8 ) and interleukins ( IL-6 , IL-18 , and IL-24 ) persisted. Trajectory analysis revealed non-uniform remodeling of T cell states with persistent differentiation signatures across naive, effector, and memory compartments. Overall, vaccination tempered early immune collapse and accelerated innate rebound, highlighting interleukin-linked checkpoints and metabolic regulation underlying post-vaccination immune resilience.

title: Host Genetic Determinants of SARS-CoV-2 Susceptibility in Transplant Recipients and Donor Candidates: A Multicohort Analysis of HLA Variation
abstract: Background: Host genetic variation plays a key role in susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) variation influences antiviral immune responses; however, allele-level associations with SARS-CoV-2 infection have varied across populations and clinical groups. This study aimed to evaluate HLA associations with SARS-CoV-2 positivity among transplant recipients and immunocompetent donor candidates representing different clinical and immunological settings. Methods: A retrospective multicohort genetic association study was conducted using data from a single-center tissue typing laboratory during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study included n = 158 pediatric transplant recipients, n = 159 pediatric donor candidates, n = 311 adult transplant recipients, and n = 336 adult donor candidates. SARS-CoV-2 infection was defined by documented positive real-time polymerase chain reaction testing. HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, and HLA-DQB1 loci were analyzed using a predefined carrier threshold (≥5). Associations with SARS-CoV-2 positivity were evaluated using Fisher’s exact test with false discovery rate correction and multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, vaccination status, and antiviral use. Results: HLA-DRB1*11 showed a consistent direction of association with higher odds of SARS-CoV-2 positivity across several cohorts, with the strongest statistical support observed in the pediatric transplant and pediatric donor cohorts. In adult solid organ transplant recipients, the association met only the predefined exploratory threshold (q = 0.12). HLA-B*51 and HLA-A*32 were associated with higher odds of positivity in pediatric and adult transplant recipients, respectively, whereas HLA-DRB1*14 was associated with lower odds of positivity in pediatric donor candidates and adult transplant recipients; both HLA-DRB1*14 findings met the predefined exploratory threshold (q < 0.20). Exploratory subgroup analyses indicated that HLA-B*38 was associated with higher vaccination uptake and lower infection frequency (p = 0.043); however, these observations were based on small carrier numbers and should be interpreted cautiously. No allele reached the predefined exploratory threshold in healthy adult donor candidates. Conclusions: The observed HLA associations differed across the four study cohorts, with several exploratory signals identified among transplant recipients. Because the cohorts also differed in demographic and clinical characteristics, these findings do not establish modification of HLA effects by immune status and require validation in appropriately matched independent populations.

title: Examining the Associations Between Menstrual Disorders and SARS-CoV-2 Exposure in Greek Adolescents: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Background: Exposure to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), whether via infection or vaccination, seems to influence the character of the menstrual cycle by disrupting hormonal and immune function. Methods: The main aim of this cohort study was to explore the association between exposure to SARS-CoV-2—through either vaccination or infection—and menstrual disorders in adolescent females. We also aimed at identifying the most prevalent menstrual disorders observed and assessing potential differences between the exposure groups that may contribute to these conditions. Results: This study included data from adolescent females who visited the Center for Adolescent Medicine and UNESCO Chair in Adolescent Health Care due to various menstrual disorders. Data from 92 adolescents, 77 participants exposed to SARS-CoV-2 and 15 controls, were retrieved. Significant associations were found between exposure to SARS-CoV-2 and abnormally frequent uterine bleeding (p = 0.032) and abnormal uterine bleeding (p = 0.025). Adolescents with a past confirmed case of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) demonstrated significantly lower serum concentrations of fibrinogen (p = 0.023) and iron (p = 0.03), as well as higher γ-GT concentrations (p = 0.028), than those who were non-infected, whereas vaccinated adolescents presented with significantly lower concentrations of coagulation factors VIII (p = 0.002), vWFAg (p = 0.023), and Rcof (p = 0.007) than those of their unvaccinated peers. Overall, adolescents exposed [infection (or/and) vaccination] to SARS-CoV-2 demonstrated increased estradiol (E2) concentrations compared to those of the controls. In conclusion, adolescent exposure to SARS-CoV-2 was strongly linked to abnormal uterine bleeding and polymenorrhea, potentially due to decreased coagulation factors or increased E2 concentrations. Conclusions: Further research involving larger samples and a more sophisticated design is needed to validate these findings.

title: VIT-DRN-OCAFF: An Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion Framework for Multi- Class COVID-19 and Pulmonary Disease Diagnosis Using Thoracic CT Images
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate pulmonary disease diagnosis remains a major challenge due to the rising prevalence of respiratory infections and chronic lung disorders. The COVID-19 pandemic further emphasized the need for intelligent diagnostic frameworks capable of rapidly identifying pulmonary abnormalities from thoracic Computed Tomography (CT) images. This study proposes a novel Vision Transformer–Dilated Residual Network with Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion (ViT-DRN-OCAFF) framework for multi-class pulmonary disease classification. The proposed architecture combines the global contextual learning capability of Vision Transformers with the lesion-sensitive feature extraction of Dilated Residual Networks, while the Optimized Cross-Attention Feature Fusion (OCAFF) mechanism adaptively refines and integrates complementary pulmonary representations. A comprehensive dataset containing 24,860 thoracic CT images collected from public repositories and collaborating clinical centers was utilized, comprising COVID-19, viral pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, and non-viral lung abnormalities. Advanced preprocessing techniques, including lung segmentation, adaptive contrast enhancement, lesion-aware normalization, volumetric augmentation, and image refinement, were employed to improve diagnostic feature quality. The Vision Transformer branch captured long-range contextual pulmonary dependencies, whereas the Dilated Residual Network extracted fine-grained pathological features associated with pulmonary lesions. Subsequently, the OCAFF module dynamically prioritized discriminative pulmonary characteristics and minimized redundant activations for improved classification reliability. Experimental evaluation using a 70:15:15 training-validation-testing protocol demonstrated superior performance with 99.42% accuracy, 99.31% precision, 99.27% sensitivity, 99.48% specificity, and 99.29% F1-score, outperforming existing pulmonary disease classification techniques.

title: Placental Vascular Malperfusion and Perinatal Outcomes During the Vasculotropic Viral Surge of Endemic SARS-CoV-2: A 50-Month Multicenter Longitudinal Study
abstract: The re-emergence of seasonal respiratory pathogens has complicated obstetric care following the transition of coronavirus disease 2019 to an endemic state. The study examined the epidemiological impact and pathogenetic characteristics associated with endemic viruses among pregnant women. A multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted using an epidemiological dataset of 9647 consecutive deliveries from 2022 to 2026. A nested clinical sub-cohort of 140 hospitalized patients was divided into coronavirus disease 2019 (67 cases) and other respiratory infections (73 cases) groups. The study compared epidemiological trends, predictive biomarkers (neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio and C-reactive protein level), and placental histopathology. The analysis showed an asymmetric U-shaped trend in adverse perinatal events over the study period (N = 9647). Following the nadir of eight stillbirths in 2024, a viral resurgence in 2025 resulted in a 2.6-fold increase in stillbirth risk, primarily linked to preeclampsia and placental abruption. Furthermore, within the clinical sub-cohort, the coronavirus disease 2019 group exhibited a significantly elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, which effectively predicted subclinical maternal vascular malperfusion. The increase in stillbirths between 2025 and 2026 may be exacerbated by waning population immunity and the vasculotropic properties of endemic coronavirus disease 2019. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio can serve as a useful biomarker for detecting subclinical thrombotic risk.

title: Longitudinal Trajectories of Inflammatory, Immune, and Coagulation Biomarkers in Critical COVID-19 Under Chronic Etanercept Therapy: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Severe COVID-19 is driven by a complex interplay between systemic hyperinflammation, cellular immune dysregulation, and activation of coagulation cascades. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 52-year-old man with a history of rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis managed with chronic etanercept therapy, who was hospitalized with rapidly progressive COVID-19. Longitudinal monitoring of C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), D-dimer, and fibrinogen demonstrated a transient suppression of select acute-phase reactants followed by profound cellular immune dysregulation and escalating thrombo-inflammatory activity. Despite multimodal management—including remdesivir, convalescent plasma, invasive mechanical ventilation, and veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO)—the patient suffered fatal cardiac arrest. Conclusions: This case highlights the clinical utility of longitudinal, multiparametric biomarker profiling in severe COVID-19 and underscores the critical importance of timely immunomodulatory interventions prior to irreversible immunothrombotic damage.

title: Three-year longitudinal safety surveillance following COVID-19 vaccination in individuals with underlying medical conditions
abstract: Individuals with chronic comorbidities are at increased risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Although post-vaccination adverse events are generally mild and comparable to those in the general population, rare events and limited longitudinal data highlight the need for condition-specific long-term safety surveillance. To address these critical evidence gaps, this study conducted a longitudinal analysis of various COVID-19 vaccine platforms within the Iranian population with comorbidities three years post - vaccination. The research evaluated the safety profiles of different vaccine platforms across these patient cohorts using a researcher-made questionnaire composing of short-term and long-term vaccine adverse events as well as cases’ medical profiles. Furthermore, an exploratory immunogenicity sub-study was performed among participants with HIV to characterize vaccine-induced humoral immune responses. A total of 1115 participants were enrolled; 43.9% had a history of COVID-19 infection, with significantly higher incidence among participants with several comorbidities. Body pain, fever, and weakness were the most frequently reported early adverse events (AEs). During long-term follow-up, 23.8% experienced at least one post-vaccination event, most commonly cardiovascular (5.4%) and neurological (4.8%) conditions. Multiple analysis identified obesity and liver disease as the strongest independent risk factors for a broad range of AEs, while increasing age was associated with higher odds of overall and several organ-specific events. After adjustment for age, sex, previous COVID-19 infection, and number of comorbidities, AstraZeneca recipients had higher rates of early AEs after the first dose and first booster. PastoCovac and Sputnik were associated with lower odds of early AEs after the second dose, whereas Bharat, Barkat, and PastoCovac were associated with higher odds of late AEs. While AEs were frequent in cases with underlying conditions, most of them were mild and transient. However, cardiovascular and neurological symptoms were the most frequently reported long-term events during follow-up. Although some kinds of comorbidities showed a higher prevalence of complains after specific vaccine types, the casual association is not possible yet.

title: Iron Status in Patients with SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: This study evaluated the iron status and diagnostic usefulness of iron-related parameters in patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection upon admission to the hospital and during hospitalization. The study group included 87 patients with COVID-19 and 45 healthy subjects. Serum iron, ferritin, transferrin, transferrin saturation (TSAT), soluble transferrin receptor (sTfR), and hepcidin concentrations were measured using routine laboratory methods. Serum iron, transferrin concentrations, and TSAT were significantly decreased in COVID-19 on hospital admission, before initiation of treatment, whereas ferritin and hepcidin levels were increased in comparison to the control group (p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p = 0.048, p < 0.001, and p < 0.001, respectively). Serum iron and ferritin levels were significantly higher after hospitalization than those on admission (p < 0.05 for all comparisons). Significant differences were observed only in ferritin and transferrin levels between the groups categorized according to disease severity (p = 0.002 and p < 0.001, respectively); levels were significantly higher in patients with critical disease severity compared to those with moderate disease severity (p = 0.005 and p < 0.001, respectively). Transferrin also showed a negative correlation with disease severity (p = 0.040). Serum ferritin and TSAT levels were significantly higher, whereas transferrin concentration was significantly lower in patients with cytokine storm compared to those without it (p < 0.001, p = 0.011, and p < 0.001, respectively). Ferritin and TSAT also showed a positive correlation, while transferrin revealed a negative correlation with the cytokine storm (p < 0.001, p = 0.011, and p < 0.001, respectively). Additionally, serum ferritin concentrations were significantly decreased, while transferrin levels were increased in survivors compared to non-survivors (p = 0.015 and p = 0.001, respectively). Changes in ferritin, transferrin, TSAT, and hepcidin concentrations were significantly associated with inflammatory markers and hematological parameters. The results of our study indicate that iron homeostasis is disrupted in patients with COVID-19. This dysregulation may contribute to impaired hemoglobin synthesis and could play a role in the development of anemia of inflammation. Furthermore, alterations in iron-related biomarkers were associated with disease severity in patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. While these findings suggest a potential role for these indices in disease assessment, additional studies incorporating appropriate predictive analyses are required to establish their diagnostic and prognostic value.

title: Autoimmunity and autoinflammation in COVID-19: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies
abstract: As of May 2021, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has infected over 150 million people worldwide. The mechanisms of immune dysregulation in resulting coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) have not yet been fully elucidated. There is growing evidence to suggest a connection between SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of autoinflammatory and autoimmune responses. This article will investigate how immune dysregulation in COVID-19 contributes to autoinflammation and autoimmune disease, and discuss the therapeutic implications. The viral infection provokes hyperinflammation by shifting innate and adaptive immune responses towards a proinflammatory state, while suppressing immune regulation. Immune dysregulation and molecular mimicry by SARS-CoV-2 have the potential to break down immunological tolerance, stimulate cross-reactive immune responses, and induce lasting autoimmune disease. Promising immunomodulatory therapies include treatment with type I and III interferons, antibodies against the virus or inflammatory immune pathways, corticosteroids, cell therapies, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and superantigen therapy. Contextualized by the current research, this article will also address the emerging cases of vaccine-induced thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT): a life-threatening autoimmune disease elicited by certain SARS-CoV-2 viral vector vaccines. This review exposes the necessity for longitudinal studies investigating the prevalence and persistence of autoinflammatory damage and autoimmune disease following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Syncytia Formation: A trademark of severe SARS-CoV-2 infection and a potential target for novel drug therapies
abstract: Coronavirus disease (COVID-19), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, is characterized by its symptoms and complications primarily affecting the upper respiratory tract. Infected multinucleated syncytial pneumocytes have been observed in severe COVID-19 cases, alongside lung damage and lymphocytopenia. Syncytia formations allow the virus to evade the immune system, disseminate without cell exocytosis and cause cytopathicity and cell death. The mechanism of cell-cell fusion in SARS-CoV-2 infected cells is well documented as it relies on the same machinery as cell entry. The free spike (S) proteins localized at the cell membrane interact with ACE2 receptors and host proteases on neighbouring cells causing the cell membranes to fuse. However, the biological composition of these multinucleated cells is not well characterized. Furthermore, how these multinucleated syncytia are interacting with their surrounding environment to cause the physical manifestations that are observed in COVID-19 patients is not yet fully understood. At present, there are no antivirals drug that have been developed or in use that directly target syncytia formation in SARS-CoV-2 and other syncytia-inducing viruses. This makes syncytia inhibition an overlooked yet promising area for new drug therapy development. Naturally, these shortcomings lead to the following questions that this article will focus upon 1) what the cellular and molecular composition of multinucleated syncytia is and how do they function biologically, and 2) how syncytia can be targeted to produce broad spectrum multidrug antivirals. A better understanding of the cellular composition and biological functions of syncytia can allow for a novel syncytia targeted antiviral that can prevent or reduce severe lung damage and other syncytial manifestations. Cell-cell fusion is not unique to SARS-CoV-2 as many other enveloped viruses such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and Middle East respiratory syndrome related coronavirus (MERS-CoV) are known to induce syncytia in infected cells. Therefore, the impact of this research extends beyond SARS-CoV-2 and can pave the way for broad spectrum antivirals that target syncytia formation in other enveloped viruses. This could potentially reduce the burden that syncytia forming viruses have on public health, including the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Dysregulated complement activation in COVID-19: The Role of Soluble Complement Inhibitors
abstract: In viral infections, complement activation can contribute to viral clearance, but excessive activation, as observed in severe COVID-19, may drive immunopathology. While much is known about complement-activating factors in COVID-19, insight into the role of endogenous complement inhibitors remains limited. We performed a longitudinal analysis within the BEAT-COVID cohort, comprising hospitalized patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) or ward, and age-matched healthy controls. Serum levels of the complement activation marker soluble membrane attack complex (sC5b-9) and soluble inhibitors C1-Inhibitor (C1-INH), C4b-Binding Protein (C4BP), Factor H, and Factor I were measured by ELISA. In vitro endothelial complement sensitivity was assessed by flow cytometry. Soluble inhibitors were also measured in a cohort of patients with long COVID. title: Assembling an understanding: the critical role of SARS-CoV-2 envelope and membrane proteins in virion formation
abstract: In March 2020, the World Health Organization declared coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) a global pandemic. Since then, COVID-19 has claimed the lives of over 2 million people and is continuing to spread at an alarming rate, straining public health systems and crippling economies. The virus responsible for such global devastation is the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), a betacoronavirus (ß-CoV) composed of a positive-sense, single stranded RNA genome surrounded by a viral envelope. The envelope of ß-CoVs consists of four major structural proteins: the envelope (E) protein, membrane (M) protein, spike (S) protein, and nucleocapsid (N) protein, with previous research implicating these proteins in the assembly and budding process of new virion particles. As these structural proteins are relatively conserved, previously acquired knowledge from other ß-CoV strains has helped characterize the structure and function of these viral envelope proteins in the context of SARS-CoV-2. However, our understanding remains incomplete surrounding the SARS-CoV-2 viral assembly and budding process and the host and viral proteins that are involved. This review will summarize the current knowledge on SARS-CoV-2 virion assembly and budding at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-to-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC). Specifically, the structure of the major viral envelope proteins, E and M, and the conservation of their sequences will be discussed in detail, followed by a thorough examination of the functions of the E and M proteins during viral assembly at the ERGIC. Finally, an in-depth explanation of how these viral envelope proteins not only represent new target molecules for the development of novel therapeutics but also their potential as vaccine candidates will be highlighted. With the emergence of new variants exacerbating the state of the pandemic, advancing our understanding of viral and host proteins involved in the critical steps of the SARS-CoV-2 virus lifecycle remains a crucial aspect in continuing the fight against COVID-19. Expanding global knowledge on the molecular mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 will provide further insight into the pathogenesis and epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 infection and create new avenues for vaccine development and therapeutic interventions.

title: Sex-Specific Plasma Proteomic Alterations Underpin Distinct COVID-19 Progression and Post-COVID-19 Condition
abstract: Abstract Sex differences in COVID-19 and its sequelae remain poorly understood, which hinders targeted therapies. We performed plasma proteomic analyses of 69 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 and 30 healthy controls from a prospective Chinese cohort. The UK Biobank and Mount Sinai Biobank were employed for validation and provided insights into the progression mechanisms. Biological and tissue enrichment analyses characterized sex-specific pathways and tissue-enriched proteins. We identified ANXA11, a molecular tether that physically links RNA granules to lysosomal membranes to enable their long-distance transport and local translation, as a protein associated with male-specific susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Decreased ANXA11 protein levels were linked to higher risk of infection in males, replicated in the UK Biobank. Sex-specific proteomic alterations revealed distinct biological responses, including glycosylation-related pathways in females and cell adhesion, platelet-leukocyte interactions, and inflammatory responses in males. Sex-specific protein changes were also associated with distinct post-COVID-19 symptom profiles. ANXA11 was identified as a novel protein associated with the male-specific susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Sex-specific protein changes revealed distinct mechanistic differences between male and female patients in COVID-19 progression and may explain sex differences in post-COVID-19 conditions.

title: Sex steroids differentially modulate SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammatory responses in endothelial and immune cells
abstract: Introduction Sex-related differences in coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity suggest an important role for sex steroids in regulating immune and endothelial responses to severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Methods Receptor expression, inflammatory signaling, and monocyte transendothelial migration were assessed by RT-PCR, immunoblotting, and Boyden chamber assay, respectively. HULEC-5a and primary human immune cells were exposed to in vitro -amplified SARS-CoV-2. Samples were collected between June 2020 and April 2022, with sample sizes based on primary sample availability and independent experiments. Results SARS-CoV-2 differentially regulates estrogen receptor gene expression, decreasing it in endothelial cells (p<0.05) while increasing it in immune cells (p<0.01). SARS-CoV-2 generally activated inflammatory signaling pathways, including NFκB, STAT3, and p38 MAPK, in THP-1 monocytic cells (up to 1.9-fold). The NFκB response was augmented by the androgen receptor agonist dihydrotestosterone (DHT, 44.6%) and attenuated by the androgen receptor antagonist flutamide (44.1%). In endothelial cells, DHT twice reduced SARS-CoV-2 activation of the p38 MAPK signaling pathway. β-estradiol inhibited (2.2-fold), whereas DHT stimulated (4.9-fold) NFκB signaling pathway in neutrophils isolated from patients with COVID-19. SARS-CoV-2 activation of inflammatory signaling pathways deteriorates over time in monocytes from patients with COVID-19 (p<0.05). Furthermore, DHT significantly increased trans-endothelial migration of monocytes (p<0.001) and detachment of SARS-CoV-2 exposed endothelial cells (p<0.01), suggesting a potential role for androgen-responsive pathways in endothelial dysfunction and immune cell trafficking. Discussion These findings elucidate the molecular mechanisms driving male-biased COVID-19 severity and underscore the potential of targeting androgen-responsive pathways as a therapeutic strategy to mitigate severe viral inflammation and endothelial dysfunction.

title: Identity Theft at the Intersection of Citizenship and Ethnicity Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Design-Correct Replication and Extension Using the National Crime Victimization Survey
abstract: Abstract Identity theft cost 23.9 million U.S. victims $16.4 billion in 2021. Analysis of the 2018 NCVS Identity Theft Supplement found lower victimization odds for noncitizens than citizens and for Hispanic than non-Hispanic persons, but elevated risk for Hispanic noncitizens beyond either alone. Whether this held during the pandemic, when benefit programs required institutional engagement many noncitizens had avoided, was unknown. We replicate and extend this analysis with 2018 and 2021 data, adding the weights and design correct standard errors it lacked. The Hispanic protective effect was stable. The noncitizen effect lost significancein 2021, but no cross-wave change was significant. The doubly marginalized interaction replicated only under the original method and was null in 2021. Benefits fraud among victims surged, with implications for emergency-program identity verification.

title: Comparative Optimism for Getting Infected With COVID-19: An Individual Participant Data Meta-Analysis and Critical Reflection on Research Practices
abstract: Comparative optimism (believing one’s own risk is lower than others’) has been widely studied. Nonetheless, important methodological features have largely remained unrecognized. Focusing on a single event (contracting COVID-19), we estimated the average effect, tested moderators with attention to measurement artifacts, and appraised methodological quality. We synthesized 135 effect sizes from 50 studies (38 articles; sample sizes summing to 88,935, not necessarily unique participants) using a multilevel model with random effects for study, article, and nationality. We then examined moderators at both aggregated and individual-participant levels. Although, on average, comparative optimism was observed (d = 0.334, 95% CI [0.225, 0.444]), true effects varied substantially, and the meta-analytic prediction interval ranged from −0.371 to 1.040. Strikingly, this substantial heterogeneity was observed despite our efforts to control for various potential sources of heterogeneity during data collection. Measurement format was the most consistent moderator, with indirect assessments yielding larger adjusted effects than direct assessments, whereas longer response scales were not consistently associated with smaller effects. Effects were larger in samples collected in 2021 than in 2020, but this exploratory finding was sensitive to one article. The association with national collectivism was unclear in the primary model. Individual-participant analyses showed no clear overall associations for age, gender, or education. Response distributions indicated that nearly half of participants reported lower personal risk than others, more than one third reported equal risk, and about one sixth reported higher risk. Small-study and selection-model analyses suggested possible selective reporting. In sum, although we observed an average comparative optimism effect for contracting COVID-19, the generalizability of the effect and its measured correlates is limited by substantial heterogeneity and the influence of measurement choices and study context.

title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. The authors conclude that in taking almost total responsibility for the welfare of pupils and their families during the pandemic, participating schools – whatever their governance – continued to resist neoliberal-driven educational policy that focuses purely on the classroom and excellent teaching. Learning from the pandemic suggests that there is a strong case to re-imagine schools as integral to communities and furthermore, that there is an appetite to achieve this.

title: Assessment of the humoral immune response and post-vaccination events when using various COVID-19 vaccines during the pandemic, taking into account the change of virus strains
abstract: To study the humoral immune response and evaluate the frequency of post-vaccination events when using various COVID-19 vaccines during the pandemic, taking into account the change in virus strains. Materials and Methods. The study of the immunogenicity and frequency of post-vaccination events during COVID-19 immunization using the vaccines Sputnik V, Sinopharm and Soberana Plus approved for use in the Republic of Belarus, as well as the vaccine BelKovidVak, was conducted. According to the results of genotyping of SARS-CoV-2 strains in 2021, the majority of the samples (67.3%) were genovariants of B.1.617.2 (Delta) lines. In 2022 they accounted for 1.3% of samples. In 2022 93.5% of samples belonged to other genetic lines of the SARS-CoV-2 virus not related to B.1.1.529 and B.1.617.2. The highest concentration of IgG to SARS-CoV-2 was observed on the 90th day after administration of the BelKovidVak vaccine. In a study of the frequency of adverse events after primary immunization with Sputnik V (Gam-COVID-Vac) and Sinopharm (BBIBP-CorV) vaccines, 45% of participants had mild or moderate adverse events: soreness (74.1%) and redness (11.1%) at the site of injections, fever (40.7%), weakness (3.7%), headache (3.7%), swelling of the injection site (3.7%). Elevated body temperature was significantly more common (p<0.001) in the group vaccinated with Sputnik V. According to the BelKovidVak vaccine study, most of the adverse events fell into the categories of “Systemic disorders and injection site reactions”, “Nervous system disorders”, “Respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal disorders” and “Laboratory and instrumental data” of mild severity. Adverse events were noted in 37.8% of cases (p=0.02) after administration of the Soberana Plus vaccine (FINLAY-FR-1A). Soreness at the injection site was most often noted (67.3% of cases). COVID-19 vaccines have a beneficial safety profile and develop a humoral immune response that persists for several months.

title: Læmple: a benchmarking framework for virus lineage deconvolution tools for SARS-CoV-2 from wastewater
abstract: 1 Abstract Background Correct and accurate deconvolution of SARS-CoV-2 lineages from wastewater sequencing data is a challenging task, given the intricacy of wastewater amplicon-sequencing data and the ever-growing complexity of the lineage classification. Existing benchmarking studies made use of artificial spike-in compositions, thereby falling short of reflecting the prevailing complexity of wastewater samples. Results We present a modular, expandable, simulation-based benchmarking framework as a reproducible Snakemake workflow, named Læmple, to evaluate the performance of virus lineage deconvolution tools. Using in silico simulated data sets of varying complexity and sequencing quality, we demonstrate its utility by evaluating seven publicly available tools, based on their precision, sensitivity, and reproducibility. Freyja showed robust sensitivity and consistent performance across diverse data set complexities, alongside user-friendly installation and documentation, while VaQuERo demonstrated the highest precision. Conclusions Our results reveal substantial variation in tool performance across conditions, emphasizing the need to benchmark with diverse and complex scenarios. This framework enables informed tool selection for researchers and public health agencies and allows developers to stress-test their tools during development and maintenance, i.e., updating the lineage definition for newly emerging virus lineages. To this end, Læmple was designed in a modular fashion for customization and future expansion to support ongoing software development across all stages of the application life-cycle management.

title: Psychoeducational Challenges of Dyslexic Children During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Dyslexic students faced psychological and educational challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic and online learning, including increased anxiety, low self-esteem, reduced reading interest, limited access to educational technologies, insufficient teacher support, and difficulties with reading fluency and concentration. Examining these challenges is crucial for implementing effective measures and enhancing post-pandemic learning. This study investigates the psycho-educational challenges of dyslexic children during the pandemic, highlighting the need for targeted interventions to support them in current and future contexts. This systematic review identified relevant articles through electronic searches of PubMed, Wiley, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and ScienceDirect, supplemented by the snowballing technique, which involved examining the bibliographies of retrieved references. The study identified two main categories of challenges for dyslexic children: psychological (mental health, emotional well-being, behavioural issues, parental stress) and educational (socioeconomic status, technology access, special educational needs, teacher support, remote learning difficulties) affecting children with learning disabilities. The research results show that dyslexic children faced various psychological and educational difficulties identified in this review during the COVID-19 pandemic. Therefore, targeted, evidence-based strategies-such as teacher training, family-school collaboration, adaptive learning technologies, and psychological support-are needed to mitigate these challenges in the post-pandemic period.

title: Discovery of Epoxysuccinates as Potent Covalent Inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Papain-like Protease
abstract: Abstract The papain-like protease (PLpro) of SARS-CoV-2, essential for viral processing and immune evasion, is a promising therapeutic target for coronavirus infections. Incorporating strategies used to enhance activity of non-covalent inhibitors, notably engagement of the BL2-groove, remote from the active site Cys-111, covalent PLpro inhibitors were designed. Epoxysuccinamide inhibitors demonstrated subnanomolar potency and 107-fold reduction in viral titer in cell cultures. The flexible hydrazide linker required for reaction of Cys-111 with the epoxysuccinamide warhead was susceptible to hepatic carboxylesterase metabolism. Replacement of hydrazide with alternative linkers was unsuccessful. Administered i.v., an epoxysuccinamide was well tolerated in mice. Although metabolically limited for targeting SARS-CoV-2 PLpro, the warhead was validated as a potent tool in the armamentarium of antivirals to confront emerging viruses.

title: Persistent or Exacerbated Lymphopenia Predicts Mortality in Kidney Transplant Recipients Hospitalized with COVID-19

title: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers persistent hepatic immunometabolic remodeling following SARS-CoV-2 infection in obese hosts
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection affects multiple organs, and chronic post-viral tissue injury is often associated with persistent immune dysregulation. Obesity and related metabolic disorders are major risk factors for severe COVID-19 and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), including liver dysfunction. To define hepatic responses during post-acute infection, we studied lean and diet-induced obese mice at 7 and 28 days following infection with mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2. Compared with lean mice, obese mice exhibited persistent lung inflammation and fibrosis, along with liver injury characterized by increased lipid accumulation, cellular apoptosis, and metabolic dysfunction. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed obesity-associated alterations in hepatic immune and metabolic programs during post-acute infection. In particular, hepatic macrophages in obese mice showed sustained inflammatory and metabolic transcriptional alterations, while hepatocytes displayed altered programs associated with gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism. Endothelial cells also exhibited persistent transcriptional changes linked to immune activation and prothrombotic pathways. These alterations remained evident at 28 days post-infection, suggesting incomplete restoration of immune and metabolic homeostasis in obese liver. Collectively, our findings reveal persistent obesity-associated hepatic immunometabolic remodeling following SARS-CoV-2 infection and identify cellular and molecular programs that may contribute to post-acute liver sequelae in metabolically compromised hosts.

title: Leakage-Controlled and Calibrated Deep Ensemble Learning for Reliable COVID-19 Classification from Chest X-Ray and CT Images
abstract: Reliable evaluation of artificial intelligence models for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) imaging remains challenging because patient-level dependencies, source-related biases, and differences between imaging modalities can lead to overly optimistic performance estimates. This study proposes a leakage-controlled, modality-aware deep ensemble framework for COVID-19 classification using chest X-ray (CXR) and computed tomography (CT) images from the COVID-19 Radiography Database and the SARS-CoV-2 CT-Scan Dataset. Separate evaluation protocols were established for CXR and CT, with duplicate control and available source information incorporated for CXR and patient-level partitioning applied to CT before data augmentation. Four ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural networks (CNNs)—VGG16, ResNet50, DenseNet169, and InceptionV3—were evaluated, followed by temperature scaling for probability calibration and validation-optimized weighted soft voting for ensemble fusion. The original CT architectural comparison was conducted at the slice level, whereas the final CT evaluation was performed at the patient level. In the final modality-specific held-out evaluation, DenseNet169 achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.985, an accuracy of 97.32%, and an F1-score of 98.1% on the 2870-image CXR test set. The calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.990, an accuracy of 98.43%, and an F1-score of 97.9%, with a Brier score of 0.030 and an expected calibration error (ECE) of 0.023. For CT, DenseNet169 achieved an AUROC of 0.941 and correctly classified 16 of 18 patients (88.89%), whereas the calibrated weighted ensemble achieved an AUROC of 0.969 and correctly classified 17 of 18 patients (94.44%), with a Brier score of 0.070 and an ECE of 0.053. An uncertainty-aware selective-prediction analysis identified 316 of 2870 CXR test images (11.01%) and 2 of 18 CT test patients (11.11%) as low-confidence cases for specialist review. Among the remaining CT cases, 15 of 16 patients were correctly classified (93.75%). Because the CT test cohort contained only 18 patients, the patient-level CT performance and selective-prediction results should be interpreted cautiously as descriptive estimates from this limited cohort. The original pooled evaluation, in which DenseNet169 achieved 98.51% accuracy, is retained only as an exploratory architectural comparison and should not be interpreted as directly comparable with the final modality-specific evaluation. The findings demonstrate that evaluation design, statistical unit, probability calibration, and ensemble fusion materially influence the interpretation of COVID-19 imaging-classification performance. The proposed framework provides leakage-aware and calibrated performance estimates under the evaluated datasets; however, independent multicenter external validation is required before broader claims of clinical generalizability or deployment readiness can be made.

title: Intranasal immunization expressing S1 antigen can confer functionally sterile protection against an intranasal SARS-CoV-2 challenge in mice
abstract: Currently approved COVID-19 vaccines have shown significant protective efficacy against disease onset and progression after SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, systemic immune responses induced by intramuscular vaccination have limited impact on protection of viral transmission. Intranasal vaccination is an important strategy for induction of mucosal immune responses for protection of viral transmission. Here, we investigated the potential of intranasal immunization expressing a SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) antigen to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection in a mice model. Intranasal immunization with a Sendai virus vector expressing SARS-CoV-2 S1 domain fused with the trimerization domain of T4 fibritin induced neutralizing antibodies detected not only in plasma but also in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) in BALB/c mice. After an intranasal challenge with a mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 strain QHmusX, all the unimmunized mice (n = 9) showed significant body weight loss and high viral load in BALF. In contrast, the intranasally-immunized mice (n = 8) had no detectable viral sgRNA nor infectious viruses in BALF except for one mouse with marginal level of sgRNA, showing no body weight loss. This study indicates that intranasal immunization expressing S1 antigen can confer functionally sterile protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Vaccine uptake patterns for COVID-19 and cholera among healthcare workers: a cross-sectional study in Yaoundé-Cameroon
abstract: Healthcare workers (HCWs) are at increased risk of COVID-19 infection and play a critical role in influencing public vaccine acceptance. This study aimed to assess vaccination coverage and identify the determinants of vaccine uptake among healthcare workers in Cameroon, in order to inform targeted strategies to strengthen immunization programs and improve epidemic preparedness. Among 406 participants (75.6% female, 65.5% aged 30–44 years, 61.3% nurses), 42.4% were fully vaccinated against COVID-19, while only 4.7% had completed the cholera vaccine series. Coverage varied across districts, with Biyem-Assi (53.0%) and Odza (46.0%) recording the highest COVID-19 uptake, and Nkolndongo (11.5%) leading for cholera vaccination. Independent predictors of COVID-19 uptake included being a nurse (aOR = 3.20; 95% CI: 1.75–5.96; p ˂ 0.001) and laboratory technician professions (aOR = 3.67; 95% CI: 1.69–8.19; p = 0.001). For cholera vaccination, age group was associated with uptake although this was statistically not significant ( p = 0.106 and 0.807). Nearly two-thirds of HCWs (62.8%) perceived their work environment as high-risk, knowledge of recommended vaccines was limited, with only 18.7% aware of cholera vaccination recommendations. Strengthening vaccine education and improving accessibility could enhance vaccine acceptance among HCWs. These findings provide important insights for designing targeted immunization strategies in Cameroon and similar contexts.

title: From Sewer to Sentinel: Characterizing the safety, signal reliability, and early detection capabilities of Wastewater-Based Epidemiology for surveillance of SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Infectious disease surveillance has always been limited by what can be detected. Clinical case reporting relies on infected individuals developing symptoms, seeking care, being tested and reported, while making it blind to asymptomatic individuals and fundamentally reactive by nature. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed these limitations of the existing system and led to the fast development of wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) programs that track viruses like SARS-CoV-2 as they are shed into the municipal sewage, regardless symptoms, creating a population-level surveillance system. With the increased adoption of WBE there are three important questions to be answered: (i) does it maintain operational safety, (ii) does it give early warning, and (iii) is its signal reliable? This thesis provides answers to all three questions based on tracing of WBE signal path from viral shedding through sewer transport to epidemiological analysis. First, the safety of the approach is demonstrated through experiments that assess the decay of infectious SARS-CoV-2 in wastewater and its inactivation through UV-C disinfection procedures, while posing a non-negligible but low occupational risk. Then, signal reliability is tested with the use of Sewer Physical Twin and the routine dosing with ferrous iron in sewer networks was found to increase SARS-CoV-2 detectability in wastewater and rescue near–limit of detection enteric targets through the solids-partitioning mechanism irrespective of infection level. Finally, early detection of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VOCs) is investigated with the use of NGS approaches in five London, Ontario treatment facilities with respect to seven VOCs. The wastewater signal is shown to precede the genomic clinical detection of SARS-CoV-2 by several months. Similar results were obtained in Kampala (Uganda) with less sewerage coverage, suggesting the circulation of emerging variants in places that are under-monitored before the global acknowledgment of the threat. These results show the complex arc of biological, environmental, and genomic factors influencing the process of WBE. This work demonstrates that in addition to the beneficial outcome of SARS-CoV-2 monitoring during the pandemic the long-term benefit of WBE lies in the future with the potential for proactive monitoring for new pathogens before the next threat arises.

title: Assessing the capacity of CRISPR systems as anti-viral therapies against SARS-CoV-2 variants of concerns
abstract: Throughout the pandemic, COVID-19 has evolved into a disease of multiplicity; the rapid emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concerns (VOCs) have revealed the necessity of broad-ranged, anti-viral treatments as a potential pandemic countermeasure. CRISPR systems are being explored as a promising venture to solve this issue. Current research on CRISPR anti-viral research has utilized the suitability of the CRISPR effector Cas13 due to the large amounts of potential Cas13 target sites on the SARS-CoV-2 genome as well as its ability to specifically cleave RNAs. Using bioinformatics pipelines, a wide variety of crRNAs can be generated and pooled to easily target a wide range of viral RNA sequences. Moreover, proof-of-concepts such as Cas13-assisted restriction of viral expression and readout (CARVER), and Prophylactic Antiviral CRISPR in huMAN cells (PAC-MAN) promote the feasibility and practicality of this idea. Despite this, the development of CRISPR systems as an anti-viral is still in its infancy, and many limitations must be first overcome before they can reach the clinical stage. This article will strive to objectively assess 1) the mechanisms of the antiviral CRISPR platforms and their potential as a pandemic countermeasure and 2) current limitations plaguing CRISPR Cas13 anti-viral development and a few possible solutions. It is important to understand the potential of CRISPR and how it could benefit Sars-CoV-2 research in ways that are lacking in available/traditional antiviral therapies. Moreover, employing these CRISPR systems would require the creation of novel solutions for overcoming the current obstacles against clinical testing. By further understanding the modularity of CRISPR systems, additional forays into countermeasures can be explored against not only the rapidly evolving strains of Sars-CoV-2, but any RNA virus.

title: Self-reported long COVID associated with sleep problems and poor sleep quality among adults in Germany: results of the German Health Update 2023 (GEDA 2023)
abstract: Long COVID refers to various long-term health impairments following a SARS-CoV-2 infection, including physical, cognitive, and psychological symptoms. Sleep problems are among the most prevalent neuropsychiatric symptoms of long COVID and can negatively affect daily functioning and quality of life. This study aims to investigate sleep onset problems, problems maintaining sleep and poor sleep quality in associations with long COVID among adults in Germany. Analyses are based on data from the cross-sectional nationwide telephone interview survey “German Health Update” (GEDA 2023). Between March 2023 and February 2024, 9,310 adults (50.8% female, median age = 60.8 years) answered questions on any prior SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID status, as well as on sleep onset problems, problems maintaining sleep and poor sleep quality over the past 4 weeks. Weighted prevalence estimates for each sleep variable were calculated by self-reported SARS-CoV-2 infection and long COVID status. Multivariable logistic regressions were conducted, adjusted for age, sex, level of education, chronic conditions, depressive symptoms, COVID-19 vaccination status, and multiple SARS-CoV-2 infections. Participants with self-reported current long COVID reported higher proportions of sleep onset problems (32.6%), problems maintaining sleep (47.8%) and poor sleep quality (44.8%) compared to participants without a SARS-CoV-2 infection (20.0%, 30.8 and 24.1%, respectively) or prior infected participants without long COVID (13.8%, 23.8 and 20.0%, respectively). In multivariable logistic regression analyses, participants with self-reported current long COVID had an increased likelihood of experiencing problems maintaining sleep (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.73; 95% CI = 1.23–2.44) and a higher likelihood of poor sleep quality (aOR = 1.81; 95% CI = 1.29–2.55) compared to non-infected individuals; however, sleep onset problems were not associated with long COVID. Our findings from general population data suggest that adults with current long COVID have 1.7- to 1.8-fold higher odds of problems maintaining sleep and poor sleep quality than non-infected individuals. Given the potential impact on quality of life and physical and psychological functioning, sleep-related symptoms may represent an important target for clinical assessment and management in individuals with long COVID.

title: Revisiting What HIV in the Brain Can Teach Us About SARS-CoV-2 Neurological Complications
abstract: In 2021, a Perspective article suggested that principles of HIV neuropathogenesis could provide a conceptual framework for understanding the neurological complications of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection when mechanistic evidence was limited. Five years later, extensive clinical, neuropathological, and experimental studies allow reassessment of that framework. Current evidence has shifted emphasis away from direct viral infection of the central nervous system toward host-mediated mechanisms involving persistent immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, glial activation, thromboinflammation, and disruption of the neuroimmune axis. At the same time, persistent viral antigens and adaptive immune responses, including autoantibodies in subsets of patients, have expanded our understanding of the biological heterogeneity underlying post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection with neurological manifestations. This Perspective revisits the original framework in light of these advances and examines how concepts derived from HIV neuropathogenesis continue to inform our understanding of persistent neurological dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Characterizing perceived dysexecutive behavioral changes following SARS-CoV-2 infection in individuals with different clinical trajectories
abstract: Neuropsychological alterations, particularly executive dysfunction, are frequently reported after SARS-CoV-2 infection. While cognitive aspects have been widely studied, a multidimensional assessment integrating a behavioral perspective is crucial for a comprehensive understanding of diverse post-SARS-CoV-2 infection trajectories. This study examined perceived dysexecutive behavioral changes after SARS-CoV-2 infection, comparing different post-infection trajectories. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 69 participants: 45 with a history of acute COVID-19 (AC) and 24 with post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS). The Frontal Systems Behavior Scale (FrSBe) was used to assess perceived dysexecutive behavioral changes. The mean z -scores for the FrSBe behavioral dimensions (apathy, executive dysfunction, and disinhibition) increased in both groups in the post-infection period. The PCS group showed significant increases in all dysexecutive symptoms, with clinical difficulties in apathy and disinhibition dimensions. The AC group exhibited slight perceived behavioral changes in executive dysfunction, and more marked changes in disinhibition. SARS-CoV-2 infection may be associated with perceived changes in dysexecutive behavior, with distinct patterns of self-reported alterations across individuals with different post-infection trajectories. The FrSBe may be a useful tool for identifying behavioral alterations in the different clinical spectrum of the disease. These exploratory findings should be interpreted with caution and justify further research using a more robust methodological approach.

title: Prevalence of 406 rare diseases by ethnicity and recorded COVID-19 infection rates among 62.5 million people in England
abstract: Abstract Rare diseases (RD) are individually uncommon but collectively affect millions of people. Yet national estimates of their prevalence, especially across ethnic groups, are limited, and how the COVID-19 pandemic affected people with RD across ethnic groups is unknown. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of 406 RD by ethnicity, and to describe recorded COVID-19 infection across these RD and ethnic groups, in England. We conducted a cross-sectional study within the National Health Service (NHS) England Secure Data Environment, accessed via the British Heart Foundation (BHF) Data Science Centre’s CVD-COVID-UK/COVID-IMPACT Consortium, linking primary care, hospital, and mortality records for individuals alive on 31 July 2023. We calculated age- and sex-standardised prevalence for 406 RD, and recorded COVID-19 infection rates for the overall group, for each RD, and across the six-group Office for National Statistics (ONS) and 19-group NHS ethnicity classifications. Of 62.5 million people, 1.05 million (1.7%) had at least one of the 406 RD. Recorded COVID-19 infection was higher in the RD group than in the non-RD population (32.8% vs. Within the RD group, infection rates varied by ethnicity (e.g. 27.7% in the Pakistani and 23.8% in the Black African groups, versus 33.7% in the White British group) and by specific RD (24.6–41.2% among the 25 most common). Age- and sex-standardised prevalence also varied widely across ethnic groups, with substantial heterogeneity emerging only when broad categories were disaggregated into the more granular NHS classifications (for example, markedly elevated discoid lupus erythematosus prevalence in Black Caribbean but not Black African individuals, obscured within the aggregate “Black” category). This national, ethnicity-resolved map shows that rare-disease prevalence varies substantially across ethnic groups, with differences largely hidden within broad categories, and that recorded COVID-19 infection among people with RD varied across ethnic groups, with the highest rates observed in the ONS White and NHS White British groups. These findings provide a baseline to support earlier, fairer diagnosis and more targeted care.

title: hnRNPA1 Remodels SARS-CoV-2 Genomic G-Quadruplexes through Its UP1 Domain
abstract: The single-stranded RNA genome of SARS-CoV-2 contains several predicted G-quadruplex (G4) forming sequences. Pharmacological stabilisation of these structures has been shown to suppress viral replication, suggesting that their resolution may be required for efficient viral replication. However, the roles of host proteins in stabilization or destabilization of G4 structures have remained largely unexplored. Human hnRNPA1, one of the most abundant RNA-binding proteins in eukaryotic cells, is a G-quadruplex unfolding protein and has independently been identified as a SARS-CoV-2 genome-binding protein. However, whether it acts on the G-quadruplexes within the SARS-CoV-2 genome has not been examined. Here, we screened eight putative G-quadruplex forming sequences conserved across SARS-related coronaviruses and identified two sequences that fold into G4 structures, confirmed by circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy and thioflavin T (ThT) fluorescence-based experiments. Furthermore, we showed that the UP1 and UP1+RGG domains of hnRNPA1 specifically bind and unfold these two viral RNA G-quadruplexes. Both UP1 and UP1+RGG unfold viral RNA G-quadruplexes to similar extent, indicating that recognition and unfolding of these viral G-quadruplexes are mediated mainly by the UP1 domain of hnRNPA1. Together, these findings identify hnRNPA1 as a host factor capable of binding and remodelling SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA G-quadruplexes and suggest a mechanism by which the virus may exploit an abundant host protein to resolve G4 structures within its genome.

title: The impact of COVID-19 on all-cause mortality and life expectancy: findings from a population-based cohort in uMkhanyakude district, northern KwaZulu-natal
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the comprehensive death reporting system in South Africa, significant gaps persist in our understanding of the pandemic's impact in rural areas. METHODS: We computed monthly death counts stratified by demographic factors from a population-based demographic surveillance cohort in rural KwaZulu-Natal. We fit seasonally adjusted negative binomial regression models to estimate excess mortality during the COVID-19 pandemic period (5 March 2020 to 31 December 2021) compared to the pre-pandemic period (1 January 2015 to 4 March 2020). We then assessed the relative risk of death by health and sociodemographic factors and considering apotential interaction with the COVID-19 pandemic. title: Evaluation of Two Combined Analytical Approaches to Assess the Impact of Rare Variants on Severe COVID-19
abstract: Severe COVID-19 displays substantial inter-individual variability that cannot be fully explained by common genetic variants, suggesting a contribution of rare functional variation. We performed whole-genome sequencing in 191 Italian patients (96 moderate, 95 severe) to investigate rare coding variants (minor allele frequency <1% and <5%) via complementary network-based and machine learning approaches. Classical single-variant and burden tests did not identify significant associations after multiple testing correction. However, Network-based Heterogeneity Clustering (NHC) revealed that multiple gene clusters were enriched in severe cases, particularly those involving RNA polymerase II–mediated transcription, RNA metabolism, and vesicle-mediated transport pathways. Gene-level rare variant analysis via the variable threshold method identified five genes significantly associated with severe disease (FDR < 0.05), namely, EIF4G3, GTF2F2, LY96, COX6A1, and STK11, which are involved in transcriptional and translational regulation, innate immune signaling, and mitochondrial function. Unsupervised biclustering significantly stratified patients by severity, and a decision tree model highlighted the burden of DOCK10 variants as a key discriminator between phenotypes. Convergence between the network-based and machine learning results further supported the robustness of the identified signals. Overall, our integrative framework underscores the contribution of rare variants to COVID-19 severity and highlights the coordinated perturbation of interconnected molecular pathways as a determinant of clinical outcome.

title: COVID-19 among people with intellectual disability in comparison to the general population: diagnoses, hospitalizations, deaths, and vaccinations (IDcare)
abstract: BACKGROUND: People with intellectual disabilities (ID) were identified as one of the vulnerable groups during the COVID-19 pandemic. However, few studies have investigated a comprehensive set of COVID-19-related outcomes. The aim of this study is therefore to describe COVID-19-related diagnoses, hospitalizations, deaths, and vaccinations among people with ID compared to the general population. METHODS: This register-based cohort study included all people living in Skåne, Sweden, on January 1st, 2014. People with ID and still alive January 1st, 2020, constituted the ID cohort (n = 14 046). Those remaining after excluding people in the same family/household comprised the general population cohort (gPop, n = 1 157 138). Data regarding outcomes were collected from Swedish national and regional registers for 2020 and 2021. RESULTS: People in the ID cohort had higher risk of being diagnosed with COVID-19 but were less likely than those in the gPop cohort to have the diagnosis confirmed by laboratory test. Adults and older people in the ID cohort had higher COVID-19 related healthcare utilization in terms of physical primary care visits in 2020 and hospitalizations in both 2020 and 2021, with some sex and age differences within the ID cohort. Among those with at least one physical primary care contact, adults and older women in the ID cohort had fewer contacts in 2020 compared to their peers in the gPop cohort. Where the number of observations allowed for analyses, people in the ID cohort had higher risk of death from COVID-19 than those in the gPop cohort. CONCLUSIONS: People with ID had similar healthcare utilization as the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the same or higher levels of COVID-related healthcare, and similar vaccination rates. However, people with ID with healthcare contacts had fewer contacts and bed days and higher mortality. Overall, the Swedish COVID-19 strategy regarding vaccination and healthcare prioritization for people with ID seems to have worked as intended.

title: Strategi Kampanye Komunikasi Publik Satgas Covid-19 Nasional dalam Penanganan Covid-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia generated significant impacts on public health and the national economy, reflected in rising confirmed cases, economic contraction, and increasing unemployment resulting from physical distancing policies. These conditions required society to adapt to new behavioral norms through structured and effective public communication. This study aims to analyze the public communication campaign strategy implemented by the National COVID-19 Task Force in managing the pandemic and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors influencing its implementation. The research employed a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public communication division and community members and were analyzed interpretatively. The findings indicate that the campaign strategy was systematically designed with informative and persuasive objectives to enhance public awareness and encourage behavioral change. Messages were science-based and delivered by credible communicators with authentic voices. Furthermore, stakeholder mapping was conducted to strengthen collaborative support, contributing to the development of active and sustainable public participation in pandemic management.
