title: Newly diagnosed leukemias during SARS-CoV-2 infection in Abidjan, Côte d′Ivoire: A case series of four patients
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, various comorbidities associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection have been reported, but few cases of malignant hematological diseases diagnosed during the infection have been described. We present four cases of hematological malignancies revealed during SARS-CoV-2 infection. In all the patients, medical history did not suggest any hematological diseases prior to the COVID-19 episode. All patients presented with cough, fever, and dyspnea and were admitted for severe acute respiratory illness. During the hospitalization, blood cell counts in all patients showed hyperleukocytosis above 50,000 cells/μL, which raised suspicion of leukemia. Blood smear, bone marrow biopsy, and immunophenotyping confirmed four different hematological malignancies: acute lymphoblastic leukemia (n=1), acute myeloid leukemia (n=1), chronic lymphocytic leukemia (n=1), and adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (n=1). All patients received COVID-19 treatment according to national guidelines. Definitive chemotherapy was administered for CLL; for AML, chemotherapy could not be initiated because of the patient's clinical instability, and only cytoreductive therapy with hydroxycarbamide was given. Two patients died (patients 1 and 4), and two survived and were discharged after 37 days and 20 days. The comorbidity of COVID-19 and newly diagnosed leukemias presents the extraordinary challenge of treating two potentially fatal diseases simultaneously. These cases suggest that an underlying hematological malignancy should be investigated in patients with persistent or unexplained hematological abnormalities during COVID-19.

title: The two pronged approach: The direct and indirect mechanisms mediating SARS-CoV-2 effects on the central nervous system
abstract: Neurological symptoms of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection have been reported in addition to primarily respiratory symptoms. These symptoms range from mild chronic effects including headaches and fatigue to acute consequences including stroke and encephalitis. Although a crucial field of research, mechanisms as to how SARS-CoV-2 exerts these effects remains unclear. However there is growing evidence to suggest underlying mechanisms are likely multifactorial. Thus examining the impact of SARS-CoV-2 on the central nervous system (CNS) is key because of its wide array of noted neurological effects, vexing underlying mechanisms and its potential relationship with long-COVID. Assessing leading hypotheses for proposed mechanisms by which SARS-COV-2 mediates neurological symptoms is an emerging field. This article will examine the effects and support for potential mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 direct neuroinvasion of the CNS. We will also explore the effects and support for means by which SARS-CoV-2 can indirectly contribute to neurological symptoms without the virus entering the CNS, through the host response. Examining this field provides context in understanding neurological effects alongside their contributing viral and host mechanisms to assess neurological impact and develop potential remedies for both acute and chronic symptoms. This article found direct mechanisms of neuroinvasion of SARS-CoV-2 include transversal of the blood brain barrier (BBB) by means of endothelial cells and astrocytes as well as passage through the olfactory pathway. Indirect effects on the CNS mediated by the host’s response consist of excessive neuroinflammation and hypoxic damage to brain tissue. The impact of this work in characterizing CNS effects and underlying mechanisms strengthens the foundation and provides new avenues for which areas, cells, and processes could be used to develop novel diagnostics and therapeutics. The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern (VoC) also pose a concern for neurological impacts, emphasizing our need to advance this field.

title: Does country of origin matter in COVID-19 vaccine preferences? The role of vaccine transparency and regime type
abstract: Abstract A significant obstacle to public health during the COVID-19 pandemic has been the hesitancy of different groups to get vaccinated. This paper discusses whether the country of origin is an important reason for refusing vaccination. To do so, we provide evidence from Turkey, where COVID-19 vaccines from countries such as China, Germany, and the USA are available. We present evidence from a survey experiment that experimentally evaluated information about regime-type qualities of the country where the vaccine is produced and the production processes of the vaccine itself. Our findings show that regime qualities in the country of origin and information available about the vaccine production process determine vaccine preferences. Vaccines produced transparently and in democratic countries are evaluated more positively and are more readily accepted than vaccines produced through opaque processes or in autocratic countries, and production transparency matters more than regime type. We also show that the experimental effect of regime type depends on individual democratic attitudes.

title: Higher risk of Long COVID among patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases and immunomodulatory therapy: a retrospective cohort analysis of national US data.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Little is known about the prevalence of and factors associated with Long COVID in patients with autoimmune rheumatic diseases (AIRDs). METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C). We included adults with a first documented SARS-CoV-2 infection between September 2021 and December 2023, with follow-up through December 2024. Long COVID was defined as ICD-10-CM code U09.9 or a Long COVID clinic visit occurring 28 to 365 days after first infection. We compared patients with AIRD with matched non-AIRD controls using 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching on age with exact matching on sex, race/ethnicity, SARS-CoV-2 variant-dominant period, and data-contributing organization. We estimated hazard ratios using multivariable Cox regression models. Among people with AIRD, we assessed risk by AIRD type and medication exposure before acute COVID-19. RESULTS: In the matched cohort of 187,106 patients, Long COVID occurred in 2.8% of AIRD patients and 1.5% among non-AIRD patients. In multivariable analyses, AIRD was associated with an increased risk of Long COVID compared with non-AIRD patients (aHR 1.56, 95% CI 1.45-1.67). Among patients with AIRD, higher acute COVID-19 severity, pulmonary disease, obesity, and exposure to rituximab or glucocorticoids were associated with an increased risk of Long COVID. Sjögren's syndrome was associated with a higher risk of Long COVID. CONCLUSION: The higher risk of developing Long COVID among AIRD patients compared with those without AIRD underscores the need to identify potential risk factors for Long COVID in this population to minimize its long-term effects.

title: The role of children and adolescents in SARS-CoV-2 transmission and susceptibility to infection warrants further investigation
abstract: Early investigations of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection revealed relatively low rates of infection and mild clinical outcomes among children and adolescents. The burden of disease on the pediatric population was thus determined to be relatively low, and their role in viral transmission likely insubstantial. However, our current understanding may be limited by the emphasis on identifying symptomatic cases and lack of widespread diagnostic testing. As such, children and adolescents, who are reportedly less likely to be symptomatic during infection may be under-represented. This paper aims to provide an updated summary of the manifestation of SARS-CoV-2 infection in children and adolescents, and their role in viral transmission as documented by previous studies. A comprehensive review of the existing literature will provide insight on the current status of our understanding of SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-infection outcomes within this subpopulation, identify limitations of early reports, and highlight the necessity for either further investigation or re-assessment of initial conclusions. Ultimately, recognizing and addressing the current gaps in our knowledge will better inform the development of public health policies to mitigate the spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection, assist clinical management of disease, and reduce the burden on our healthcare systems.

This paper aims to provide an updated summary of the manifestation of SARS-CoV-2 infection in children and adolescents, and their role in viral transmission as documented by previous studies. A comprehensive review of the existing literature will provide insight on the current status of our understanding of SARS-CoV-2 infection and post-infection outcomes within this subpopulation, identify limitations of early reports, and highlight the necessity for either further investigation or re-assessment of initial conclusions. Ultimately, recognizing and addressing the current gaps in our knowledge will better inform the development of public health policies to mitigate the spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection, assist clinical management of disease, and reduce the burden on our healthcare systems.

title: Target trial emulation of effectiveness of COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy in four European countries
abstract: Evidence on real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy remains limited. Using health data from the UK, Sweden, Spain, and Norway, we emulated two target trials to estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines administered during pregnancy against COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation, and admission to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The first trial compares initiation of a primary (two-dose) vaccination with unvaccinated, and the second compares the receipt of a first booster (third dose) with unboosted after primary vaccination. Pregnant women receiving a first or booster vaccination were matched weekly to comparable unexposed pregnant women. A total of 62,061 and 41,096 pregnant women were included in the first and second trial, respectively. Meta-analysis across the four databases showed a VE for primary vaccination of 26·2% (95% CI 16·2–35·1) against infection and 55·6% (95% CI 44·1–64·8) against hospitalisation. For boosters, the VE was 33.6% (95% CI 1·6–56·6) against infection and 34·1% (95% CI 0·6–56·4) against hospitalisation. ICU admission outcomes were too rare to analyse. In this work, we show that primary and first-booster mRNA vaccination during pregnancy is associated to a lower risk of COVID-19-related hospitalisation, while protection against infection is more modest and heterogeneous across databases. This study of over 100,000 pregnancies in four European countries found that both initial and booster COVID-19 mRNA vaccination during pregnancy were linked to lower risks of infection and related hospital admission.

title: Genetic Variability of IFNAR2 Gene and Risk of COVID-19 Critical Illness Among the Tunisian Population
abstract: The IFNAR2 gene encodes an essential component of the type I interferon receptor, which is essential for antiviral defense. It has been proven that the severity of COVID-19 may be influenced by the genetic variants in IFNAR2; however, the results are inconclusive in the African cohorts. Thus, in this study, we investigate the association between three IFNAR2 SNPs and the critical form of COVID-19 in the Tunisian population. A total of 413 COVID-19 patients classified as hospitalized with critical illness (ICU) (n = 46) and non-hospitalized (n = 367) are included. Genotyping of three IFNAR2 polymorphisms (rs1051393, rs2236757, rs9984273) was performed using Taq Man RT-PCR assays. rs2236757 (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.16–0.60), p = 4 × 10−4) and rs9984273 (OR = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.22–0.76, p = 0.0055) were associated with COVID-19 severity with a potential protective effect. However, rs1051393 did not show a significant association with disease severity. Additionally, exploratory haplotype analysis suggested a possible protective association for the TAC haplotype (OR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.02–0.86, p = 0.036), based on a very small number of carriers and not significant after correction for multiple testing. The GAC haplotype, absent from ICU patients, yielded a continuity-corrected OR of 0.03 (95% CI [0.002–0.53]); this estimate rests on a zero cell and is hypothesis-generating only. These preliminary findings, obtained from a single-center cohort with a limited number of critically ill patients, warrant replication in larger, independent, and multicentric populations.

title: Post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) are associated with distinct clinical phenotypes two years after SARS-CoV-2 infection: A data-driven approach
abstract: It is important to determine whether the persistent cognitive and fatigue complaints, as part of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), are associated with underlying patterns and specific symptoms clusters. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate symptom clusters and clinical phenotypes in PASC. We included n = 153 individuals (53 years old, 66% female, 2 years post SARS-CoV-2 infection) categorized into groups with (n = 88) and without (n = 65) PASC, defined by severe fatigue and concentration problems using validated cut-offs. Symptom clusters (i.e., component loadings and component scores) were identified using principal component analyses (PCA, eigenvalue[EV]>1.0), using clinical, somatic, coping and sleep factors, symptom severity, neuropsychological and physical tests (totalling 19 tests and questionnaires). We then used logistic regression techniques on (participant-level) component scores (standardized) to investigate associations with PASC. Finally, K-means clustering methods to identify clinical phenotypes. Analyses were adjusted for age, sex, education, nationality and time since infection. PCA identified 5 components, explaining 70% of the variance. We labelled these components as follows: (1) PEM, ME/CFS and sleep symptoms, coping factors (EV = 7.0, 36.9% variance), (2) information-processing speed (EV = 2.5, 13.3%), (3) executive functioning (EV = 1.5, 8.0%, (4) physical performance (EV = 1.2, 6.5%), (5) somatic comorbidities and hospital admission (EV = 1.0, 5.5%). Logistic regression showed that only the first component scores (Odds ratio [95% confidence interval] = 97.1 [16.5-570.3], p 0.05), associated with PASC. Cluster analysis revealed two distinct clinical phenotypes among individuals with severe chronic fatigue: one marked by physical impairment and the other by diminished cognitive performance. Consistent with existing literature, we confirmed that PASC is a heterogeneous syndrome marked by extensive, interrelated symptoms. Notably, we identified specific cognitive and physical clinical phenotypes. These findings are important for future targeted diagnosis and treatment.

title: Are the newly authorized antiviral drug treatment for non-severe COVID-19 may change the course of the pandemic?
abstract: Since the emergence of the coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has killed over 6.83 million and infected 670 million people worldwide. The disease is evolving, and numerous COVID-19 prevention and treatment have been approved or suggested. The only antiviral currently approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of COVID-19 is remdesivir (brand name Veklury). Molnupiravir (brand name Lagevrio) and ritonavir-booster nirmatrelvir (brand name Paxlovid) have been granted Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) for the treatment of COVID-19. Despite these antivirals having demonstrated efficacy for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in authorized patients; however, there is a restriction to who can take these antivirals due to the inaccessibility and drug-to-drug interactions that can be lethal to many immunocompromised and severe liver disease patients. With thousands of new COVID-19 cases reported daily, there needs to be more effective strategies to increase the accessibility of antivirals to stir the course of the pandemic and move out of it. This paper will review the current knowledge on antivirals for the treatment of SARS-CoV-2 and its mechanisms and highlight key research areas in the field that remain to be understood regarding antivirals, focusing on 1) why antivirals are inaccessible to many patients, 2) explore possible new treatments that could mitigate COVID-19 related inequalities and drug accessibility. By understanding the accessibility and mechanisms of the antivirals for COVID-19, researchers and health authorities will be able to promote effective and novel treatments and bring hope for more antivirals to change the course of the pandemic.

title: Random Matrix Theory Analysis of Global Agricultural Futures Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: We use Random Matrix Theory to analyze the impact of COVID-19 on the correlation structure of the agricultural futures market, using daily returns for 56 futures from various countries around the world before, during, and after COVID. For each of the three time periods, we build correlation matrices of the daily returns, and we examine the matrices’ entries, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. We find that agricultural futures exhibited stronger collective behavior during COVID than before or after it. We also find clustering based on geographic location, with there being one cluster in the West (North America, South America, Europe) and one in the East (Asia, Oceania), which show predominantly opposite-signed loadings relative to the dominant market mode; since pre-pandemic times, the East has gained weight in the market while the West has lost it. On top of regional clustering, we also find independent exchange-level clustering, where futures tend to be more correlated with futures in its same exchange than any other. Our results demonstrate how Random Matrix Theory can reveal both transient changes in collective behavior and longer-term structural patterns in an interconnected global market.

title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Widening the Gap? The Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Education for Students With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in an English Special School
abstract: Abstract This study explores how COVID-19 restrictions impacted on the provision of education for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), from the point of view of four parents and the headteacher at a special school in the North of England. Thematic analysis of the data through Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological theory and Biesta’s domains of education contextualised the effects of school closures and policies on the people and systems that students engage with, as well as how they both interact with one another. While existing research has largely examined the impact of school closures and remote learning, this case study highlights the critical role of specialist provision in supporting families and maintaining student wellbeing. Findings reveal how the pandemic exacerbated existing inequalities and exposed the marginalisation of SEND learners within policy and practice. The study calls for a radical reframing of education through a social model of disability, advocating for inclusive environments and pedagogies. Although focused on only one special school, insights offer valuable lessons for mainstream and specialist settings alike. Wellbeing must be embedded in educational policy and practice to better support all learners moving forward.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Epidemiología del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica: transmisión, carga viral salival y bioseguridad Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in dental practice: transmission, salivary viral load and biosafety
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la transmisión del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica, la carga viral salival y las medidas de bioseguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la saliva y los aerosoles de los procedimientos odontológicos son vías relevantes de transmisión. La detección molecular del virus en saliva respalda su papel como reservorio y como muestra diagnóstica. Los colutorios antisépticos reducen el virus in vitro, pero su efecto clínico sobre la carga viral salival es limitado. El triaje, la protección personal, el control de aerosoles y la teleodontología fueron las medidas centrales. Conclusión: la bioseguridad debe mantenerse como norma permanente.

title: Working Remotely from Home During and Post-COVID-19
abstract: Abstract The chapter reviews and analyzes the merits and challenges of people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States regarding working from home in the post-pandemic period when a return to office was mandated by both governments. Both countries had similar legislation regarding reasonable accommodations for people with disabilities. The Equality Act 2010 in the United Kingdom was comprehensive, covering disability as one of nine “protected characteristics.” The US ADA Title I focused exclusively on the employment of people with disability. The UK policy showed much more willingness to regulate the labor market during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period and allowed remote working. The US policy demonstrated less interference in the labor market during the pandemic and post-pandemic. The UK government was concerned with employer pushback on remote working and tended to disproportionally affect workers with disability regarding flexible arrangements. The UK policy recognized the right to flexible work, and employees with disabilities still had stronger protection under the “reasonable adjustment” framework. The US federal policy-imposed return-to-office mandate led to a rise in ADA lawsuits regarding the denial of remote work as a reasonable accommodation. The United States carried out the “essesntial functions” test, meaning the key legal question in many US cases was whether remote work eliminated an “essential function” of the job. Although courts aligned with employers vis-à-vis employees’ claims for working remotely, judges in some circuits started considering an employee’s remote work after the pandemic.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: UK and US Policies Regarding Employees with Disabilities During and Post-COVID-19 Pandemic and in a Few Low-Middle-Income-Countries
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, the United Kingdom and United States prioritized flexible working arrangements and adjustments for employees with disabilities, particularly those at higher risk. In the post-pandemic period, both nations have focused on solidifying these flexible arrangements but have also faced criticism over potentially regressive policies related to disability benefits. The UK approach focused on the expansion of access to work. However, the UK government proposed significant welfare reforms aimed at pushing more people into work. The United States prioritized post-pandemic Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) guidance that solidified the legal precedent for remote work as a reasonable accommodation under the ADA. Employers were required to evaluate renewed requests for remote work based on individual circumstances rather than reverting to pre-pandemic policies. Employers were expected to ensure a safe return-to-office (RTO) process but were not required to eliminate essential job functions to accommodate remote work. Finally, case law in the United States continued to evolve regarding what constituted an “undue hardship” for employers denying remote work, often referencing the successful remote work period during the pandemic. The COVID-19 pandemic disproportionately affected employees with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), exacerbating preexisting inequalities in employment, income, and access to services. Post-pandemic policies required a more comprehensive and systematic approach to address the deeper structural barriers to inclusion.
journal: Prospects for Employment of Persons with Disabilities in the Post-COVID-19 Era

title: Both sides of the CEO-to-employee pay ratio: evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Purpose Given that pay ratios did not decline following the Dodd-Frank disclosure mandate, we investigate how investors interpret these disclosures across normal and crisis periods. Exploiting the Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic to highlight variation in managerial talent and ability, we assess whether high pay ratios reflect efficient contracting or managerial opportunism and examine links to performance and chief executive officer (CEO) power. Design/methodology/approach We examine market reaction to CEO-to-employee pay ratio disclosures for S&P 1500 firms for 2018–2021. Using the COVID-19 pandemic as a macroeconomic shock, we define the event date as the Definitive Proxy Statement (Schedule 14A) (DEF 14A) filing and estimate a panel model with firm fixed effects. We control for firm, CEO, and industry characteristics and incorporate both traditional and social media sentiments as additional controls for the broader information environment surrounding proxy filings. Cross-sectional and robustness tests further distinguish between optimal contracting and rent-extraction explanations. Findings While announcement-period returns were negatively associated with pay ratios in 2018, this relation weakens and disappears during the COVID-19 period. This evidence is consistent with the possibility that investors place relatively greater weight on managerial ability considerations during the COVID-19 period, although the event-study design does not fully isolate the pay ratio component from other contemporaneous proxy disclosures. Firms with higher pay ratios exhibit stronger operating performance and higher valuation, particularly during the pandemic. Positive market reactions remain strongest in large firms and in firms with weaker CEO power. Originality/value This paper is the first to examine market reactions to pay ratio disclosures during the COVID-19 shock, providing a setting that sharpens identification between competing theories. It also links pay ratio levels to broader issues of employee treatment and within-firm inequality, offering a novel and integrated perspective on what high pay ratios reveal about managerial ability and firm dynamics.

title: Exploring Romanian Misinformation with GraphRAG: Community-Level Narratives of COVID-19
abstract: Predefined thematic taxonomies can obscure how misinformation narratives emerge, overlap, and change over time. One way to address this limitation is by developing bottom-up data-driven approaches that identify narratives directly from data. We present a pipeline that extracts entities and relations from news articles using GraphRAG, identifies communities using the Leiden algorithm, and uses this information to explore and predict misinformation. We evaluate the pipeline on a set of Romanian COVID-19 pandemic news articles with expert-defined narrative annotations and adapt the extraction prompts to Romanian. Exploratory results show that in this corpus, the graph for fake news is more fragmented and less modular than the graph for real news; it also contains higher proportions of events, disinformation theory, and vaccine entities, whereas the real-news graph contains higher proportions of locations, hospitals, and public health measures. Communities in the combined graph align weakly with the predefined super-narrative labels, indicating that the two representations group articles differently. Furthermore, expert review of similar articles from communities identified within the combined real–fake graph suggests that an approach based on entity and community may offer a promising avenue for identifying subtle misinformation strategies. Regarding the prediction task, a three-component ensemble that uses graph information achieves 85.86% macro-F1 (95% CI [78.50, 91.27]) and 86.51% accuracy (95% CI [78.57, 91.27]) on classifying articles as fake or true. These point estimates suggest incremental gains over the two-component ensemble without the graph similarity signal, though these gains are not statistically confirmed at this sample size. Together, these exploratory results illustrate the use of GraphRAG as a tool in pipelines that support the exploration and prediction of misinformation.

title: The Capital Flow Management in the Global Economy During the COVID-19 Pandemic and After the Russian Invasion of Ukraine – A Comparative Analysis
abstract: This article analyses the evolution of capital flows management (CFM) measures in the global economy between 2017 and 2023, with particular attention to the COVID-19 pandemic and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Drawing on data from the IMF’s Annual Report on Exchange Arrangements and Exchange Restrictions (IMF AREAER), the study evaluates how different groups of economies: advanced, emerging market, developing and low‐income developing countries, used tightening and easing measures to manage capital inflows and outflows. The findings suggest a shift in the use of CFMs: from predominantly temporary, counter-cyclical instruments of liquidity management during the pandemic to more preventive and, in some cases, security-linked measures in the post-2022 geopolitical environment. The analysis shows that emerging and developing economies displayed the highest policy intensity, while advanced economies increasingly integrated CFMs with investment screening and financial‐security policies. The findings are consistent with the IMF’s revised Institutional View in that they suggest a broader and more preventive role for CFMs within the macrofinancial policy toolkit, bridging monetary, prudential, and, in some cases, security-related objectives. By linking empirical evidence from the pandemic and wartime periods, this article contributes to the ongoing debate on the balance between financial openness and resilience. It argues that, in the context of geoeconomic fragmentation, capital flows management is increasingly being used not only as a stabilisation mechanism but also, in some cases, as a strategic instrument linked to national and systemic resilience.

title: Selected metrics of children’s health 2 years after COVID-19 infection
abstract: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has concluded, ongoing research on the disease remains a priority. Analyzing the long-term consequences of COVID-19 infection is particularly important. To evaluate the impact of COVID-19 on healthcare-visit incidence rates, chronic pathology prevalence, infection index (II), and resistance index (RI) among children in Chelyabinsk two years after infection, compared with the pre-pandemic period. Materials and methods. We used random sampling to review medical record forms No. 30/y and 112/y for 107 children aged 3 to 15 years who were diagnosed with COVID-19 between July and August 2021. The II and RI were calculated based on the number of prior respiratory illnesses. The incidence rates were analyzed by healthcare visits, with each completed case considered one disease episode. Descriptive analysis assessed increases in chronic diseases and incidence rates, calculating both absolute and relative changes in indicators. Incidence rates based on healthcare visits increased across most classes of the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision. Chapter IV (Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases; +133%) and Chapter XIII (Diseases of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue; +75%) showed the largest relative increases. Chapter XI (Diseases of the digestive system) had the largest absolute increase (+21 cases). Recurrent infections were more frequently associated with chronic pathology (50% of cases). Hospitalization data were not collected in this study. The findings underscore the need for regular monitoring of health metrics (II, RI, morbidity) in children with a history of COVID-19. The results also emphasize the importance of further prospective studies to refine follow-up protocols, develop personalized rehabilitation strategies, and prevent post-COVID complications in pediatric populations.

title: Host Protein Palmitoylation: A Two-Edged Sword in the Pathogenesis of COVID-19
abstract: Protein palmitoylation is a two-edged sword in regulating Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. On the one hand, SARS-CoV-2 hijacks the host’s palmitoyl transferases (ZDHHC5/9/20) to modify its spike protein (S protein), enhancing its stability, membrane anchoring, and fusion, consequently facilitating SARS-CoV-2 entry, replication, and release. On the other hand, the host utilises this modification to activate antiviral defences: palmitoylation of the mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein (MAVS) leads to its accumulation in the mitochondria and initiates interferon signalling; palmitoylation of the stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is essential for its activation and transport; and palmitoylation of interferon-induced transmembrane protein 3 (IFITM3) increases its ability to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 membrane fusion. This defensive–offensive interplay within the same regulatory system offers fresh opportunities for targeted therapy, including the development of specific ZDHHC inhibitors, palmitoylated angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2)-based decoy vesicles, and metabolic intervention approaches. In the future, it will be necessary to conduct in-depth analyses of the functions of key modification sites and develop precise regulatory strategies to address the ongoing threat posed by coronaviruses.

This defensive–offensive interplay within the same regulatory system offers fresh opportunities for targeted therapy, including the development of specific ZDHHC inhibitors, palmitoylated angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2)-based decoy vesicles, and metabolic intervention approaches. In the future, it will be necessary to conduct in-depth analyses of the functions of key modification sites and develop precise regulatory strategies to address the ongoing threat posed by coronaviruses.

title: Evaluating the effects of population mobility on transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Abstract Changes to community mobility during the COVID-19 pandemic, together with unprecedented availability of surveillance and mobility data, provide a unique opportunity to quantify the effect of mobility on respiratory infection transmission. We present a renewal model that incorporates epidemiological mechanisms influencing SARS-CoV-2 transmission along with a non-mechanistic scaling process. We compare models with and without mobility using epidemic data from 122 countries and quantify the influence of mobility through reductions in non-mechanistic scaling. In several countries, this non-mechanistic process closely tracks mobility trends and varies substantially less when mobility is incorporated. This is especially evident in Western Europe and North America, but not in several countries of West Africa and the Arabian Peninsula. Google and Facebook data produce similar findings, and parks is frequently assigned the lowest weight in the multi-location Google analysis. Mobility trends are strongly aligned with short-term transmission dynamics in many high-income settings, although between-country heterogeneity remains.

title: CORRELATION SIGNS OF CLINICAL COURSE AND DIAGNOSTIC FEATURES OF CRANIAL POLYNEUROPATHIES AFTER COVID-19 INFECTION COVID-19 INFEKSIYASIDAN KEYIN RIVOJLANGAN KRANIAL POLINEVROPATIYALARNING KLINIK KECHISHI VA DIAGNOSTIK XUSUSIYATLARI O‘RTASIDAGI KORRELYATSION BELGILAR
abstract: This study focuses on the clinical course and diagnostic features of cranial polyneuropathy in patients following COVID-19 infection. A total of 30 patients aged 18–60 years were examined. Clinical, neurological, and laboratory investigations were performed. Changes in leukocyte, lymphocyte, platelet, thrombocrit, and D-dimer levels were observed in the studied patients. These changes were associated with a prolonged course of the disease, delayed recovery, and persistent focal neurological symptoms. The results emphasize the importance of clinical and laboratory assessment in patients with post-COVID cranial polyneuropathy.
journal: YANGI DAVR ILM-FANI: INSON UCHUN INNOVATSION G‘OYA VA YECHIMLAR

title: Western Responses to COVID-19
abstract: Abstract There were three stages of learning about the COVID pandemic. First came lessons learned from past pandemics, four of which appeared relevant. These lessons were re-evaluated when good data became available about the infectivity and lethality of COVID and the effectiveness of various methods for treating patients. These lessons, their application, and the problems and success of public health responses were then re-evaluated in the aftermath of the pandemic. At each stage of learning, the chapter evaluates the relevance of the propositions developed in Chapter 2. The chapter addresses variation across the West in responses to COVID and the reasons for this variation. It also explores the degree and politicization of public health and its consequences.

title: Pacientes con COVID-19 grave en cuidados intensivos: revisión narrativa Patients with severe COVID-19 in intensive care: a narrative review
abstract: Objetivo: analizar las características clínicas, la mortalidad, los factores de riesgo y los tratamientos de los pacientes con COVID-19 grave ingresados en unidades de cuidados intensivos. Método: revisión narrativa de literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: cohortes, un metaanálisis y ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Resultados: en Europa, cerca de tres cuartas partes de los pacientes críticos eran varones y la mitad tenía hipertensión. La mortalidad en cuidados intensivos descendió del 60 % al 36 % durante 2020, pero en América Latina alcanzó el 59 % en Brasil y el 47,8 % en Medellín. La edad, la diabetes, la obesidad y la hipoxemia grave aumentaron el riesgo de muerte. La dexametasona, el tocilizumab y la posición prona en pacientes despiertos mejoraron los desenlaces. Conclusión: el pronóstico depende de la gravedad al ingreso y de la aplicación de tratamientos con eficacia demostrada.
journal: Sanitas. Revista arbitrada de ciencias de la salud

title: Alteraciones hepáticas en pacientes con COVID-19 y estrategias terapéuticas: revisión narrativa Liver abnormalities in patients with COVID-19 and therapeutic strategies: a narrative review
abstract: Objetivo: describir la frecuencia, el significado pronóstico y el manejo terapéutico de las alteraciones hepáticas en pacientes con COVID-19. Método: revisión narrativa de la literatura indexada en PubMed y SciELO entre 2020 y 2022; se seleccionaron 15 documentos: seis estudios observacionales, cinco revisiones y cuatro ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Resultados: la alteración de las pruebas hepáticas osciló entre el 14 % y más del 50 % de los pacientes hospitalizados, predominó la elevación de aminotransferasas y fue más frecuente en la enfermedad grave. En la India, la mortalidad fue del 19,6 % con disfunción hepática frente al 2,1 % sin ella. La dexametasona redujo la mortalidad en pacientes con oxígeno o ventilación; lopinavir/ritonavir, hidroxicloroquina e interferón no mostraron beneficio. Conclusión: las alteraciones hepáticas son frecuentes y suelen ser transitorias, pero señalan mayor gravedad; su manejo exige vigilancia bioquímica y ajuste de fármacos potencialmente hepatotóxicos.

title: Research attitudes through the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Introduction Identifying the factors that influence attitudes toward biomedical research is essential for improving public engagement and participation. The COVID-19 pandemic offers a unique opportunity to assess how a public health crisis shapes perceptions of clinical research. We investigated whether attitudes toward biomedical research differed across phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods We analyzed data from 5,098 adults enrolled in the UC Irvine Consent-to-Contact (C2C) registry, an online voluntary recruitment registry in Southern California, between June 2016 and August 2025. Research attitudes were assessed with the validated 7-item Research Attitudes Questionnaire (RAQ) at enrollment and annually thereafter. Scores were analyzed continuously (7 -35) and dichotomously, with >28 defined a priori as high. COVID-19 periods were defined a priori as: P1 (before March 13, 2020—the U.S. national emergency declaration), P2 (March 13 to December 11, 2020—prior to COVID-19 vaccine approval), and P3 (after December 11, 2020—post-vaccine approval). Cross-sectional analyses included all participants; longitudinal analyses were limited to 1,388 participants who enrolled before March 2020 and had ≥3 assessments. Results Our sample of 5,098 adults was predominantly non-Hispanic White (70.2%), female (65.7%), highly educated, and over age 50 (66.7%). Participants enrolling during P2 had 60% higher odds of a high RAQ score (>28) compared with P1 (aOR 1.60; 95% CI: 1.07, 2.40; p =0.022). Longitudinally, the mean within-subject RAQ score was significantly higher during P2 versus P1 (Est. 0.37; 95% CI: 0.08, 0.66; p =0.011), and the odds of a high RAQ score were 24% higher in P2 (aOR 1.24; 95% CI: 1.09, 1.39; p <0.001) compared to P1. Discussion These findings suggest that awareness of urgent medical issues, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, may affect attitudes toward research.

title: COVID-19 Geçiren Böbrek Nakli Alıcılarında Persistan veya Kötüleşen Lenfopeni Mortaliteyi Öngörür: Lymphopenia in KTRs with COVID-19
abstract: Objective: Kidney transplant recipients are at increased risk for severe coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) because of chronic immunosuppressive therapy and impaired cellular immunity. Lymphopenia is a well-established predictor of adverse outcomes in the general population; however, the prognostic significance of persistent lymphopenia during hospitalization in kidney transplant recipients remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia and clinical outcomes, including mortality and renal function, in hospitalized kidney transplant recipients with COVID-19.Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study including adult kidney transplant recipients hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 at a tertiary referral center between March 2020 and January 2022. Patients were classified based on the presence or absence of persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia during hospitalization. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, laboratory findings, treatments, and clinical outcomes were compared between groups. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included intensive care unit (ICU) admission, requirement for respiratory support, requirement for invasive mechanical ventilation, length of hospital stay, requirement for hemodialysis, and renal function at 90 days after discharge. Independent predictors of mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression analysis.Results: A total of 181 kidney transplant recipients were included, 63% of whom developed persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia. Patients with persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia experienced significantly higher rates of ICU admission, respiratory support, invasive mechanical ventilation, prolonged hospitalization, and in-hospital mortality compared with other patients (all p < 0.05). They also had significantly higher levels of inflammatory markers, including ferritin and C-reactive protein. In multivariable analysis, persistent/exacerbated lymphopenia remained independently associated with in-hospital mortality after adjustment for age, inflammatory markers, and hemodialysis requirement [adjusted odds ratio 14.16 (95% confidence interval: 3.6-55.7), p < 0.001]. However, persistent lymphopenia was not associated with loss of renal function at 90 days.Conclusion: Persistent or exacerbated lymphopenia during hospitalization is a strong independent predictor of in-hospital mortality among kidney transplant recipients with COVID-19 and is associated with greater disease severity and increased resource utilization. In contrast, it does not appear to predict 90-day renal function decline. Serial assessment of lymphocyte counts may provide a simple, inexpensive, and readily available tool for early risk stratification in hospitalized kidney transplant recipients with COVID-19.

title: STABILITY OF AN ELISA TEST SYSTEM BASED ON A RECOMBINANT CHIMERIC SM PROTEIN FOR THE DETECTION OF ANTIBODIES TO SARS-COV-2 UNDER DIFFERENT TEMPERATURE CONDITIONS
abstract: Assessment of the stability of kit components is a critical step in the development of enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) systems, as it directly determines the accuracy and reproducibility of diagnostic results during storage and routine use. In the present study, the stability and reproducibility of a newly developed ELISA test system based on the recombinant chimeric SM protein were evaluated under different temperature conditions. The stability of the kit components was assessed by monitoring changes in the analytical signal, expressed as optical density (OD), and the variability of replicate measurements, expressed as the coefficient of variation (CV, %), over a controlled period at -20oC, 4oC, 22oC, and 37oC. The results demonstrated that the stability of the developed ELISA test system was strongly temperature-dependent. Standard refrigerated storage at 4oC was identified as the optimal condition, providing the highest preservation of the analytical signal, with 81.3% of the initial signal retained (OD450 = 1.933), while maintaining high reproducibility (CV = 1.74%), consistently below the predefined acceptance threshold of ≤5%. Storage at -20oC showed notable limitations. Despite maintaining a relatively high analytical signal (OD450 = 1.623) and 68.2% residual activity, freezing and thawing of the reagents resulted in increased analytical variability (CV = 5.56%), exceeding the established acceptance criterion. Exposure to elevated temperatures of 22oC and 37oC had a pronounced detrimental effect on test-system stability, resulting in degradation of protein components and a loss of more than 65% of the initial activity. These findings demonstrate that, to ensure long-term preservation of the sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of the developed ELISA diagnostic kit, storage at 4oC under properly maintained cold-chain conditions is an essential technological requirement.

title: A multiscale mechanical model for flexible spike protein-mediated SARS-CoV-2 viral entry into host cells.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has so far been sustained by recurrent outbreaks, largely owing to the strong contagiousness of SARS-CoV-2 (SARS2). Here, to explain its high infectivity from a mechanical viewpoint, we propose a multiscale mechanical model that links molecular-scale binding with cell-scale endocytosis in the initial stage of viral entry mediated by flexible spike (S) proteins. With three hinges in the stalk domain, SARS2-S has unanticipated orientational freedom, giving rise to a high binding affinity up to 10 times that of SARS-S binding with ACE2. Interestingly, when SARS2-S is in the "RBD-down" conformation, the affinity decreases dramatically to only one thousandth of that of SARS-S binding with ACE2, suggesting that the conformational hiding of the receptor-binding site in this flexible state could reduce its exposure to the host immune system and therapeutic antibodies. Therefore, the mechanical properties of S proteins can be exploited by the virus to enhance its recognition of host ACE2 and attachment to host cells. As S proteins bind to ACE2 receptors, the resulting S-ACE2 complexes bridge the viral and host-cell membranes and progressively accumulate at the virus-cell interface, while their deformation and loading states evolve continuously during subsequent membrane wrapping. Increasing molecular stiffness enhances the interfacial pulling force, and the resulting increase in complex stiffness further amplifies this effect. It should be noted that excessively high molecular or complex stiffness, a higher membrane bending modulus, and a larger viral size all increase the mechanical resistance to late-stage membrane wrapping. Together, these results shed light on the pivotal role of molecular flexibility in the initial stage of viral entry, showing how spike flexibility regulates both ACE2 recognition and the mechanical progression of membrane wrapping, and may provide guidance for vaccine development and drug design.

source_records.title: A multiscale mechanical model for flexible spike protein-mediated SARS-CoV-2 viral entry into host cells.
source_records.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has so far been sustained by recurrent outbreaks, largely owing to the strong contagiousness of SARS-CoV-2 (SARS2). Here, to explain its high infectivity from a mechanical viewpoint, we propose a multiscale mechanical model that links molecular-scale binding with cell-scale endocytosis in the initial stage of viral entry mediated by flexible spike (S) proteins. With three hinges in the stalk domain, SARS2-S has unanticipated orientational freedom, giving rise to a high binding affinity up to 10 times that of SARS-S binding with ACE2. Interestingly, when SARS2-S is in the "RBD-down" conformation, the affinity decreases dramatically to only one thousandth of that of SARS-S binding with ACE2, suggesting that the conformational hiding of the receptor-binding site in this flexible state could reduce its exposure to the host immune system and therapeutic antibodies. Therefore, the mechanical properties of S proteins can be exploited by the virus to enhance its recognition of host ACE2 and attachment to host cells. As S proteins bind to ACE2 receptors, the resulting S-ACE2 complexes bridge the viral and host-cell membranes and progressively accumulate at the virus-cell interface, while their deformation and loading states evolve continuously during subsequent membrane wrapping. Increasing molecular stiffness enhances the interfacial pulling force, and the resulting increase in complex stiffness further amplifies this effect. It should be noted that excessively high molecular or complex stiffness, a higher membrane bending modulus, and a larger viral size all increase the mechanical resistance to late-stage membrane wrapping. Together, these results shed light on the pivotal role of molecular flexibility in the initial stage of viral entry, showing how spike flexibility regulates both ACE2 recognition and the mechanical progression of membrane wrapping, and may provide guidance for vaccine development and drug design.

title: Post SARS-CoV-2 sequelae in healthcare personnel of a non-COVID institution in Mexico City
abstract: Background: COVID-19 is a disease caused by SARS-CoV-2, a highly contagious virus belonging to the Coronaviridae family.It is transmitted from person to person through the air.The clinical presentation ranges from mild to severe can be fatal.Worldwide, 10-20% of people who recover from the acute phase may continue to experience symptoms for a longer period.Objectives: To estimate the prevalence of post-SARS-CoV-2 sequelae in staff of a tertiary healthcare institution, five years after the beginning of the pandemic, and to describe the types of sequelae by sex and year of onset according to the different infection episodes.Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted based on self-administered surveys.The study population consisted of 179 participants.Sequelae were evaluated in relation to the different infection episodes.Results: A peak in health impact on staff was observed during 2022 (37%).59.2% of the population presented some type of sequelae; the majority (95%) experienced some sequelae after the first episode of infection.The most prevalent sequelae were neuro logical and state of mind (66.4%), musculoskeletal (51.5%), and respiratory (36.6%), with a predominance in females (p ≤ 0.05).Conclusions: The obtained results are similar to those reported in previous studies.The most prevalent sequelae were neurological and persisted throughout the study period, primarily in women.

title: Serologic Testing for Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus and SARS-CoV-2 Cross-Reactive Immune Responses, the Netherlands
abstract: Cross-reactive SARS-CoV-2–specific antibodies could compromise the specificity of MERS-CoV serology, potentially leading to misclassification of infection history. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced MERS-CoV antibodies primarily targeting the conserved S2 domain, with occasional neutralizing capacity. Combining MERS-CoV S1 binding with neutralization, however, limited the influence of SARS-CoV-2–induced cross-reactivity on MERS-CoV serology.

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: Normative dynamics in the acquisition of COVID-19 vaccines and the echoes of coloniality
abstract: This article analyzes the influence of the coloniality of power on Brazilian legislation concerning vaccine procurement in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on the analysis of Law No. 13,979/2020 and subsequent legal frameworks, it examines the impacts of regulatory flexibilization on the Brazilian State. Laurence Bardin’s Content Analysis method is employed to identify categories that reveal the central role of transnational pharmaceutical corporations in the relativization of national regulatory sovereignty. The study demonstrates that such measures, although justified by sanitary urgency, reproduce structural patterns of dependence and subordination typical of the coloniality of power, as theorized by authors such as Aníbal Quijano, Walter Mignolo, Enrique Dussel, and Boaventura de Sousa Santos, among others. It concludes that the model adopted contributed to the weakening of national sovereignty and to the expansion of dependence on hegemonic centers of knowledge and technology production.

title: Non-structural protein 6: a hallmark of SARS-CoV-2 disease progression and its connection to lipid droplets
abstract: The genome of SARS-CoV-2 has been heavily studied with the roles of many enzymatic, and structural proteins being well-defined. However, knowledge remains limited for the 16 non-structural proteins (NSPs) known to be encoded by the genome. Until recently, these NSPs were not considered to be of importance for the viral lifecycle. Recent findings have demonstrated that NSP6 is a key determinant of disease progression. It is a multifunctional protein involved in the stimulation of the formation of double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), inhibition of autophagosome expansion within the cell, and induction of pyroptosis along with additional functions. In addition, many (+) ssRNA viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, have been shown to manipulate lipid droplets (LDs), highly conserved intracellular organelles that are composed of neutral lipids, as substrates for energy and as platforms for their replication. This article will highlight the current knowledge on NSP6 encoded in the SARS-CoV-2 genome and the involvement of LDs in the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle, focusing on 1) NSP6 and its integral role as a determinant of viral pathogenicity and 2) the relation of NSP6 with the functionality of LDs in relation to DMVs and SARS-CoV-2 pathogenesis. It is evident that NSP6 is a critical protein to target in order to disrupt the viral life cycle. Thus, understanding the molecular details of the NSPs and their roles in the viral pathway presents an opportunity to identify potential therapeutic targets. Therefore, further investigation into the involvement of NSPs in disease progression is essential for furthering our understanding of the SARS-CoV-2 infection cycle.

title: Identification of SLC15A3 as a shared prognostic biomarker for AML and COVID-19 via integrative bioinformatics, machine learning and Mendelian randomization
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA regulatory networks, and established an AML prognostic model to evaluate the tumor immune microenvironment. Combining survival analysis, clinical correlation, immune infiltration assessment and m 6 A modification analysis, SLC15A3 was preliminarily screened as a candidate prognostic gene for AML. Subsequent weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning (ML) and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses further identified SLC15A3 as a promising prognostic biomarker for AML. Finally, RT-qPCR and Western blotting assays verified its aberrant expression in AML cells. Consistent with bioinformatic prediction, SLC15A3 serves as a shared candidate biomarker for AML and COVID-19,although its mechanistic role linking AML and SARS-CoV-2-related inflammation requires further functional validation.

title: Computational Analysis of Immunohistochemistry Enables Quantitative Assessment of SARS-CoV-2 Nucleocapsid Immunolabeling in Experimentally Infected Mice
abstract: Histopathology and immunohistochemistry (IHC) are central to COVID-19 tissue evaluation. However, conventional manual scoring is limited by its semiquantitative nature and potential observer variability. In this retrospective study of experimentally infected mice, we implemented a semi-automated digital pathology workflow using commercially available software to quantitatively assess SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (N) immunolabeling in lung (n = 135) and brain (n = 67) tissues. The performance of digital quantification was evaluated against conventional manual scoring, and its association with virological and pathological parameters was assessed across different stages of disease progression. Digital IHC quantification demonstrated strong agreement with manual scoring in both lung [R = 0.94, p < 0.0001, concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) = 0.95] and brain [R = 0.98, p < 0.0001; CCC = 0.977], demonstrating concordance between the two approaches. In addition, digital SARS-CoV-2 N immunolabeling quantification showed significant positive correlations with viral RNA levels, infectious viral titers, and histopathological scores, supporting its association with independent measures of SARS-CoV-2 infection and lesions. Although computational image analysis requires additional infrastructure, technical expertise, and increased analysis time, it provides an objective continuous quantitative measure of SARS-CoV-2 N immunolabeling that complements conventional manual assessment and may reduce observer-dependent variability.

title: Biochemical Parameters Associated With COVID-19 Severity: A Statistical Analysis
abstract: Objectives Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by the SARS-CoV-2, is a contagious infectious disease. The aim of the present study is to identify the most effective biochemical parameters associated with COVID-19 severity. Early identification of these parameters is crucial for rapid risk stratification of patients and for initiating timely clinical management. Material and Methods A total of 584 patients with COVID-19 admitted to a tertiary care hospital in Mysuru, Karnataka, were included in the study. The routinely measured biochemical parameters obtained after hospital admission were evaluated for their association with the study outcome. Descriptive statistics, independent sample t -test, Pearson’s correlation analysis, binary logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were performed at a 5% level of significance using IBM SPSS Statistics version 22. Results Demographic and clinical characteristics showed that male patients, 427 (73%) and older adults aged 60–80 years, 157 (48.5%), constituted the largest proportion of hospitalised patients with COVID-19. A higher proportion of male patients was observed in both the ICU 16 (2.74%) and non-ICU 411 (70.38%) groups. Correlation analysis demonstrated mild to moderate associations among selected biochemical markers. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, serum creatinine was the only biochemical parameter significantly associated with the study outcome (OR = 0.265; p = 0.027) and also demonstrated acceptable discriminatory performance in the ROC analysis. Conclusion Early identification of biochemical abnormalities improves clinical prognosis by enabling timely risk stratification and appropriate therapeutic intervention. These findings support the routine assessment of biochemical parameters as part of the initial evaluation of patients with COVID-19.

Descriptive statistics, independent sample t -test, Pearson’s correlation analysis, binary logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were performed at a 5% level of significance using IBM SPSS Statistics version 22. Results Demographic and clinical characteristics showed that male patients, 427 (73%) and older adults aged 60–80 years, 157 (48.5%), constituted the largest proportion of hospitalised patients with COVID-19. A higher proportion of male patients was observed in both the ICU 16 (2.74%) and non-ICU 411 (70.38%) groups. Correlation analysis demonstrated mild to moderate associations among selected biochemical markers. In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, serum creatinine was the only biochemical parameter significantly associated with the study outcome (OR = 0.265; p = 0.027) and also demonstrated acceptable discriminatory performance in the ROC analysis. Conclusion Early identification of biochemical abnormalities improves clinical prognosis by enabling timely risk stratification and appropriate therapeutic intervention. These findings support the routine assessment of biochemical parameters as part of the initial evaluation of patients with COVID-19.

title: The toll of voting in a pandemic? Regional elections and the spread of COVID-19 in Bavaria
abstract: This study investigates whether the regional elections held in the German state of Bavaria on March 15 of 2020 - shortly after the WHO declared COVID-19 a global pandemic - contributed to the spread of COVID-19 cases and COVID-related deaths. Constructing synthetic controls for each of Bavaria's 96 districts based on non-Bavarian German districts, we find that over a third of the increase in positive test results cannot be explained by district-level demographic, economic, health or child care characteristics, nor by the distance to Ischgl - a proxy for skiing tourism associated with the first COVID-19 wave in Germany. Within Bavaria, districts with higher voter participation witnessed a steeper increase in COVID-19 cases and deaths after the election, while controlling for alternative drivers, such as the distance to Ischgl and the number of strong-beer festivals. Our results are highly robust and suggest that an unfortunate timing of elections contributed to the spreading of an infectious disease.
journal: The European Journal of Health Economics

title: A Novel Chemotype of Orally Active SARS-CoV-2 NSP14 Methyltransferase Inhibitors
abstract: Abstract The periodic emergence of human coronaviruses (hCoVs) necessitates direct-acting antivirals targeting underexploited viral proteins with broad-spectrum potential. Building on our discovery of TDI-015051, a first-in-class SARS-CoV-2 mRNA cap guanine-N7 methyltransferase (MTase) NSP14 inhibitor whose translational development was limited by metabolic liabilities, we conducted medicinal chemistry optimization of a structurally distinct high-throughput screening hit. We arrived at MAVDA-K-256, a small-molecule inhibitor with improved pharmacological properties compared to TDI-015051. MAVDA-K-256 engaged NSP14 through the formation of a ternary complex with S-adenosyl-l-homocysteine, potently inhibiting its MTase activity and SARS-CoV-2 replication (EC50 = 24.6 nM). MAVDA-K-256 demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse hCoVs without targeting the host mRNA cap MTase. Its favorable metabolic stability and pharmacokinetic properties enabled twice-daily oral dosing in a murine SARS-CoV-2 infection model, resulting in a five-log reduction in viral lung burden. These findings validate NSP14 inhibition as a promising antiviral strategy and support further preclinical development of MAVDA-K-256.

title: Glycemic control and COVID-19 outcomes across the continuum of glucose regulation: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Introduction Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has disproportionately affected individuals with underlying metabolic dysfunction. This study investigates the association between varying levels of pre-infection glycemic control and COVID-19-related health outcomes. Methods A retrospective chart review was conducted on Kaiser Permanente Georgia patients with confirmed COVID-19. Participants (N = 2071) were categorized into five groups based on their HbA1c levels: patients without diabetes, those with prediabetes, and those with diabetes with varying degrees of glycemic control. We adjusted for demographics, social determinants of health, comorbidities, medications, and lifestyle factors. Results Among 2071 patients, 986 (47.6%) were without diabetes, 658 (31.8%) had prediabetes, 183 (8.8%) had diabetes with HbA1c 9%. Patients with HbA1c>9% had the highest proportion hospitalized (38.3%, p<0.001), and admitted to ICU (14.8%, p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression models, prediabetes and insulin use were associated with greater odds of hospitalization; odds ratio 1.43 [95% CI 1.09-1.87] and 3.02 [95% CI 1.95-4.68], respectively. Conclusions There is a gradient of increasing COVID-19 severity with worsening glycemic control. The study shows the importance of recognizing prediabetes as a significant risk factor for severe COVID-19, comparable to poorly controlled diabetes.
journal: Frontiers in Clinical Diabetes and Healthcare

title: COVID-19 and subsequent new allergy drug prescriptions: a matched cohort study in Japan
abstract: Emerging evidence indicates that COVID-19 may increase the incidence of new allergic conditions requiring medication. This matched cohort study investigated the impact of COVID-19 on new allergy medication prescriptions utilizing Japan’s National Insurance Claims Database. The study compared the incidence rate ratio (IRR) and difference (IRD) of new prescriptions for H1 antihistamines, leukotriene receptor antagonists, eye drops, and nasal sprays between groups. Additionally, subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the heterogeneity among subgroups and the long-term effects of COVID-19 on allergy medication prescriptions. A total of 778,362 Patients with COVID-19 and matched controls were followed for a median of 7 months. The IRR for new prescriptions of H1 antihistamines, leukotriene receptor antagonists, eye drops, and nasal sprays was 1.21 (95% CI, 1.2–1.23), with an IRD of 1,528 per 1,000,000 person-months (95% CI, 1,492–1,564). Subgroup analyses showed higher IRRs for individuals aged ≥ 65 years (IRR: 1.33, 95% CI: 1.31–1.35) and those with Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) scores ≥ 4 (IRR: 1.35, 95% CI: 1.31–1.38). Sensitivity analyses IRRs remained higher than controls, particularly in older adults and those with higher CCI scores. Age ≥ 65 years (IRR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.11–1.18) and CCI scores ≥ 4 (IRR: 1.17, 95% CI: 1.11–1.23) were significant even after 1 year. These findings suggest COVID-19 may have a lasting impact on the incidence of new allergy medication prescriptions, especially in vulnerable populations, underscoring the need for continued monitoring and personalized post-COVID-19 support.

title: Current Trends in Drug Discovery Using Bioinformatics Tools Targeting SARS-CoV-2
abstract: The COVID-19 epidemic caused by SARS-CoV-2 has demanded better therapeutic approaches. Through developments in bioinformatics and computational biology, extensive screening for prospective antiviral molecules has been performed against the crucial viral proteins like the main protease (Mpro), papain-like protease (PLpro), RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase (RdRp) and the spike (S) glycoprotein exhibiting host cell entry through ACE2 receptor. A number of lead phytochemicals including flavonoids, terpenoids and alkaloids exhibited potential antiviral activities positively determined by molecular docking and dynamics simulations and exhibited a strong interaction affinity with Mpro and spike proteins. The objective of the current study is although immediate outbreak response to drug redosing via in silico screening, the existing antiviral drugs and bexarotene as COVID-19 therapeutics. These computational methods 64 facilitate discovery of new drugs by allowing predictions of pharmacologic interactions, stability, etc prior to clinical testing. The combination of phytochemical screening and chemical repurposing techniques represents an inexpensive approach for the identification of new bioactives to fight SARS-CoV-2 and other related viral challenges.
journal: Intelligent Applications in Bioinformatics and Healthcare Technologies

title: Assessment of the Association between Myocarditis (New-onset Heart Failure) and COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Introduction: Myocarditis is a rare but significant cardiovascular complication that may occur after receiving COVID-19 vaccines, particularly in younger individuals. The majority of cases have been reported after receiving mRNA-based vaccines, while inactivated and viral vector-based vaccines have been associated with fewer occurrences. Despite this, myocarditis is much more common and results in a poorer prognosis following COVID-19 infection. However, the relationship between myocarditis post-vaccination and its potential mechanisms remains unclear due to limited information. Methods: This study investigated patients with myocarditis (new-onset heart failure) who had received the COVID-19 vaccine and those who had been infected with COVID-19 between March 2021 and March 2023 in Farshchian Cardiovascular Hospital in Hamedan. The data was analyzed using Stata version 14 software and Python. Results: Among 146 myocarditis patients, unvaccinated individuals had higher rates of hypertension, diabetes, obstructive pulmonary disease, and substance abuse, and exhibited more severe cardiac issues like mitral regurgitation and ventricular dysfunction. Vaccinated patients had better lab results and fewer severe symptoms. A model identified advanced age and cardiovascular dysfunction as key mortality risks, suggesting vaccination may mitigate severe cardiac complications and improve outcomes. Conclusion: The findings of this study show that although there is a risk of myocarditis as a side effect following the COVID-19 vaccination, its severity is far less than the occurrence following the COVID-19 infection, with fewer complications and a better prognosis. However, more studies are still necessary to complete the existing findings and clarify their unknown aspects.

title: Reducing Poverty and Income Inequality Through Zakat Redistribution During the COVID-19 Crisis
abstract: Poverty and income inequality remain persistent development challenges across many countries, including those with established zakat management systems. Although zakat is widely recognized as an Islamic social finance instrument capable of improving social welfare, empirical evidence regarding the effectiveness of zakat redistribution across different economic conditions, particularly before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic, remains limited. This study addresses this gap by examining whether zakat redistribution effectively reduces poverty and income inequality and whether its effectiveness is state-dependent across crisis and recovery regimes. This study employs the Pooled Mean Group Autoregressive Distributed Lag (PMG-ARDL) approach using quarterly panel data from eight countries covering the 2016-2025 period. Quarterly observations were generated through quadratic match-average interpolation. Two empirical models, poverty and income inequality, were estimated while controlling for GDP per capita, inflation, and the Human Development Index. The findings reveal that zakat redistribution exerts a significant negative effect on poverty in both the short and long run, with the strongest long-run impact occurring during the COVID-19 period. Regarding income inequality, zakat redistribution produces a significant long-run negative effect, whereas the short-run effect is significant only for the full-sample estimation. Robustness tests using Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares (FMOLS) and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares (DOLS) confirm the consistency of the PMG-ARDL estimates. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening zakat governance, collection, redistribution, and digitalization to enhance poverty alleviation and inequality reduction, particularly during future economic crises.

title: Early inflammation-driven damage and delayed viral clearance are associated with prolonged biliary perturbation in a Cameroonian cohort of COVID-19 patients
abstract: Although COVID-19-associated liver abnormalities are documented, the link between delayed viral clearance, IgG seroconversion, and inflammation remains poorly defined, particularly in Sub-Saharan African populations, where baseline liver enzymes differ from Western standards. In 38 SARS-CoV-2-positive individuals monitored at D0, D14, and D30, we quantified liver biomarkers (ALT, AST, BILT, BILD) by spectrophotometry (COBAS), plasma IL-6 by Luminex, viral load (N and ORF1ab genes) by RT-qPCR, and IgG/IgM serology. Analyses were performed in GraphPad Prism v9.0. ALT and AST rose transiently at D14, returning to baseline by D30. IL-6 peaked at D14 and correlated positively with BILT (r = 0.64, p = 0.001) and BILD (r = 0.54, p = 0.006). ORF1ab Ct at D14 correlated negatively with ALT at D0 (r = -0.67, p = 0.004) and D14 (r = -0.71, p = 0.006); N gene Ct at D14 correlated with ALT at D0 (r = -0.61, p = 0.011). Mixed-effects models identified IL-6 as the sole independent predictor of AST (β = 3.04, p = 0.005) and Ct N gene as an independent predictor of direct bilirubin (β = -0.003, p = 0.025), supporting a dual-pathway model of COVID-19-associated cholestasis. Paradoxically, IgG seropositivity independently predicted higher direct bilirubin (β = 0.06, p = 0.030) but did not mark biliary normalisation. Elevated ALT and BILT at D0 were associated with detectable viral RNA beyond D14 (P = 0.03). Participants aged >30 years drove rising BILD, with significant increases at D14 (P = 0.03) and D30 (P = 0.04) versus D0. COVID-19 liver injury follows a biphasic course: D14 alterations are inflammation-driven (IL-6), while D30 abnormalities track with delayed viral RNA clearance independent of IgG seroconversion. Extended hepatic monitoring is warranted, especially in older patients with delayed viral clearance in resource-limited settings.
