title: Quantifizierung der humoralen Immunantwort auf einen MVA-basierten SARS-CoV-2-Impfstoff mittels Multiplex-Technologie
abstract: Im März 2020 erklärte die Weltgesundheitsorganisation COVID-19 offiziell zur Pande-mie. Aufgrund der rapide steigenden Erkrankungs- und Todesfälle entstand ein dringen-der Bedarf an Impfstoffen. Seitdem wurden zahlreiche Impfstoffe entwickelt, getestet und teilweise zugelassen. Dennoch bleibt angesichts des nachlassenden Impfschutzes und neuer besorgniserregender Varianten (VOC) weiterhin Bedarf an wirksamen Impfstoffen bestehen. Diese Arbeit berichtet über Daten zur humoralen Immunogenität aus zwei klinischen Phase-1-Studien, in denen zwei rekombinante Modified-Vaccinia-Virus-Ankara-(MVA)-Impfstoffkandidaten gegen COVID-19 untersucht wurden: MVA-SARS-2-S und MVA-SARS-2-ST, die jeweils das native bzw. das präfusionsstabilisierte SARS-CoV-2-Spike-Protein kodieren. Zur Analyse der humoralen Immunantwort wurde der MULTICOV-AB-Assay einge-setzt, ein auf Multiplex-Bead-basierter Durchflusszytometrie beruhender Immunoassay. Dieser ermöglicht die Detektion von IgG- und IgA-Antikörpern gegen die SARS-CoV-2-Antigene Spike-Trimer, RBD, S1 und S2 sowie gegen verschiedene RBD-Varianten (Alpha, Beta, Delta, Omikron BA.1, BA.2, BA.5). Nach Standardisierung mit dem WHO-Referenzstandard und dem Vergleich mit anderen Immunoassays erwies sich der MUL-TICOV-AB-Assay als geeignet für den Einsatz in klinischen Studien. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass MVA-SARS-2-ST mit dem präfusionsstabilisierten Spike-Protein vor allem RBD- und S1-spezifische IgG- und IgA-Immunantworten induzierte, während MVA-SARS-2-S mit dem nativen Spike-Protein eine stärkere IgG- und IgA-Immunantwort gegen das vollständige Spike-Trimer sowie die S2-Domäne hervorrief. Insgesamt war MVA-SARS-2-ST immunogener als MVA-SARS-2-S, jedoch zeigten beide Impfstoffe im Vergleich zu zugelassenen mRNA-Impfstoffen bei SARS-CoV-2-naiven Personen eine geringere Immunogenität. Die Immunantwort auf SARS-CoV-2-RBD-Varianten zeigte zudem, dass weder MVA-S noch MVA-ST einen erhöhten Schutz gegen stark mutierte Varianten wie Beta und Omikron im Vergleich zu mRNA-Impfstof-fen bieten konnten.

Dennoch bleibt angesichts des nachlassenden Impfschutzes und neuer besorgniserregender Varianten (VOC) weiterhin Bedarf an wirksamen Impfstoffen bestehen. Diese Arbeit berichtet über Daten zur humoralen Immunogenität aus zwei klinischen Phase-1-Studien, in denen zwei rekombinante Modified-Vaccinia-Virus-Ankara-(MVA)-Impfstoffkandidaten gegen COVID-19 untersucht wurden: MVA-SARS-2-S und MVA-SARS-2-ST, die jeweils das native bzw. das präfusionsstabilisierte SARS-CoV-2-Spike-Protein kodieren. Zur Analyse der humoralen Immunantwort wurde der MULTICOV-AB-Assay einge-setzt, ein auf Multiplex-Bead-basierter Durchflusszytometrie beruhender Immunoassay. Dieser ermöglicht die Detektion von IgG- und IgA-Antikörpern gegen die SARS-CoV-2-Antigene Spike-Trimer, RBD, S1 und S2 sowie gegen verschiedene RBD-Varianten (Alpha, Beta, Delta, Omikron BA.1, BA.2, BA.5). Nach Standardisierung mit dem WHO-Referenzstandard und dem Vergleich mit anderen Immunoassays erwies sich der MUL-TICOV-AB-Assay als geeignet für den Einsatz in klinischen Studien. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass MVA-SARS-2-ST mit dem präfusionsstabilisierten Spike-Protein vor allem RBD- und S1-spezifische IgG- und IgA-Immunantworten induzierte, während MVA-SARS-2-S mit dem nativen Spike-Protein eine stärkere IgG- und IgA-Immunantwort gegen das vollständige Spike-Trimer sowie die S2-Domäne hervorrief. Insgesamt war MVA-SARS-2-ST immunogener als MVA-SARS-2-S, jedoch zeigten beide Impfstoffe im Vergleich zu zugelassenen mRNA-Impfstoffen bei SARS-CoV-2-naiven Personen eine geringere Immunogenität. Die Immunantwort auf SARS-CoV-2-RBD-Varianten zeigte zudem, dass weder MVA-S noch MVA-ST einen erhöhten Schutz gegen stark mutierte Varianten wie Beta und Omikron im Vergleich zu mRNA-Impfstof-fen bieten konnten.

title: Models and theories investigating the interactions of SARS-CoV-2 infection with the blood-brain barrier
abstract: The neurological effects of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) remain largely unclear. With the ever-mounting concerns surrounding the neurological harm of SARS-CoV-2, it is important to elucidate these effects and how they transpire. Given that these symptoms include an altered mental status in some cases (including brain fog, headaches, sleep impairment, etc.), it is believed that SARS-CoV-2 must somehow access the central nervous system (CNS), whether by direct infection by virions or by indirect means (1, 2). There is often disagreement as to whether SARS-CoV-2 directly infects the blood-brain barrier (BBB) to gain entry to the CNS. Certain research groups speculate that SARS-CoV-2 harms the CNS indirectly. Studies have found that the viral S1 protein, cleaved off by host furin during entry of the virus into cells, has the ability to pass the BBB, and may be partially responsible for the neurological symptoms exhibited (3). Regardless of what theory is being investigated, to examine the interactions of SARS-CoV-2 on the BBB, an accurate model is necessary. The models and experiments examined in this paper suggest that SARS-CoV-2 BBB invasion is possible, but the mechanism by which this occurs is still uncertain. However, models such as these can be used to continue experimentation and eventually discover how SARS-CoV-2 gains access to the CNS.

title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids
abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

title: The Association Between the Vaccine Equity Initiative's Get Boosted Campaign and COVID-19 Vaccination in Massachusetts, 2022–2023
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether the Vaccine Equity Initiative's (VEI) Get Boosted (GB) financial incentive increased rates of COVID-19 vaccination. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study using an interrupted time series design. PARTICIPANTS: The Massachusetts Department of Public Health selected municipalities for participation in VEI based on elevated scores on the Social Vulnerability Index and high COVID-19 cases. Using baseline data, we matched the 43 vaccine sites within the VEI municipalities offering the GB incentive to comparison vaccine sites on vaccine capacity and service population. SETTING: We extracted COVID-19 vaccination data from a statewide registry spanning May 31, 2022-May 30, 2023. INTERVENTION: The GB campaign offered a $75 gift card for receiving the COVID-19 vaccine in select vaccine sites within the VEI municipalities between October 24, 2022 and March 26, 2023. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Our outcome was rates of COVID-19 vaccination per 100 000 population. We created a binary variable indicating the GB sites during the incentive period to examine whether the incentive was associated with statistically significantly higher rates of vaccination. We generated weekly conditional rates of COVID-19 vaccination per 100 000 population accompanied by 95% confidence intervals (CIs) to examine impact among subpopulations. Finally, we conducted sensitivity analyses to determine whether missing data, comparison site selection, or shifts in vaccine site traffic affected study conclusions. RESULTS: Comparison and GB sites had similar baseline socio-demographic characteristics and vaccination trends. The GB incentive period variable indicated that vaccination rates were statistically significantly higher during the GB campaign period at GB sites (IRR 2.29, 95% CI 2.12-2.48). In addition, COVID-19 vaccination rates at GB sites were statistically significantly higher than comparison sites during the campaign among all subpopulations. Sensitivity analyses agreed with our main findings. CONCLUSIONS: Moderately sized, guaranteed incentives can increase COVID-19 vaccination. Our findings can be leveraged by public health practitioners to increase vaccine uptake.
journal: Journal of Public Health Management and Practice

title: Reproducible smoker’s paradox in COVID-19 - comparative evidence from Swedish and Norwegian cohorts
abstract: Abstract Literature on the impact of smoking on COVID-19 has been inconsistent, and the association remains incompletely understood. To assess the effect of smoking on COVID-19 outcomes using different data sources. We analyzed two cohorts with detailed smoking information linked to COVID-19: a cohort defined from Swedish chronic disease registers (airway disease, heart failure, cardiac disease, and diabetes) and a general population cohort from Norway. Participants with smoking information from 2019 (registers) or 2017–2019 (general population) were included and classified as never, former or current smokers. Adjusted Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for COVID-19 outcomes from January 2020 to December 2022. The chronic disease register cohort included 506,745 individuals, and the general population cohort 155,333. Current smokers were the smallest group (13% and 11%), and never-smokers the largest (55% and 46%), in the two cohorts, respectively. Compared with never-smokers, current smokers had lower hazards of non-fatal COVID-19 events. For COVID-19 infection, HRs were 0.75 [CI: 0.73–0.77] in the chronic disease register cohort and for diagnosis 0.93 [0.91–0.96] in the general population cohort; for hospitalization, the HR was 0.88 [0.84–0.93] in the chronic disease register cohort. However, current smokers had higher hazards of COVID-19 death in both cohorts, although CIs included the null. Former smokers had clearly elevated hazards for most outcomes across both cohorts. While paradoxical inverse associations were observed for COVID-19 infection and hospitalization, current smokers consistently exhibited higher HR estimates for COVID-19 death across cohorts, although the confidence intervals were wide and included the null value.

title: Covid 19 Deneyimi ve Sağlık Sistemlerinde Dayanıklılık
abstract: COVID-19 pandemisi, dünya genelinde sağlık sistemleri üzerinde önemli baskılar oluşturmuş; sağlık hizmeti kapasitesi, insan gücü, bilgi sistemleri, tedarik zincirleri, finansman, hizmet sürekliliği ve koordinasyon gibi alanlarda çeşitli kırılganlıkları görünür hâle getirmiştir. Bu bölümün amacı, COVID-19 pandemisi bağlamında sağlık sistemi dayanıklılığı kavramını ele almak ve sağlık sistemlerinin krizlere hazırlık, yanıt verme, temel işlevlerini sürdürme, toparlanma ve değişen koşullara uyum sağlama kapasitesini değerlendirmektir. Bu kapsamda öncelikle COVID-19 pandemisinin küresel boyutu ve sağlık sistemi dayanıklılığı kavramı incelenmiş; pandemi sürecinde sağlık sistemlerinin karşılaştığı temel sorunlar ve dayanıklı sağlık sistemlerinde bulunması gereken özellikler ele alınmıştır. Ardından pandemi dönemlerinde hızlı yanıt stratejileri ve farklı ülke deneyimleri sağlık sistemi dayanıklılığı açısından değerlendirilmiş, Türkiye’nin COVID-19 pandemisindeki deneyimi; birinci basamak sağlık hizmetleri, filyasyon ve temaslı takibi, sürveyans ve bilgi sistemleri, dijital sağlık altyapısı, sağlık hizmeti kapasitesi, insan kaynakları, tedarik zincirleri, finansman ve merkezi koordinasyon boyutlarında incelenmiştir. Son bölümde ise iklim değişikliği ve diğer ortaya çıkabilecek sağlık tehditleri, sağlık sistemi dayanıklılığının gelecekteki sınamaları kapsamında ele alınmıştır. Bölümde yapılan değerlendirmeler, sağlık sistemi dayanıklılığının yalnızca fiziksel sağlık hizmeti kapasitesiyle açıklanamayacağını; hazırlık, bilgi yönetimi, insan gücü, koordinasyon, hizmet sürekliliği, uyum sağlama ve krizlerden öğrenme gibi birbiriyle ilişkili çok sayıda kapasitenin birlikte değerlendirilmesini gerektirdiğini göstermektedir. Bu doğrultuda, COVID-19 pandemisinden elde edilen deneyimlerin kurumsal öğrenmeye dönüştürülmesi ve sağlık sistemlerinin gelecekteki pandemiler, iklim kaynaklı olaylar ve diğer karmaşık sağlık tehditlerine karşı hazırlık ve uyum kapasitesinin sürekli olarak geliştirilmesi önem taşımaktadır.

Bu doğrultuda, COVID-19 pandemisinden elde edilen deneyimlerin kurumsal öğrenmeye dönüştürülmesi ve sağlık sistemlerinin gelecekteki pandemiler, iklim kaynaklı olaylar ve diğer karmaşık sağlık tehditlerine karşı hazırlık ve uyum kapasitesinin sürekli olarak geliştirilmesi önem taşımaktadır.

title: Comparative Evaluation of the Inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 and Human Coronavirus 229E against Sodium Hypochlorite
abstract: Introduction: Surface disinfection is one of the important non-pharmaceutical intervention measures that help prevent the spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Disinfectants with an efficacy claim against Human Coronavirus strain 229E (HCoV-229E) have been used for the disinfection of SARS-CoV-2; however, the comparative susceptibility of these two viruses to chemical disinfection has not been well defined. To address this, laboratory data were generated to compare the level of inactivation of human coronaviruses HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to a common antimicrobial agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), on a hard non-porous surface. Methods: A hard surface-based Quantitative Method (QM) was used to evaluate the viral inactivation efficacy by three treatments of NaOCl against HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2. For each treatment, viral inoculum containing soil load was applied onto a stainless steel carrier and dried. The inoculated carrier was exposed to NaOCl or a control fluid and held for five minutes. Following the exposure time, a neutralizer was added, and the sample was serially diluted and inoculated onto host cells to determine the number of infective units. The resulting Log10 of the density for control and treated carriers was used to generate Log10 reduction (LR) values for comparative statistical evaluation. Results: The mean LR ± standard error (SE) for HCoV-229E was 0.96 ± 0.09 (n=10) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 2.41 ± 0.15 (n=10) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.54 ± 0.13 (n=10) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. The mean LR ± SE for SARS-CoV-2 was 0.91 ± 0.24 (n=4) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 1.96 ± 0.26 (n=4) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.23 ± 0.16 (n=4) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. Both viruses were significantly responsive to the increasing concentrations of NaOCl. HCoV-229E had slightly higher mean LRs compared to SARS-CoV-2 at each NaOCl concentration; however, these differences were not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.067). Regression analysis using a linear mixed effects model (LMM) also indicates that the susceptibility of HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to NaOCl is comparable. Discussion: Understanding the antimicrobial tolerance of viruses can enhance public health response to viral infections. By determining the tolerance, the most appropriate antimicrobial agent can be chosen to disinfect surfaces contaminated with viral particles. Disinfection of highcontact surfaces can reduce the amount of fomite transmission and limit outbreaks. Conclusion: The data suggest that HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 are statistically comparable in their susceptibility to NaOCl treatments.

title: The Road Less Traveled: Advancing SARS-CoV-2 research with the exploration of non-structural proteins using organoid models
abstract: Until recently, the study of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) pathogenesis has primarily focused on surface structural proteins, with non-structural proteins (NSPs) regarded as less important. However, recent findings have shown the critical role of NSP6 in replication organelles, shedding light on these lesser-studied proteins. This paper proposes using organoids to explore NSP functions in SARS Cov-2. The study addresses two main questions: how can organoids be further applied to allow SARS-CoV-2 research advancement with NSPs, and what NSPs of SARS-CoV-2 need further exploration? A systems biology approach is suggested, involving the overexpression of NSPs in cells forming the organoid and analyses using transcription screening, proteomics, and microRNA profiling. Exploring all 16 NSPs using the proposed approach will provide a more robust understanding of SARS-CoV-2 mechanisms and could lead to the development of therapeutic agents. This research also has implications for "long COVID" research, in which various organoids can be used to model changes in different affected organs. Furthermore, it has implications for developing nanoparticles targeting viral or host chaperone proteins. By implementing the proposed approaches, we can move closer to understanding SARS Cov-2 mechanisms and developing a therapeutic that can be used against the virus.

title: Six-Month Trajectories of Symptoms, Perceived Recovery, and Functional Health in Ecuadorian Adults with COVID-19
abstract: Background/Objectives: Most longitudinal evidence on post-acute COVID-19 comes from hospitalized patients in high-income countries and less is known about community samples in low- and middle-income settings. This study examined changes in perceived recovery, symptom burden, general health perception, and functional difficulties over six months in Ecuadorian adults with confirmed COVID-19. Methods: In a prospective observational cohort in Quito, Ecuador, 120 adults with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 were assessed at baseline (within four weeks of diagnosis) and again three and six months after the baseline assessment; 91 completed all three assessments. The Spanish-language ISARIC follow-up survey covered 39 symptoms, perceived recovery, the EQ-5D-5L and EQ-VAS, and six Washington Group functioning items rated retrospectively for the pre-COVID period and currently. Analyses were exploratory and descriptive, and all p-values are nominal and unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Results: Participants’ perceived complete recovery improved (χ2 = 15.24, p < 0.001), as did perceived general health (F(2, 178) = 5.80, p = 0.004). Chest pain, palpitations, muscle weakness, confusion, tinnitus, and diarrhea declined over follow-up. At six months, 37.4% still reported headaches, 35.2% fatigue, 35.2% confusion or inattention, and 25.3% sleep disturbance. Among EQ-5D-5L domains, only pain/discomfort improved (p = 0.012). Vision, walking, memory, and communication declined from pre-COVID to baseline and improved between baseline and six months; pre-COVID and six-month levels were not compared directly. Conclusions: Recovery over six months was gradual but incomplete, with a substantial minority reporting ongoing or recurrent symptoms at six months. These findings describe post-acute symptom burden following confirmed COVID-19 rather than formally diagnosed post-COVID-19 condition.

title: SARS-CoV-2 lysosomal egress pathway
abstract: The early stages of the SARS-CoV-2 lifecycle have been relatively well-defined. However, knowledge of how newly assembled SARS-CoV-2 particles egress from cells remains limited. Until recently, SARS-CoV-2 egress was misunderstood as being dependent on the biosynthetic secretory pathway commonly used by enveloped viruses. Recent findings have demonstrated that SARS-CoV-2 instead utilizes an unconventional lysosomal egress pathway. This pathway has been characterized as being dependent on the Arl8b GTPase for anterograde movement of the lysosome along microtubules to the plasma membrane. Viral hijacking of the lysosomal pathway leads to lysosome deacidification and deactivation of lysosomal hydrolases, which perturbs antigen presentation. However, many questions regarding the molecular details of this lysosome-mediated egress remain unanswered. This article will highlight the current knowledge gaps in the lysosomal-egress pathway, focusing on 1) how newly assembled SARS- CoV-2 particles are trafficked to lysosomes, 2) the mechanisms by which lysosome deacidification occurs, and 3) the reasons why deacidification of lysosomes is essential for successful egress. Through its disruption of lysosome function and perturbation of antigen presentation, the lysosomal egress pathway has implications for the clinical presentation of COVID-19. Furthermore, understanding the molecular details of the pathway presents an opportunity to develop novel therapeutic targets. Therefore, further investigation of the viral and host factors involved in this egress pathway is essential in understanding SARS-CoV-2 as a whole.

title: Incomplete assessments: Including harms and trade-offs in assessing policy approaches to Covid-19
abstract: Policies to combat COVID-19 were often implemented without a systematic assessment of trade-offs with other public objectives. This approach implicitly assumed that these policies would do little harm to other aspects of public health. Recently published evaluations of pandemic-era policies have also largely avoided cost-benefit (or harm-benefit) analysis in public health decision-making. This is likely due to a narrow framing of their analyses to the possibility of underreaction to the pandemic. We argue that a disproportionate policy response framework can offer a valuable toolkit to understand the policy choices to combat the pandemic. This article first reviews The Lancet COVID-19 Commission and The BMJ COVID-19 series evaluating policies implemented during the pandemic in Canada, the United States, and the United Kingdom. We suggest that these documents, likely motivated by concern with underreacting to the pandemic, fall short in evaluating the trade-offs between the harms and benefits of COVID-19 policies to ensure that they are of net benefit to the public. We further argue that the failure to address these trade-offs contributed to an erosion in public trust in health authorities and the unequal impacts of the global COVID-19 response, especially among low-income countries.

title: Depression, Anxiety, and Stress in a Primary Care Population in Northern Portugal: A Cross-Sectional Study in the Post-COVID-19 Context
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic has had lasting psychological consequences, with primary care playing a key role in identifying emotional distress. Objective: Our objective was to characterize levels of depression, anxiety, and stress in a primary care population in the post-pandemic context and to examine their associations with sociodemographic and COVID-19-related variables. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 adult users of a Family Health Unit. Participants completed a sociodemographic questionnaire and the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-21). Group differences were assessed using Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests, and multivariable generalized linear models (negative binomial regression for symptom scores and logistic regression for perceived impact) were used to identify factors independently associated with each outcome. Results: Most participants fell within normal symptom ranges (66.9% depression; 65.0% anxiety; 74.6% stress), although approximately one-third presented at least moderate levels of depressive or anxiety symptoms. In unadjusted analyses, women, older adults and professionally inactive individuals had significantly higher levels of psychological distress. Self-reported COVID-19 infection history was not associated with DASS-21 scores. In contrast, participants reporting a negative psychological impact from the pandemic and poorer self-rated mental health had significantly higher depression, anxiety, and stress scores. Conclusions: In this primary care sample, self-reported psychological impact from the pandemic and self-rated mental health were more strongly associated with psychological distress than self-reported COVID-19 infection history. Multivariable analyses identified independent associations between psychotropic medication use, self-rated health, and DASS-21 scores and the outcomes examined. These findings indicate associations between these variables within the cross-sectional sample; however, their temporal or causal relationships cannot be established.

title: The mediating role of social distance on the association between audience-protagonist similarity and fear: a case of fear of COVID-19
abstract: Objective This study examined the effects of news content on fear of COVID-19 by examining perceived social distance and audience-protagonist similarity. Method Participants ( N = 78) read a fictitious news story about a COVID-19 patient (similar/dissimilar protagonist) and then rated social distance regarding this protagonist and their fear of COVID-19. Results The results showed that participants exposed to a similar protagonist reported significantly lower perceived social distance, and that social distance was moderately negatively correlated with fear of COVID-19. Social distance mediated the association between audience-protagonist similarity and fear of COVID-19. Conclusion These findings provide insights into how exposure to health-related news content can impact fear of disease.

title: It’s All Just A Lie. I Know It!COVID-19 Conspiracy Beliefs and COVID-19 Anxiety Versus the War in Ukraine: The Role of Dogmatism
abstract: Abstract Our study investigated the relationship between Romanian adults' COVID-19 and the Ukrainian war conspiracy beliefs, COVID-19 anxiety, and dogmatism. The sample comprised 227 Romanian adults aged 18 to 57 ( M = 24.21, SD = 8.82), residents of the northeastern part of the country, located near the Ukrainian border. Participants completed self-reported measures of COVID-19 anxiety, COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs, dogmatism, and Ukrainian war-related conspiracy beliefs. Correlation analysis suggested that dogmatism was not significantly related to COVID-19 anxiety, COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs, and conspiracy beliefs about war. However, COVID-19 anxiety was positively associated with conspiracy beliefs about war. Also, COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs were positively associated with conspiracy beliefs about the war in Ukraine. Furthermore, the results suggested that COVID-19 anxiety did not moderate the relationship between dogmatism and conspiracy beliefs about the war. We discuss the current findings regarding their possible contribution to addressing the harmful effects of conspiracy beliefs on one’s social, political, and psychological environment.

Correlation analysis suggested that dogmatism was not significantly related to COVID-19 anxiety, COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs, and conspiracy beliefs about war. title: PROFIL PERILAKU PENGGUNAAN MASKER PENGUNJUNG PUSKESMAS PADEMAWU DI ERA PANDEMI COVID-19
abstract: This study aimed to analyze factors associated with mask-wearing behavior among visitors of Pademawu Health Center during the COVID-19 pandemic. An analytical observational cross-sectional design was used. Data were collected through questionnaires and interviews among patients visiting GOPC, MCH, and emergency units from 3–9 August 2020 using total sampling. Of 169 respondents, 145 met inclusion and exclusion criteria. Independent variables included age, knowledge, education, income, and attitude; the dependent variable was mask-wearing compliance. Chi-square and odds ratio analyses were performed. Results showed 94 respondents (65%) were non-compliant and 51 (35%) compliant. Compliance was significantly associated with knowledge (p=0.022; OR=2.43), education (p=0.001), income (p=0.021; OR=5.3), and attitude (p<0.001; OR=4.75). Age was not associated (p=0.449). Discussion indicates that knowledge, attitude, education, and income are determinants of COVID-19 preventive behavior. This study provides important insights for local public health interventions. The novelty lies in profiling mask compliance among health-center visitors in rural Madura. Implications suggest strengthening health education and health-protocol promotion, especially for groups with low knowledge, negative attitudes, and lower income. Keywords: COVID-19, mask, compliance, knowledge, attitude.

title: Charting stigma’s impact on mental health among college students during COVID-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic catalyzed widespread disruption in higher education, contributing to a marked increase in mental health challenges among college students. This comprehensive narrative review uses the biopsychosocial perspective to examine the complex relationship between COVID-19-related stigma and mental health of this vulnerable population. The literature suggests that stigma during the pandemic was an important contributor to and an exacerbating factor in mental health challenges among college students. The various dimensions of stigma including enacted (discrimination, social exclusion), internalized (shame, self-blame), perceived (fear of judgment), anticipated (reluctance to disclose), and associated forms potentially compound pre-existing psychosocial stressors, directly initiating or worsening feelings of loneliness, anxiety, and depression. Furthermore, stigma’s operation at sociocultural (institutional policies), interpersonal (peer avoidance), and individual levels could have undermined students’ resilience and created barriers to academic and social reintegration, thus hindering recovery and sustaining poor mental health throughout the crisis. The findings underscore the need for stigma-reduction initiatives and targeted mental health interventions within higher education settings during public health crises.

title: Caring for the greater good during crisis: worsening of the COVID-19 is associated with increased valuation for social welfare
abstract: This project examined how prosocial decision-making changed during the COVID-19 crisis. Using a prosocial decision-making task and computational modeling, we tracked self- versus other-benefiting choices biweekly over 10 weeks in the United States (April–June 2020), and examined whether choices were associated with local COVID-19 case levels or week-to-week increases. We also tested the pattern in an independent sample one year later. Prosocial choices increased following larger week-to-week increases in local cases, primarily reflecting a stronger preference for social welfare over self-interest. This pattern did not replicate in 2021, when case fluctuations had decreased. This is a post-study registration of a completed project. It archives the raw data, task and survey materials, data-processing and analysis code, and instruction files.

title: Impact of COVID ‐19 Restrictions on Estimating Causal Effects: Fluoroquinolones and Tendon Rupture
abstract: PURPOSE: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare services, potentially affecting causal effect estimation using real-world data. As a case study, we replicated a cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum to evaluate whether pandemic-related disruptions influenced the measured association between fluoroquinolone use and tendon rupture. METHODS: We included adults initiating fluoroquinolones/cephalosporins during 1 January 2006-31 March 2023. Four analyses compared treatment effect estimates using different periods for exposure and outcome ascertainment: pre-pandemic only, pre-pandemic exposure with follow-up extending through the pandemic, all available data and post-pandemic only. We estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for tendon rupture using Cox regression. RESULTS: Among 891 968 fluoroquinolone users and 895 229 cephalosporin users, fluoroquinolone users had more comorbidities than cephalosporin users in the pre-pandemic period but fewer in the post-pandemic period. Pre-pandemic analysis showed an increased risk of tendon rupture associated with fluoroquinolones (Propensity score weighted [PSW]-HR: 1.94; 95% CI: 1.46-2.59), consistent with previous evidence. Estimates using all available data were similar for the overall study period (PSW-HR: 1.91; 95% CI: 1.46-2.51) and the pre-pandemic period (PSW-HR: 1.96; 95% CI: 1.47-2.61) but were less precise during/post-pandemic period (PSW-HR: 1.57; 95% CI: 0.72-3.41) with no evidence of a period-treatment interaction (PSW-HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.35-1.84). Post-pandemic analysis showed very few events among cephalosporin users but not fluoroquinolone users with a larger but imprecise estimate (PSW-HR: 3.32; 95% CI: 0.62-17.72). CONCLUSION: In this case study, there was no clear evidence that pandemic-related healthcare disruptions materially altered causal estimates, albeit with limited power to detect differences between before and during/post-pandemic effects. Studies using real-world data across the pandemic should routinely examine temporal changes in baseline characteristics and outcome incidence.

title: COVID-19 PANDEMIYASI VA YANGI SINOVLAR (2020-2021) DAVRIDA GERMANIYA GERMANY DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC AND NEW CHALLENGES (2020–2021)
abstract: Tadqiqotda COVID-19 ning Germaniya iqtisodiyoti, bandlik bozori va ijtimoiy hayotiga ta’siri masalasini tadqiq etilgan. Davlat biznesni qoʻllab-quvvatlash boʻyicha keng koʻlamli dasturni ishlab chiqdi va amalga oshirishni boshladi. Ushbu maqolada koronavirusning Germaniya iqtisodiyotiga ta’siri, hukumatning biznesni qoʻllab-quvvatlash mexanizmlari va ularning samaradorligi tahlil qilinadi. Muallif Germaniyaning 2020-2021-yillardagi iqtisodiy va ijtimoiy rivojlanishini baholaydi.

title: Orthogonal Fc engineering enables multiplexed delivery of mRNA-encoded bispecific antibodies that constrain viral escape
abstract: The continuous antigenic evolution of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has repeatedly undermined the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies, underscoring the need for innovative approaches that improve therapeutic mAb breadth and durability of protection. Here, we engineered messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)-encoded bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) that, upon intravenous administration in lipid nanoparticles, achieved high serum concentrations, extended half-life, and serum neutralizing titers exceeding 1:10,000 in human neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)-expressing mice. To enhance resilience to viral escape, we used structure-guided computational design to introduce Fc modifications that promoted selective homodimerization, thereby enabling codelivery of multiple mRNA-encoded bsAbs with cognate heavy chain pairing. In vivo expression of a triple bsAb combination resulted in broad serum neutralization of historical and contemporary SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the highly mutated BA.3.2.2 lineage. Preexposure prophylaxis with the mRNA-delivered bsAb combination conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 challenge, preventing weight loss and decreasing viral burden in the lungs compared with vehicle control treatment. Together, the results provide proof of principle for mRNA-based delivery of Fc-engineered bsAb combinations to combat SARS-CoV-2 and potentially other rapidly evolving pathogens.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartmentalization including immune-specific clusters across DAD patterns. Importantly, spatially informed ligand-receptor interaction analysis revealed intercellular communication signatures defining COVID-19 induced DAD. Transcription factor activity enrichment analysis identified the TGF-β pathway as DAD driver, highlighting the antagonizing roles of SMAD3 and SMAD7 activity during fibrosis. Integration of these data yielded a signaling kinase pathway in peribronchial fibroblasts with amenable novel targets. Finally, spatio-temporal trajectory analysis characterized an alveolar epithelium regeneration program. Here, Garcia-Prieto et al use spatial transcriptomics to reveal progressive endothelial, pneumocyte type I and natural killer cell loss, expansion of myeloid and stromal cells, TGF-β-driven fibrosis signaling and alveolar regeneration programs in fatal COVID-19 lung injury.

Similar content being viewed by others Introduction Infection by the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) virus caused a worldwide pandemic of the derived coronavirus disease 2019, COVID-19. Beyond 775 million confirmed cases and more than 7 million deaths have been reported (https://data.who.int/dashboards/covid19/). Although most affected individuals exhibit mild clinical manifestations or are asymptomatic, respiratory failure linked to lung damage and acute respiratory distress syndrome could occur, being the most common cause of death1,2. Importantly, the maintenance of lung lesions in a subgroup of COVID-19 patients could also be associated with prolonged clinical manifestations3,4. Upon SARS-CoV-2 infection in the severe cases, the pathological change is defined by diffuse alveolar damage (DAD)5 that initiates with an acute stage of early intra-alveolar epithelial lesions, interstitial inflammation and edema, followed by the proliferative stage with a final appearance of pneumocyte hyperplasia and fibroblast proliferation1,2. The molecular context of lung damage provoked by SARS-CoV-2 infection is not fully established. Most studies have addressed the bulk transcription landscape6,7,8 or a particular lineage such as immune cells9,10. A more granulated view of the lung affected by severe COVID-19 has been gained by single-cell gene expression profiles11,12,13. However, all these approaches destroy the anatomical structure of the lung and the spatial cell-cell interactions. Only a limited number of studies have analyzed a spatial component in the lung of COVID-19 cases, using high-parameter imaging mass cytometry for targeted proteins14 or focusing on regions of interest (ROI)15,16,17,18. Importantly, larger pathological scrutiny of spatial transcriptomics in COVID-19 patients has only been performed recently19. To overcome these issues, we leveraged the recently developed Visium spatial transcriptomics (VisiumST) technology in a cohort of lungs with normal histology and those that underwent DAD during the course of fatal COVID-19. Using the single-cell RNA expression data of a human cell atlas of the lung to annotate cell types13, we provide the constellation of shifts in forty-five cell types, the perturbations in cell-to-cell communications and the spatial alterations of molecular pathways that occur upon severe COVID-19. Results Identification of lung cell types and cellular compartments in COVID-19 associated DAD histological patterns To assess how fatal COVID-19 affected cell type composition, cell-cell communication, and global expression patterns across acute and proliferative DAD, we followed the study design shown in Fig. 1A. We first retrieved twenty-three formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded post-mortem lung tissue samples obtained from nineteen patients with DAD, corresponding to seven cases of acute DAD and twelve proliferative DAD, and four lung samples from control lungs with normal morphological appearance without SARS-CoV-2 infection (Table 1). We then analyzed the spatial transcriptomics patterns using tissue spots on a microarray slide with arrayed oligonucleotides to capture spatial gene expression information following the final generation of next generation sequencing (NGS) libraries20, adapted by 10× Genomics as “10× Visium” (VisiumST) (“Methods”). In total, 91,068 tissue spots were studied after quality control (QC) and preprocessing (“Methods”). To assess the spatial organization of cell types across tissue slides, we used the integrated Human Lung Cell Atlas (HLCA)13 as a reference to deconvolute the main cell types present in each spot by applying the validated cell2location pipeline21. Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) using the integrated global spatial transcriptome data showing the spots colored by our three groups of lung samples (control, acute DAD, and proliferative DAD) distinguished these three entities (Fig. 1B). Illustrative examples are shown in Fig. 1B. Using cell2location, we annotated forty-five cell types in HLCA defined by derived markers (“Methods”) in our lung samples (Fig. S1). A UMAP visualization of these cell populations according to their lineage (epithelial, stroma, immune and endothelial) in the spatial transcriptomics spots for all the integrated samples and illustrative examples are shown in Fig. 1B. Spots from different donors were well intermixed within each DAD pattern in the same embedding, indicating limited donor-driven batch effects across the integrated dataset (Fig. S2). The mapping of the identified cell types on top of the VisiumST brightfield images stained with Hematoxylin and Eosin (HE) for the described lineages in illustrative control, acute and proliferative DAD cases are shown in Fig. 1C. Cell types mapped to their expected locations, matching well-described structures, with epithelial cells lining the airway lumen and stromal cells mapping to blood vessel walls, as validated by endothelial (CD34) and epithelial (CK7) markers immunostaining (Fig. 1C). Overall, we observed that in control lungs the most abundant lineage corresponded to endothelial cell types, as previously described22, and that acute DAD was characterized by a relative decrease in endothelial cell proportions, despite endothelial cells remaining the predominant lineage, together with increased immune and stromal cell proportions, whereas proliferative DAD was mostly defined by the large proportion of fibrotic tissue, as previously described1,2 (Fig. 1D). While changes were observed across histological patterns, only the reduction of endothelial cells in proliferative DAD compared to controls exhibited a significant credible shift (false discovery rate <0.05) based on compositional data analysis (“Methods”). These findings were validated using HE-stained sections and specific immunohistochemistry (IHC) markers such as CD34 (endothelial), CD68 (myeloid lineage) and CK7 (epithelial markers) and trichrome staining (fibroblasts) (Fig. 1E). We then moved to characterize a possible uneven distribution of the identified 45 cell types according to their abundance in the control, acute and proliferative DAD lung groups (Fig. 2A, B). We observed highly consistent cell type abundance profiles across individual samples within each DAD pattern (Fig. S2), justifying grouped comparisons. To ease interpretation, we ordered these cell populations according to their lineage (epithelial, stromal, immune, and endothelial) (Fig. 2A). Among the epithelial lineage (10 identified cell types), the most important difference was observed in alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells, comprising between 5% and 10% of total cells in normal lungs as previously reported23, that were significantly downregulated in COVID-19 associated proliferative DAD cases in comparison to controls and acute DAD lungs (Fig. 2A, B). The reverse process was observed in alveolar type 2 (AT2) cells that were upregulated in proliferative cases in comparison to acute DAD and control samples (Fig. 2A, B). These results fit with the concept that AT1s are the main cell type responsible for the provision of the interface for the blood-gas exchange (a function that is compromised in COVID-19 patients), whereas AT2 cells function as progenitors that repair the injured alveolar epithelium24. Regarding the endothelial lineage (7 identified cell types), we observed that capillary cell types were the most abundant of lung cells (~30% of total cells), as previously reported22,23, and that the studied lung samples underwent a progressive loss from normal lung to acute DAD to proliferative DAD for the abundance of endothelial cells (EC) aerocyte capillary, arterial, general capillary and venous pulmonary (Fig. 2A, B). These results support the evidence linking SARS-CoV-2 infection to endothelial dysfunction25. For the immune lineage (19 identified cell populations), we observed in the myeloid lineage that alveolar macrophages (Mph), CCL3+ and monocyte-derived Mph were significantly overrepresented in COVID-19-associated proliferative DAD cases in comparison to controls and acute DAD lungs (Fig. 2A, B). Interstitial Mph perivascular showed a progressive increase. In the lymphoid lineage, a decrease in CD4 and CD8 T-cells was observed in proliferative COVID-19 patients in comparison to the control group (Fig. 2A, B). Interestingly, Natural Killer (NK) cells experienced a significant decrease from control and acute DAD samples to proliferative DAD cases (Fig. 2A, B). In this regard, these innate effector lymphocytes that respond to acute viral infections have been previously related to COVID-19 severity26. Additionally, both alveolar macrophages and plasma cells were overrepresented in proliferative DAD lungs compared to control samples. Finally, regarding the stromal lineage (9 cell types), the most dramatic change was observed for peribronchial fibroblasts (PBFs) that increased from control to acute DAD, skyrocketing in proliferative DAD cases (Fig. 2A, B). Not all fibroblast subtypes behaved in a similar manner. Subpleural fibroblasts were overrepresented in COVID-19-associated DAD fatal cases compared to the control group and between acute and proliferative DAD, whereas alveolar fibroblasts and pericytes decreased in the proliferative DAD samples compared to control and acute DAD lungs. Lastly, adventitial fibroblasts were overrepresented in proliferative DAD samples compared to controls. UMAPs for the entire set of cases in the cellular populations of AT1, AT2, EC aerocyte capillary, PBFs, monocyte-derived Mphs and smooth muscle activated stress response cells are displayed in Fig. 2B, showing the unbalanced distribution (Fig. 2A, B). Mapping of the identified cell types on top of the VisiumST brightfield images is shown in Fig. 2B. Cell types annotated with the finest granularity level are mapped to their expected locations, including subpleural fibroblasts located next to the pleura, and multiciliated cells lining small airway lumens and smooth muscle cells mapping to blood vessel walls (Fig. 2B). To assess the spatial distribution of the identified forty-five cell types within neighboring compartments, we applied the cell2location algorithm to the VisiumST data. To investigate spatial patterns of co-localization among these cell types, we performed non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) on cell type abundance estimates (“Methods”). This unsupervised dimensionality reduction technique enabled us to uncover recurrent modules of co-occurring cell types by identifying eight distinct NMF components, or factors, that captured the underlying cellular neighborhood structure, referred to as spatial compartments, across the tissue. For normal lung, the characterized cell types mapped within physiological cellular microenvironments such as the great compartment defined by immune and endothelial cells, one rich in epithelial cells (excluding AT2 proliferating, suprabasal and deuterosomal cells that shared a common location), another related to smooth muscle related cells and the fibroblast lineage (where PBFs resided in an isolated compartment) (Fig. 2C). This compartmentalization underwent an abrupt shift across DAD histological patterns. The acute DAD was characterized by a recruitment of an enriched AT2 proliferating population to the epithelial compartment; the irruption of a spatial cluster of macrophage subtypes and type-2 dendritic cells (DC2s, that promote cytotoxic T-cell responses and helper T-cell differentiation); and the appearance of plasma cells in an isolated population (Fig. 2C). Most of these cellular redistributions underwent further compartmentalization in the proliferative DAD pattern that additionally exhibited the emergence of a unique compartment for lymphatic mature endothelial cells (Fig. 2C). To further analyze and characterize tissue architecture differences, we applied GraphCompass (Graph Comparison Tools for Differential Analyses in Spatial Systems)27 (“Methods”), a set of graph-analysis methods for “omics” data to quantitatively determine and compare spatial arrangement of distinct cell types among different biological conditions successfully applied to VisiumST data27. The cell-type-specific subgraphs across condition pairs, where the size of the dot indicates the pairwise similarity score variances (“Methods”), are shown in Fig. 2D. This analysis quantified how the spatial arrangement of each cell type changed across DAD patterns. Cell types such as PBFs, alveolar fibroblasts, AT2 cells, EC aerocyte capillary cells, and monocyte-derived Mphs exhibited high variance in spatial similarity scores, indicating pronounced remodeling of their spatial architecture, especially during proliferative DAD (Fig. 2D). Among the distinct cell types identified across COVID-19 samples, we further examined PBFs, EC aerocyte capillary cells, and AT2 cells to quantify how their spatial organization changed across conditions. Using filtration curves27, we evaluated how spatially connected spots containing each cell type were, based on increasing distance thresholds (“Methods”). These curves reflect the growth of the largest connected cluster per sample, with right-shifted curves indicating tighter spatial clustering and left-shifted curves suggesting more dispersed distributions. In proliferative DAD, PBFs and AT2 cells exhibited stronger spatial clustering, while capillary endothelial cells showed more fragmented, dispersed patterns, consistent with their depletion across acute and proliferative DAD (Fig. 2E). These analyses reinforced the findings that these cell types underwent antiparallel shifts in their abundance: PBFs and AT2 cells exhibited an overrepresentation whereas endothelial aerocyte capillary cells were depleted, particularly at proliferative DAD (Fig. 2E). Spatial cell-cell interactions in COVID-19-associated DAD One of the most exciting applications of spatial transcriptomics is the potential to analyze cell-cell communication (CCC). CCC is a multicellular and complex process involving multiple mechanisms, including intercellular signaling and intracellular signaling as a downstream response. Related to the intercellular component, cells interact on diverse levels that include direct contact, such as between ligands and surface receptors, and through indirect means, such as the release of soluble factors. For single-cell analyses, the molecular profiles of sender and receiver cell types allow the inference of underlying cell communication events in a tissue using co-occurrence of ligand and receptor (LR) expression among the candidate communicating cells28,29 and through gene expression profiles in the receiving cell type related to the extracellular interaction28,29. Herein, we used the VisiumST data to identify coordinated cell-cell communication signatures shared across all tissue slides by applying NMF to the estimated local (spot level) ligand-receptor interactions (LRIs), calculated using spatially-weighted Cosine similarity with LIANA+30,31 (“Methods”). Using the elbow selection procedure, we decomposed the local interactions into three Factors (1, 2 and 3) representing three different intercellular communication signatures. The NMF factor scores indicate the strength of each factor in each spot, representing the degree of influence by the associated signature. The averaged factor scores per tissue slide clustered according to lung status are shown in Fig. 3A. Importantly, Factor 3 distinguished the best between control and COVID-19-associated DAD lung tissues, with high mean scores in proliferative DAD (Fig. 3A). Factor 1 was most prominent in control samples, whereas Factor 2 was more active in a subset of proliferative DAD. To provide further biological insight, we performed LRIs pathway enrichment analysis on the distinct interaction loadings contributing to the three factors (Fig. 3B) using multivariate linear regression32 and pathway annotations from PROGENy33 (“Methods”). We found that DAD-associated Factor 3 was significantly enriched in interactions related to the transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β) pathway (Fig. 3B), a driver of fibrosis involved in response to tissue injury34. Conversely, DAD-associated Factor 3 was depleted for the EGFR pathway (Fig. 3B). Interestingly, the wingless-related integration site (WNT) pathway was enriched in Factor 1 (characteristic of the control samples) but depleted in Factor 2 (Fig. 3B). Since Factor 3 was the most optimal discriminator between healthy and COVID-19-associated DAD, we mainly focused our analyses in this CCC readout. title: CONTESTATION OF BIOMEDICAL INFORMATION ON COVID-19 IN ALEGO-USONGA
abstract: Purpose of the study: The study examined community contestation of biomedical information and COVID-19 containment measures in Alego-Usonga, Kenya. Statement of the problem: Although containment measures were introduced to reduce viral transmission, their implementation encountered resistance shaped by local social, cultural, and economic circumstances. Understanding these responses is important for strengthening public trust in future health emergencies. Research methodology: The study adopted an ethnographic research design involving 35 purposively selected community members, key informant interviews, and focus group discussions. Data were documented through audio recordings, video recordings, and field notes and examined using thematic and discourse analysis. Findings: Community members contested curfews, mask requirements, social distancing, hygiene protocols, vaccination campaigns, transport capacity limits, school closures, and restrictions on gatherings. The reported concerns included perceived infringements of civil liberties, livelihood disruption, weakened social relationships, cultural dissonance, misinformation, and distrust of public authorities. Resistance to vaccination also reflected uncertainty about vaccine safety and inconsistent messaging. Conclusion: The study concludes that contestation reflected the interaction between biomedical interventions and community interpretations of their social consequences. Public health measures were more difficult to accept when they were perceived to disregard livelihoods, rights, and established social practices. Recommendations: The study recommends that policymakers should design culturally responsive risk-communication strategies and engage communities early in emergency planning. Health authorities should communicate consistently, address misinformation, and explain the rationale for interventions. Future responses should balance disease control with civil liberties, economic security, and community resilience. Keywords: Sociocultural barriers, contestation, COVID-19, containment measures, risk communication

title: Riesgos laborales en profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19: revisión sistemática Occupational risks among oral health professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre los riesgos laborales de los profesionales de la salud bucal durante la pandemia de COVID-19 y las medidas propuestas para controlarlos. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, ensayos clínicos, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: el riesgo biológico por aerosoles, gotas y contacto estrecho fue el principal riesgo descrito, seguido de las exposiciones a sangre y punzocortantes y del riesgo psicosocial, con agotamiento profesional y percepción elevada de riesgo. Las medidas incluyeron triaje, equipos de protección, control de aerosoles y colutorios previos al procedimiento. Conclusión: la pandemia aumentó y diversificó los riesgos laborales en odontología, por lo que se requieren protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y de protección de la salud mental.

title: In silico design of a novel hybrid compound derived from limonoids of Azadirachta indica as an inhibitor of the main protease of SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), has resulted in over 776 million cases and >7 million deaths worldwide since the beginning of the pandemic until September 2024. The main protease (M pro ) of this virus is regarded as a promising target for the development of new therapies. In this sense, the study aimed to explore the biocompounds derived from Azadirachta indica , particularly limonoids, as possible inhibitors of M pro . First, bioactive compounds were selected for their antiviral activity based on a literature review. In pharmacophore modeling, a hybrid model (Limotest) was developed using three limonoids. Pharmacokinetic and toxicological parameters were predicted using the ADMETLab 3.0 and ProTox 3.0 platforms. According to the in silico data, Limotest possesses favorable characteristics for drug development. Molecular docking calculations suggested that Limotest binds spontaneously to both the catalytic and allosteric sites of M pro , exhibiting competitive binding energy. The binding of the compounds involves hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and hydrophobic interactions, with evidence pointing to their potential for competitive inhibition. The results suggested that Limotest is a potential inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 M pro and should be considered for future synthesis and cell-based validations.

title: Pathological anatomy of the lungs in patients with humoral immunity to the SARS-CoV-2 virus
abstract: Since the COVID-19 pandemic, numerous articles have appeared on clinical changes in organs and systems in individuals with humoral immunity to the SARS-CoV-2 virus. However, there is a lack of data on a comprehensive clinical and morphological study of a group of patients with acquired immunity. OBJECTIVE: To compare lung pathology with humoral immunity data to the SARS-CoV-2 virus in patients who died from a new coronavirus infection with elevated serum Ig class G and M levels and negative PCR. MATERIAL AND METHODS: An analysis of clinical, laboratory, and pathomorphological changes was conducted in 33 autopsy observations of patients who died during the first half of 2021 in the specialized non-infectious departments of the City Clinical Hospital No. 31 named after Academician G.M. Savelyeva with an elevated content of serum Ig class G and M in the blood. RESULTS: Despite the negative PCR, elevated concentrations of Ig to SARS-CoV-2 proteins were detected in the blood of patients: IgG 0.31 - 532.56 OCE (Me 109.33 OCE), IgM 0.14 - 16.8 U / ml (Me 0.62 IU / ml). At an IgG concentration of 0.31-109.33 OCE in the lungs, an exudative phase of diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) was described, in the IgG range of 122.57-158.72 OCE, exudative-proliferative DAD was described, at IgG values 207.2-532.56 OCE, the proliferative phase of DAD occurred. CONCLUSION: The study revealed a sequence of pathological changes in the lungs, depending on the serum IgG concentration, characteristic of DAP. The findings confirm the multifaceted nature of the novel coronavirus infection.

title: Workforce Adaptation and Labor Market Reforms in Post-COVID-19 Southeastern Vietnam
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted employment, industrial production, worker mobility, and livelihoods in Southeastern Vietnam, the country’s major industrial and service-producing region. This study examines the relationship between labour-market disruption, workforce adaptation, and government policy responses, using descriptive and comparative analysis of published labour statistics, official resolutions, and relevant scholarly research, primarily for 2020–2022. It distinguishes employment and income losses from labour-force participation, enterprise-reported shortages, and longer-term recruitment difficulties. Official data for the third quarter of 2021 indicate that 59.1% of workers in the Southeast experienced adverse employment effects, the labour-force participation rate declined to 62.8%, and 30.6% of surveyed enterprises reported worker shortages. Sectoral shortages were particularly pronounced in electronics-related manufacturing, leather-related production, apparel, and other industrial activities. title: Comparing two case definitions for including severe acute respiratory infection patients in influenza and COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness studies among older adults using the test-negative design: VEBIS hospital network, seven European countries, 2023/24.
abstract: INTRODUCTION Two severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) case definitions (CDs) are often used in test-negative design (TND) hospital-based vaccine effectiveness (VE) studies. SARI-CD1 requires ≥1 symptom (cough, fever, shortness of breath, anosmia, ageusia, or dysgeusia); SARI-CD2 requires both fever and cough. Using VEBIS hospital network end-of-season 2023/24 data, we compared the effect of these CDs on influenza and COVID-19 VE estimates in Europe. METHODS Using the TND, we restricted analysis to seven countries recruiting patients using SARI-CD1; we created a subset of SARI patients also meeting SARI-CD2. Cases were RT-PCR-positive for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), or SARS-CoV-2; controls were influenza or SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR-negative. We estimated VE among patients ≥65 years using logistic regression adjusted for country, onset date, age, sex, and chronic conditions. We estimated VE overall, by age group (65-79, ≥80 years) and time since vaccination (14-59, 60-119, ≥120 days). Absolute VE differences ≥10% were considered relevant. RESULTS Patient characteristics and outcomes were similar across CDs. SARI-CD1 had slightly more vaccinated cases, with little difference in controls between the two CDs. For influenza, the absolute VE difference between SARI-CD1 and SARI-CD2 was 10% for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 (34% vs 44%), 19% among those aged ≥80 years (21% vs 40%) and 18% at 60-119 days post-vaccination (4% vs 22%). For SARS-CoV-2, absolute VE differences were 11% overall (29% vs 40%), 11% among ≥80 years (33% vs 44%), and 12% at 60-119 days (34% vs 46%). All other absolute VE differences were < 10%. CONCLUSIONS VE was similar for influenza A(H3N2), adults 65-79 years and 14-60 days post-vaccination. We observed signals of higher VE with SARI-CD2 for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and SARS-CoV-2, particularly among adults ≥80 years and ≥ 60 days post-vaccination, although 95% CIs overlapped. These signals suggest CDs may contribute to VE variability and VE studies should clearly indicate CDs used.

title: Post-COVID-19 Patterns of Respiratory Viruses in South African Children With Acute Respiratory Illness
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted respiratory virus epidemiology. We describe the postpandemic prevalence, seasonality and clinical presentation of viral respiratory tract infections (RTIs) among hospitalized South African children. METHODS: Children 0-<13 years of age with acute RTIs were prospectively enrolled between October 2024 and October 2025. Nasopharyngeal aspirates were collected on admission and tested for 7 common respiratory viruses using a multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical, demographic and outcome data were recorded. Disease severity was classified as mild, moderate or severe based on the need for hospitalization, respiratory support, intensive care or major complications. Cluster analysis identified distinct clinical phenotypes. RESULTS: We enrolled 315 children, median age 9.3 months [interquartile range 3.6-24.7, 132/315 (41.9%) female, 7/315 (2.2%) living with HIV and 53/315 (16.8%) HIV-exposed but uninfected. Disease severity was mild in 55 (17.5%), moderate in 184 (58.4%) and severe in 76 (24.1%) children. Respiratory viruses were detected in 276/315 (87.6%); most commonly human rhinovirus (167/276; 60.5%), respiratory syncytial virus (94/276; 34%) and adenovirus (59/315; 18.7%). Respiratory syncytial virus showed strong winter seasonality (P < 0.001), human rhinovirus circulated year-round (P < 0.001) and seasonal Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 activity was low at 10%. HIV exposure (adjusted odds ratio: 3.08)] and viral co-detection (43.5%; P = 0.015) were independently associated with disease severity. Cluster analysis revealed 3 distinct clinical phenotypes of RTIs, with unique symptom profiles, trajectories and virological patterns. CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses remained common in young South African children hospitalized with RTIs, with most returning to pre-COVID seasonal patterns and limited Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 activity. Distinct clinical phenotypes identify vulnerable subgroups and underscore the need for improved tools to distinguish severe disease from self-limiting illness.

title: The Impact of COVID-19 and Economic Policies on Nebraska Farm Real Estate in 2021
abstract: Land industry professionals responding to the annual survey attributed the rise in Nebraska farm real estate values to current interest rate levels, crop prices, and COVID-19 disaster assistance payments provided to operators across the state. These forces substantially impacted farm and ranch finances across Nebraska. Operators faced an exceptional amount of risk and uncertainty when navigating production decisions during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. Lower interest rates and disaster assistance payments provided stability to an industry facing an unpreceded economic shutdown and disruptions of supply chains.

title: BANK PERFORMANCE DURING AND AFTER THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: EVIDENCE FROM THE AZERBAIJANI BANKING SECTOR
abstract: This article examines the financial performance of Azerbaijani banks over the period 2019-2024 that corresponds to the COVID-19 pandemic and thereafter. The paper examines the volatility of profitability, credit risk, and post-pandemic recovery dynamics using profitability ratios including Return on Assets (ROA), Return on Equity (ROE), and the Loan Loss Provisions to Total Loans (LLP/Total Loans).It appears that during 2020-2021, there was a significant drop in performance indicators.In that period, ROA, ROE ratios deteriorated, while LLP/Total Loans ratio increased remarkably, due to higher provisions deriving from higher credit risk and precautionary provisioning.The results show that the indicators vary across banks depending on the sensitivity to shocks, risk-exposure and asset quality.Beginning from 2022, profitability figures improved, provisions decreased, credit risk dropped back to normal levels and asset quality improved.By 2023-2024, positive and stabile performance was observed in most banks, due to improved borrower creditworthiness and macroeconomic stability.
authors: Ulvi YAGUBOV Salatin HACIYEVA Aybeniz HEYDEROVA
journal: Journal of Baku Engineering University Economics and Administration

title: Future Jobs for People with Disabilities Post-COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Technology was the driving force behind future employment for people with disabilities and created opportunities, but it posed challenges regarding the gap between PWD and people without disabilities. Driven largely by the expansion of remote and hybrid work, current employment rates for PWD saw remarkable gains, even outpacing those of nondisabled workers in some sectors. The call of post-pandemic RTO mandates could erode the progress in flexibility of work and technology achieved by PWD in term of progress in the labor market during the pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States. In both countries, the legal framework encourages this kind of flexible working as a potential reasonable accommodation/adjustment, though the United Kingdom had implemented more explicit, universal rights to request it. The second half of the chapter examines the role of AI as a potential to enhance future work opportunities for workers with disabilities in both the United Kingdom and the United States through advanced assistive technologies and flexible work options. However, the realization of this potential could heavily be contingent on proactive policy and regulatory frameworks in each country to address inherent biases in AI-powered hiring tools and government systems. The post-pandemic labor market offered some potential for positive change, largely driven by technological shifts. However, despite the opportunities, the economic situation in many LMICs stayed the same or even worsened. In many of these countries the lack of robust, disability-inclusive policies and social safety nets would make individuals with disabilities vulnerable to economic shocks.

title: Employment for Persons with Disabilities in the Twenty-First Century Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Prior to the pandemic, both the United Kingdom and United States saw increasing employment rates for people with disabilities, driven by policy shifts, strong economies, and rising self-reporting of disabilities. However, significant employment gaps persisted, and workers with disabilities often faced inequality in pay, opportunities, and workplace accommodations. There was a steady increase in the number of people with disabilities who worked in the United Kingdom between 2013 and 2019. However, the gap between disabled and nondisabled people narrowed, but a substantial disparity remained. Despite improvements, workers with disabilities still faced notable inequalities. They were more likely to be in part-time work and lower-skilled occupations. Prior to the pandemic, employees with disabilities were more likely to face discrimination, leading to lower wages, fewer opportunities for advancement, and a lack of necessary accommodation. Employment for people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States had seen significant shifts in the twenty-first century, particularly shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic. While pre-pandemic efforts showed some progress, the pandemic temporarily reversed trends before accelerating new opportunities, most notably the expansion of remote work. For workers with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), the COVID-19 pandemic amplified preexisting systemic disadvantages. While the pandemic caused widespread job loss, workers with disabilities, who were already disproportionately in the informal sector, suffered more severe economic impacts. Post-pandemic, recovery has been uneven, with some progress seen through remote work, but the employment gap persists.

title: Clozapine‐Associated Neutropenia With COVID‐19 Infection and the Role of Filgrastim
abstract: ABSTRACT Clozapine is the gold standard, evidence‐based treatment of choice for treatment‐resistant schizophrenia. However, clozapine can induce serious, life‐threatening adverse effects, including neutropenia and agranulocytosis. There is accumulating evidence to suggest that rechallenging with clozapine should be considered in most patients with clozapine‐associated neutropenia (mild to moderate neutropenia) who do not respond to other treatments. Ruling out other causes of coincidental neutropenia is important when the neutropenia occurs after 2 years of treatment on clozapine, as the risk of developing neutropenia becomes negligible after 2 years and becomes nonspecific to clozapine. When our patient developed neutropenia whilst taking clozapine during Covid‐19 infection, she benefitted from Filgrastim [a Granulocyte‐Colony Stimulating Factor (G‐CSF)], which provided symptomatic treatment.

title: RELAÇÃO NEUTRÓFILO/LINFÓCITO (RNL) COMO MARCADOR DIFERENCIAL ENTRE COVID-19 E INFLUENZA:UM ESTUDO DOCUMENTAL RETROSPECTIVO
abstract: Introdução: As síndromes respiratórias causadas por SARS-CoV-2 e pelo vírus influenza apresentam manifestações clínicas semelhantes, tornando o diagnóstico diferencial precoce desafiador. No Brasil, a covid-19 circula com variações regionais importantes, enquanto a influenza tem distribuição mundial e sazonalidade distinta entre as regiões do globo, o que motiva a comparação entre o cenário brasileiro e o cenário mundial. A relação neutrófilo/linfócito (RNL) vem sendo descrita como um marcador simples, de baixo custo e já disponível em qualquer hemograma, com potencial para auxiliar nessa distinção. Objetivo: Avaliar a RNL como marcador diferencial entre covid-19 e influenza, comparando os dados de covid-19 das regiões do Brasil com os dados de influenza de todo o mundo. Metodologia: Tratou-se de um estudo documental, retrospectivo e quantitativo, baseado em dados secundários extraídos de artigos científicos publicados. Foram selecionados artigos brasileiros sobre covid-19 com dados das diferentes regiões do país e artigos sobre influenza de diversas partes do mundo. Os dados de covid-19 por região do Brasil e os dados de influenza de âmbito mundial foram extraídos dos artigos e comparados entre si. Resultados: Não foi observada diferença estatisticamente significativa entre os valores de RNL dos grupos de covid-19 e influenza nas comparações realizadas (p > 0,05). Além disso, a direção da diferença variou conforme se utilizou a RNL reportada pelos estudos ou a RNL recalculada a partir das contagens de neutrófilos e linfócitos. Conclusão: Os resultados não sustentam o uso da RNL isoladamente como marcador diferencial entre covid-19 e influenza. A RNL mantém, contudo, relevância como marcador auxiliar de gravidade e prognóstico dentro de cada doença, devendo ser interpretada em conjunto com dados clínicos e testes laboratoriais específicos.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

No Brasil, a covid-19 circula com variações regionais importantes, enquanto a influenza tem distribuição mundial e sazonalidade distinta entre as regiões do globo, o que motiva a comparação entre o cenário brasileiro e o cenário mundial. A relação neutrófilo/linfócito (RNL) vem sendo descrita como um marcador simples, de baixo custo e já disponível em qualquer hemograma, com potencial para auxiliar nessa distinção. Objetivo: Avaliar a RNL como marcador diferencial entre covid-19 e influenza, comparando os dados de covid-19 das regiões do Brasil com os dados de influenza de todo o mundo. Metodologia: Tratou-se de um estudo documental, retrospectivo e quantitativo, baseado em dados secundários extraídos de artigos científicos publicados. Foram selecionados artigos brasileiros sobre covid-19 com dados das diferentes regiões do país e artigos sobre influenza de diversas partes do mundo. Os dados de covid-19 por região do Brasil e os dados de influenza de âmbito mundial foram extraídos dos artigos e comparados entre si. Resultados: Não foi observada diferença estatisticamente significativa entre os valores de RNL dos grupos de covid-19 e influenza nas comparações realizadas (p > 0,05). Além disso, a direção da diferença variou conforme se utilizou a RNL reportada pelos estudos ou a RNL recalculada a partir das contagens de neutrófilos e linfócitos. Conclusão: Os resultados não sustentam o uso da RNL isoladamente como marcador diferencial entre covid-19 e influenza. A RNL mantém, contudo, relevância como marcador auxiliar de gravidade e prognóstico dentro de cada doença, devendo ser interpretada em conjunto com dados clínicos e testes laboratoriais específicos.

title: Evaluation of Carbon-Dots (CDs) as Antiviral Candidates Against SARS-CoV-2 Using a Chemical Crosslinking Method
abstract: The chemical crosslinking method has been effective in previous studies for interaction-based drug screening. Although CDs have been widely explored as antiviral candidates, studies that use chemical crosslinking to select effective CDs against SARS-CoV-2 remain limited. To address this gap, this study uses chemical crosslinking to test CDs as antiviral compounds. The objective of this study is to screen and determine the potential of CDs as candidate antiviral compounds for inhibiting the dimerization of the SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein using a chemical crosslinking method. Recombinant SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein was expressed, purified, and precipitated for compound testing with chemical crosslinking. The concentration ranges used in the dimerization inhibition testing were 0-2,000 ppm (pyrrolic-N CDs) and 0-6,000 ppm (pyridinic-N, graphitic-N, and nuciferine-derived CDs). The study’s results show that CDs have the potential to inhibit dimerization of the SARS-CoV-2 N-CTD protein. Among the four compounds tested, pyrrolic-N CDs showed the best inhibitory potential, as they inhibited dimerization at the lowest concentration (2,000 ppm), had the smallest percentage of dimer bands to total protein, and achieved the highest dimerization inhibition efficiency. However, further research, including in vitro and in vivo tests, is needed to comprehensively evaluate the potential of pyrrolic-N CDs.
