title: Comparative effectiveness of proactive exposure management and illness-based exclusion strategies for COVID-19 in healthcare personnel.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether COVID-19 exposure management in healthcare personnel (HCP) reduced presenteeism, occupational exposures and cases, comparing contact tracing and self-reporting exposure to standard illness management (i.e. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Large academic medical center, ambulatory and acute care. PARTICIPANTS: HCP COVID-19 exposure and case records (N = 30,102) collected at the University of North Carolina Medical Center, March 2020 through June 2021. METHODS: Among COVID-positive HCP, we measured hours worked while infectious and symptomatic, onward exposures, and secondary cases caused. Using negative binomial regression, we estimated mean count differences for each outcome comparing contact-tracing and self-reporting to standard illness management. We calculated the "number of encounters needed" to prevent one additional outcome (e.g., single onward exposure) by multiplying count differences by the proportion of exposure management encounters that identified a case. RESULTS: Contact tracing and self-reporting exposures captured a higher proportion of asymptomatic cases (14 and 18%) than standard illness management (5%). Both strategies reduced infectious work time by ~8 hours and presenteeism by ~3.5 hours. We found large relative reductions in onward exposures (62% contact tracing, 66% self-report) and secondary cases (79%, 100%), but small absolute reductions. Preventing one secondary case required identifying >1,000 traced contacts or >350 self-reports. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with standard illness management, COVID-19 exposure management reduced infectious work time, presenteeism and onward exposures, but preventing secondary cases was highly inefficient. Layered with comprehensive institutional mitigation strategies, exposure management provided limited case prevention benefits. Presenteeism was common and remains an important healthcare safety challenge.

title: Safety and immunogenicity of Thailand Government Pharmaceutical Organization (GPO) produced, COVID-19 vaccine, 10 μg HXP-GPOVac: A Phase III, double-blind, randomized trial in comparison with VAXZEVRIA.
abstract: BACKGROUND HXP-GPOVac is a Thailand-produced, egg-based, inactivated recombinant Newcastle disease virus (NDV)-chimera vaccine expressing a membrane-anchored, prefusion-stabilized SARS-CoV-2 spike (NDV-HXP-S), developed to expand vaccine access. This phase III trial evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a single HXP-GPOVac dose in healthy or clinically stable Thai adults who had completed a two-dose primary series of an authorized COVID-19 vaccine. METHODS In this double-blind, randomized, active-controlled trial in Nakhon Phanom, Thailand, 4000 participants were randomized 3:1 to receive HXP-GPOVac or VAXZEVRIA (AstraZeneca, ChAdOx1 nCoV-19). Safety outcomes included incidence, severity, and vaccine-relatedness of adverse events (AEs). AE incidence was compared between vaccine groups using Chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Immunogenicity was assessed by pseudovirus neutralization assay for 50% neutralizing antibody titers (NT50) and ELISA for anti-Spike IgG. Non-inferiority was prespecified for NT50-based endpoints at day 14, defined by (i) a geometric mean concentration (GMC) ratio (HXP-GPOVac/VAXZEVRIA) with 95% CI lower bound >0.67 and (ii) a seroconversion rate (SCR) difference with 95% CI lower bound > -10%. RESULTS Solicited AEs occurred in 43.7% of HXP-GPOVac recipients versus 53.5% of VAXZEVRIA recipients (p = 0.01). Most solicited AEs were mild. No vaccine-related serious AEs were reported. At day 14, the NT50 GMC ratio (HXP-GPOVac/VAXZEVRIA) was 0.83 (95% CI lower bound: 0.74), and the SCR difference was -2.35% (95% CI lower bound: -8.72%), both meeting non-inferiority criteria. CONCLUSION HXP-GPOVac was well-tolerated and demonstrated non-inferior immunogenicity compared with VAXZEVRIA at 14 days after vaccination. These findings provide rationale for larger studies to assess HXP-GPOVac clinical efficacy.

abstract: Objetivo: analisar a frequência, a distribuição e os fatores associados às manifestações cardiorrespiratórias registradas após a COVID-19 em participantes de estudo desenvolvido em Tucuruí, Pará, Amazônia brasileira. Métodos: estudo observacional, transversal e analítico, com análise secundária de banco de dados. Dos 98 registros auditados, dois indicavam ausência de COVID-19 e 13 não tinham informação pós-COVID interpretável, restando 83 participantes. O desfecho foi a presença de ao menos uma manifestação cardiorrespiratória registrada após a infecção. A reinfecção correspondeu ao relato de novo episódio de COVID-19 com teste diagnóstico informado. Estimaram-se frequências, intervalos de confiança de 95% (IC95%) e razões de prevalência (RP) por regressão de Poisson com variância robusta, com ajuste por idade, sexo e hospitalização. title: Análise temporal de sintomas da COVID-19 no Brasil
abstract: Objetivo: Analisar as tendências regionais de incidência de 11 categorias de sintomas em pacientes hospitalizados por Síndrome Respiratória Aguda Grave (SRAG) pela COVID-19, estratificadas por sexo e faixa etária, ao longo de seis ondas epidêmicas no Brasil (2020–2022). Métodos: Estudo ecológico de base temporal utilizando dados secundários desidentificados do sistema SIVEP-Gripe. Os sintomas foram organizados em 11 grupos e analisados por região geográfica. Empregou-se o Modelo Aditivo Generalizado (GAM) com ligação logito, ajustado via splines penalizados e estimação por REML através do software RStudio. Resultados: Observou-se redução da tendência de distúrbio térmico ao final da primeira onda em todas as regiões. O Nordeste apresentou maior tendência de distúrbio respiratório, enquanto o Norte registrou menor tendência até a quinta onda. No Centro-Oeste, predominou o distúrbio digestório, no Sudeste destacou-se maior tendência de grande fraqueza em maiores de 35 anos. No Sul, crianças e idosos apresentaram menores proporções de sintomas relacionados à dor. Na segunda onda, verificou-se redução expressiva de diversos sintomas, possivelmente associada ao avanço da vacinação. Conclusão: O estudo demonstra uma dinâmica temporal heterogênea da COVID-19 no Brasil, sensível a variações regionais e etárias, reforçando o impacto direto das variantes virais e da cobertura vacinal no perfil sintomático nacional.

abstract: We knew travelling for this measurement was going to be a challenge, but what we had not planned for was the increase of cases just before the measurement. There we were, constantly refreshing the status pages of the immigration pages of each of the countries involved to make sure we were still allowed. It was unclear what would happen with the beam time we had reserved if we were unable to enter Belgium, where the beam test facility was located.

title: Interaksi Sel Penyaji Antigen, Limfosit B dan T, serta Antibodi dalam Respons Imun terhadap Infeksi SARS-CoV-2: Tinjauan Literatur
abstract: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infection A complex immunological response involving defense mechanisms of both the innate and adaptive immune systems triggered by coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The purpose of this literature review was to methodically examine the molecular and cellular interactions that determine the clinical course of COVID-19 between antigen-presenting cells (APCs), T lymphocytes (CD4+ and CD8+), B lymphocytes, and neutralizing antibodies. Using a descriptive-qualitative literature review technique, seven scientific journals regarding the immunological response to SARS-CoV-2 were reviewed. The findings of this review suggest that the presentation of antigens via MHC-I and MHC-II is triggered when APCs (alveolar macrophages and dendritic cells) recognize Spike (S) and Nucleocapsid (N) proteins via Pattern Recognition Receptors (PRR). This process stimulates cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and B cells and activates CD4+ helper T cells to produce cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2). After differentiating into plasma cells, B cells release specific IgM, IgA, and IgG antibodies that block the Receptor Binding Domain (RBD). Loss of regulatory control leads to dysregulation in the form of activation of NLRP3/AIM2 inflammasomes, formation of Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) by the complement system, severe T-cell lymphopenia, and oversecretion of proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α), known as cytokine storms, which cause acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The development of recombinant mRNA/protein-based vaccination techniques and precision immunomodulatory drugs relies heavily on a deep understanding of the dynamics of these cellular interactions.

source_records.abstract: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infection A complex immunological response involving defense mechanisms of both the innate and adaptive immune systems triggered by coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The purpose of this literature review was to methodically examine the molecular and cellular interactions that determine the clinical course of COVID-19 between antigen-presenting cells (APCs), T lymphocytes (CD4+ and CD8+), B lymphocytes, and neutralizing antibodies. Using a descriptive-qualitative literature review technique, seven scientific journals regarding the immunological response to SARS-CoV-2 were reviewed. The findings of this review suggest that the presentation of antigens via MHC-I and MHC-II is triggered when APCs (alveolar macrophages and dendritic cells) recognize Spike (S) and Nucleocapsid (N) proteins via Pattern Recognition Receptors (PRR). This process stimulates cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and B cells and activates CD4+ helper T cells to produce cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2). After differentiating into plasma cells, B cells release specific IgM, IgA, and IgG antibodies that block the Receptor Binding Domain (RBD). Loss of regulatory control leads to dysregulation in the form of activation of NLRP3/AIM2 inflammasomes, formation of Membrane Attack Complex (MAC) by the complement system, severe T-cell lymphopenia, and oversecretion of proinflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α), known as cytokine storms, which cause acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). The development of recombinant mRNA/protein-based vaccination techniques and precision immunomodulatory drugs relies heavily on a deep understanding of the dynamics of these cellular interactions.

title: Пищевые продукты как возможный путь передачи SARS-CoV-2 (обзор литературы)
abstract: В статье обсуждается возможность фекально-орального механизма передачи вируса SARS-CoV-2, который вызывает новую коронавирусную инфекцию. Вирус проникает в клетки через рецептор ангиотензинпревращающего фермента 2 (АПФ-2), который обнаружен не только в клетках легких, но также в желудочно-кишечном тракте и печени. Это подтверждает гипотезу о том, что вирус может передаваться при фекально-оральном контакте. Хотя подтвержденных случаев передачи инфекции пищевым путем зарегистрировано не было, наличие РНК SARS-CoV-2 в фекалиях предполагает возможность фекально-орального распространения.Основной целью настоящей статьи является исследование риска заражения различных основных пищевых продуктов, включая мясо и мясные продукты, молочные продукты, хлеб, фрукты и овощи, как потенциальных средств передачи SARS-CoV-2.В ходе проведенного обобщения и систематизации результатов научных исследований выявлено, что существует риск, связанный с потреблением сырого молока.

title: Assessing Entrepreneurial Intentions and Actions Among Youth in the City of Tshwane: A Post-COVID-19 Perspective
abstract: This study assessed the perceived post-COVID-19 Entrepreneurial Intentions and actions among youth in the City of Tshwane using the Theory of Planned Behaviour. It examined the perceived influence of COVID-19 on attitudes toward entrepreneurship, Subjective Norms, and Self-Efficacy, and how these factors shape Entrepreneurial Intentions and subsequent Entrepreneurial Actions. Data were collected from 326 youths across five regions of the City of Tshwane using convenience sampling and a self-administered questionnaire. The findings were generated from analyses conducted using Microsoft Excel, IBM SPSS version 29, and STATA version 13. The results indicate that the perceived effects of the COVID-19 pandemic were positively associated with the antecedents of the Theory of Planned Behaviour. However, Subjective Norms did not significantly influence the development of Entrepreneurial Intentions. In addition, Self-Efficacy was directly linked to both youth Entrepreneurial Intentions and Entrepreneurial Actions. These findings extend the application of the Theory of Planned Behaviour by highlighting the role of Self-Efficacy in translating Entrepreneurial Intentions into Entrepreneurial Action. From a sustainability perspective, strengthening youth entrepreneurship can support more inclusive and resilient local economies by expanding opportunities for self-employment, livelihood creation, and productive economic participation. The findings therefore emphasize the importance of supportive entrepreneurial institutions and early entrepreneurship development as components of longer-term strategies to address youth unemployment and promote sustainable socio-economic development.

title: [Risk prediction of pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection].
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the risk factors for pneumonia after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2(SARS-CoV-2) infection in maintenance hemodialysis patients from a single center in China, and to establish a multivariate model to predict the risk of pneumonia. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on maintenance hemodialysis patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen or nucleic acid tests treated at Peking University Third Hospital from December 1, 2022 to January 31, 2023. Demographic data, comorbidities, dialysis-related parameters, and laboratory test results were collected. Multivariate Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve were adopted to explore risk factors of pneumonia, and a multivariate model was established to predict the risk of pneumonia occurrence. Taking the cut-off value of 0.575, the sensitivity and specificity of predictive factor Q for predicting pneumonia were 44.0% and 94.5%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Advanced age, anemia and hypoalbuminemia are risk factors for pneumonia in maintenance hemodialysis patients following SARS-CoV-2 infection. A predictive marker Q value less than 0.575 indicates low risk of pneumonia, which can be applied for rapid risk stratification among hemodialysis patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Herpes zoster epidemiology during and after the COVID-19 pandemic: A 5-year retrospective study from primary care in Poland.
abstract: BACKGROUND Herpes zoster (HZ) is caused by reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus and affects 25-30% of individuals, with the highest incidence in adults aged ≥50 years and a lifetime risk exceeding 50% after the age of 85. Its most common complication is postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), i.e., persistent neuropathic pain. Reports of increased HZ incidence during or after SARS-CoV-2 infection suggest potential epidemiological associations requiring further investigation. OBJECTIVES Our goals were to evaluate the incidence of HZ and its complications during the pandemic and the post-pandemic period in primary care settings in Poland. MATERIAL AND METHODS We conducted a retrospective multicenter study in 20 primary care clinics in Poland, covering 43,949-81,091 patients from 2020 to 2024. Incident HZ cases and complications (PHN, herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO), HZ oticus, and disseminated HZ) were identified, and demographic data, including place of residence, were collected. Statistical analyses included χ2 or Fisher's exact tests, Student's t-tests or nonparametric equivalents, odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs), and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis to assess age-related risk of prolonged symptoms. RESULTS A total of 570 HZ cases were recorded from 2020 to 2024. Incidence ranged from 1.61 to 2.14 per 1,000 persons and increased with age, reaching 6.57 per 1,000 in individuals aged ≥80 years. Patients aged ≥71 years had higher odds of developing PHN (pain persisting for >90 days) than younger patients (OR = 4.47; 95% CI: 2.30-8.67; p < 0.001). Older adults were also more likely to develop HZO (p = 0.001). Rural incidence was significantly lower during the pandemic than in the post-pandemic period (p = 0.005), with no significant differences in urban or semi-urban areas. CONCLUSIONS The risk of HZ, PHN, and HZO rises with age. During the pandemic (2020-2021), rural incidence was significantly lower than in the post-pandemic period (2022-2024). The study provides updated data on HZ epidemiology in Poland and highlights the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on healthcare access and HZ reporting in rural areas.

title: Perceptions and Predictors of Employees’ Communicative Resilience During a Crisis: Evidence From the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Organizations are constantly in flux, and the world faces crises ranging from natural disasters and pandemics to wars and economic recessions. These volatile times call for resilience. We examine employees’ resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic through the Communication Theory of Resilience (CTR). Drawing on open-ended survey responses from 827 respondents across two survey waves, we identified how workers engaged in resilience communication processes during full remote work. Workers used several strategies to deal with the crisis and develop practices that could be sustained in the long term. We also tested how sociodemographic variables predicted the mentioning of resilience processes at different times during the pandemic. Our study extends the literature by showing how resilience processes evolve over time, highlighting potential tensions between individuals and organizations. The findings clarify how individuals and organizations can become more resilient to societal disruptions.

title: Microaggressions at Work and Self-Esteem of LGBT+ Professionals During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Este trabajo buscó investigar la correlación entre las experiencias de microagresiones en el trabajo y la autoestima de los profesionales LGBT+ durante la pandemia de COVID-19, así como las posibles diferencias en las medias según el grupo de edad y la permanencia en la organización. Un total de 206 profesionales LGBT+ participaron y respondieron la Escala de Experiencias de Microagresión LGBT+ en el Trabajo, la Escala de Autoestima de Rosenberg y un cuestionario sociodemográfico. Se realizaron análisis descriptivos, la prueba de correlación de Spearman y la prueba de Mann Whitney para muestras independientes. Los resultados indicaron una correlación débil y negativa entre la autoestima y dos dimensiones de las microagresiones: los valores en el lugar de trabajo y la cultura cisnormativa. Los profesionales de 30 años o más presentaron medias más altas en autoestima y en microagresiones hacia los valores laborales. Los profesionales con más de un año de antigüedad presentaron medias más altas en autoestima, mientras que quienes llevaban menos de un año presentaron medias más altas en las tres dimensiones de las microagresiones (valores en el lugar de trabajo, supuestos heteronormativos y cultura cisnormativa). Este trabajo es pionero en el estudio de las microagresiones LGBT+ en el ámbito laboral en Brasil y sus resultados contribuyen al avance en la comprensión de la experiencia de esta población.

title: Ageism toward older adults during COVID-19: associations with emotional coping and intergenerational contact
abstract: Introduction The COVID-19 pandemic brought substantial social and emotional stressors, alongside widespread messaging that framed older adults as particularly vulnerable. It remains unclear whether these conditions were associated with hostile and benevolent ageist perspectives of older people. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the factors associated with ageism, perceived changes in emotional coping, and the attitudes and experiences of Australian residents toward older adults. Methods Ageism, aging expectations, and contact quality with older adults in the context of COVID-19 were explored using an online, cross-sectional correlational study design, participants responded to both established and novel measures for these factors. Results A total of 273 Australian residents completed the online study (aged 19–82 years, M = 40.73, SD = 14.74). There was no association between emotional coping and ageist beliefs. More positive aging expectations were related to lower hostile ageism, but not benevolent ageism. Positive contact with older adults was linked with lower hostile ageism and higher benevolent ageism, while negative contact showed the reverse pattern. Conclusion The current study suggests that ageist messages portraying ‘vulnerability’ reflected commonly held attitudes toward older Australians during the pandemic and highlights the importance of considering both the quality and nature of intergenerational contact when developing ageism-reduction strategies. Potential explanations, limitations and directions for future research are discussed.

title: Patient transfer adaptation through a crisis: The dynamics of a Hospitals Network during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: La pandemia de COVID-19 puso en crisis a los sistemas de salud en todo el mundo. Muchas infraestructuras sanitarias preexistentes tuvieron que adaptarse a condiciones nuevas y que además, cambiarían continuamente. Un sistema informático construido al inicio de la pandemia para recolectar, organizar y visualizar información sobre el uso y la disponibilidad de camas en la red hospitalaria ayudó a la Red Sudeste (que involucra 14 hospitales del sudeste de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, Argentina) en la gestión de la crisis (Instituto de Cálculo, 2020; Yacobitti et al., 2021). Además, el sistema permitió almacenar información sobre los traslados de pacientes que ocurrieron dentro de la Red. Los traslados representan uno de los rastros digitales posibles para entender cómo se interrelacionaron los hospitales de la red. Este trabajo estudia la dinámica del funcionamiento de la red a través de los traslados a lo largo de cuatro etapas diferenciadas de la pandemia.

title: Dynamic Co-Integration of Fintech Stock Returns During COVID-19 and Beyond
abstract: We demonstrate how Covid 19 impact their co-integration across crisis phases on leading fintech stock returns. While prior research has limited attention focused on interconnectedness, this study utilized the Johansen test to analyze the co-integration of major fintech stock returns across three phases: pre-, during, and post-crisis. The test value statistics indicate substantial long-term co-integration over the entire sample period. This indicates that the interconnectedness among fintech stocks remains stable despite external shocks, suggesting resilience in the digital financial sector. These insights can help investors draft diversification strategies for fintech stocks and help policymakers understand systemic risk and the resilience of the fintech sector during crises, thereby shaping regulations that promote market stability.

title: Viral interference with SARS-CoV-2 during the COVID-19 pandemic: An individual participant data meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Viral interference between SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory virus infections has been implicated, but symptom-based testing in observational studies may bias estimations. We used individual participant data from ten cohort studies conducted during pandemic years 2020–2024 to study virus interference. Respiratory samples were PCR-tested for viruses including SARS-CoV-2. The primary analysis was based on samples collected from cohort participants regardless of respiratory symptoms. A secondary analysis included only symptom-based testing data. We estimated odds ratios for co-occurrence of SARS-CoV-2 with other respiratory viruses. The primary analysis included data from six cohorts (n = 1 023). In total 205 of 2 465 samples were SARS-CoV-2 positive (8.3%). Co-detections with SARS-CoV-2 occurred less frequently than expected under the assumption of zero interference (OR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.40–1.25) for samples positive for another virus. The secondary analysis (five cohorts, n = 1 715) included 2 088 samples from symptomatic subjects, with 506 SARS-CoV-2 infections (24.2%). title: Covid-19 and the Shift in Deontological Feeling
abstract: In this chapter, I argue that the response to the spread of Covid-19 had significant effects on the bodily attunement of large parts of Western populations which, in turn, contributed to a palpable shift in these populations’ ethical sensitivity. I investigate how this shift affected the deontological domain pertaining to the way in which individuals recognize particular kinds of obligations and rights. In order to provide an account for that deontological shift, I identify several factors that contributed to the atmospheric condition in 2020/2021 and arguably had significant effects on the bodily attunement of those exposed to the atmosphere in question. I then suggest how a bodily attunement that is palpably shaped by these factors could account for the observed deontological shift.

title: Liquidity demand, financing and investment decisions: evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Purpose This study examines how firms adjust financing and investment decisions in response to the COVID-19 shock, focusing on whether external financing supports investment or preserves liquidity and how these responses vary across firms with different pre-pandemic characteristics. Design/methodology/approach Using data on US public firms, I employ a generalized difference-in-differences framework with firm and quarter fixed effects to identify differential financing and investment responses based on pre-pandemic firm characteristics. I also examine the allocation of external financing to cash holdings and investment, including capital expenditures, acquisitions and R&D. Findings I document that large and positive-cash-flow firms experience greater declines in cash flows, while small and negative-cash-flow firms raise more external capital, particularly through equity. Despite increased financing, firms generally reduce investment: large and high-cash-flow firms cut capital expenditures, while small and negative-cash-flow firms reduce R&D. At the same time, cash holdings increase, suggesting that external financing is used primarily to preserve liquidity rather than fund investment. Overall, the findings indicate that financing decisions during the pandemic reflect precautionary liquidity needs under heightened uncertainty rather than investment needs. Originality/value This study provides new evidence that increased external financing does not necessarily prevent investment contraction during a crisis, highlighting the importance of uncertainty and liquidity preservation in shaping firms' financing and investment decisions. By jointly examining financing, investment and cash holdings, the study provides evidence consistent with liquidity-driven explanations of corporate financing under heightened uncertainty.

title: Two-pore Channel Protein 2 as a Novel Broad-Spectrum Host-Acting Antiviral Target
abstract: In the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, the need for development of new broad-spectrum host-acting antivirals (HAV) has become more apparent than ever before. Given that there remain nearly 20 human viruses that are WHO priority pathogens who have the potential to be just as deadly as SARS-CoV-2, research has shifted focus to finding host targets that are widely used by human viruses during their lifecycle for HAV development. The two-pore-channel 2 protein (TPC2) may be such a target. TPC2 is a voltage gated calcium ion channel found ubiquitously in all host cells, predominantly in late endosome and lysosome-related organelles. The main function of TPC2 is to control intracellular calcium mobilization from endolysosomal bodies, regulating calcium efflux from these acidic compartments. Due to the nature of TPC2’s positioning within the cell as a master regulator of cytosolic calcium signaling, it has been predicted that inhibiting TPC2 may negatively affect viruses whose entry and escape pathways are calcium dependent. Building of this notion, here in this article we explore the mechanisms behind the potential of TPC2 as a broad spectrum HAV target. We first delve into previous literature to confirm if blocking TPC2 has antiviral activity via regulation of the endolysosomal pathway, which is often hijacked by WHO priority viruses such as Ebola, MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 for viral entry into the cytoplasm. In this realm, we also briefly look at the existing approaches of TPC2 inhibition and its applicability in a multidrug regimen. Next, we move to investigate if TPC2 inhibition can affect other mechanisms important to the general viral lifecycle beyond just the endolysosomal pathway, such as furin mediated viral glycoprotein processing or exosome biogenesis. Answering this question would ultimately allow us to also delineate the broad-spectrum nature or lack thereof for TPC2 as an HAV target. By examining the mechanisms by which TPC2 interacts with and influences the viral lifecycle of different WHO priority pathogens, we can better understand and appreciate its putative action as a broad-spectrum HAV target, giving credence to its development as a novel HAV therapy.

title: Trajectories of changing complexity: Inter-hospital inpatient transfer during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Los pacientes que acuden a un sistema sanitario se benefician de la interconexión de los hospitales que pertenecen al mismo, ya que facilita su derivación entre diferentes niveles de complejidad. Esto es fundamental en momentos de crisis como la pandemia de COVID-19, donde la disponibilidad de recursos es escasa. Considerando datos recolectados por un sistema informático creado al inicio de la pandemia para gestionar el uso de camas en la Red hospitalaria Sudeste, estudiamos la interacción entre el nivel de complejidad hospitalaria y la supervivencia del paciente. Este artículo presenta resultados preliminares sobre las estadísticas descriptivas de las trayectorias de los pacientes y analiza futuras líneas de investigación para el modelado de trayectorias individuales de pacientes.

title: Hybrid Populism in the Global East: Evidence from the Visual Campaigning on Facebook in the Era of COVID-19
abstract: This study examines visual communication as a voter engagement tool on social media during the COVID-19 pandemic in Albania and Kosovo, two hybrid regimes that share historical and cultural legacies but distinct party systems and media landscapes. Guided by the theory of hybrid populism and a quantitative content analysis of 2,003 Facebook posts from the 2021 elections, we test the engagement effects of cognitive and emotional dimensions of visual mobilization. Findings reveal a gap between party messaging and audience engagement. In Albania, populist visuals were more common but less engaging; in Kosovo, they drove higher interaction. Cognitive mobilization posts fostered engagement but were underutilized. We discuss implications for digital political communication within the context of transitional societies in the Global East.

title: Beyond the Lockdown: Long-Term Impact of COVID-19 on Registered Domestic Violence in the Netherlands
abstract: Domestic violence is a pervasive, societal issue impacting millions of people worldwide. While numerous studies have examined the short-term impact of the COVID-19 restrictions on domestic violence, research on its long-term effects remains limited. This study aims to explore the long-term impact of the pandemic on domestic violence trends in the Netherlands. Through descriptive quantitative analyses of official registrations and advisory requests from national domestic violence agencies from March 2019 to March 2024, covering one year before, two years during, and two years after the pandemic, this study investigates potential delayed or catch-up effects in domestic violence registrations using descriptive analyses. The results show a decline in the number of reports during the pandemic, followed by a rebound in the two years after it ended, reaching levels slightly below pre-pandemic levels. However, shifts in reporting behavior were observed, with a gradual increase in reports by individuals directly involved and a decrease in reports from family members and neighbors. Notably, while official reports suggested no long-term increase in domestic violence registrations, advisory requests continued to increase. These findings highlight discrepancies in data sources and emphasize the need for careful consideration of existing patterns and reporting thresholds when interpreting trends.
authors: Steve G. A. van de Weijer

title: Reconfiguring university students’ relationships with urban space during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This study analyses how the COVID-19 pandemic transformed students’ spatial practices and experiences of urban space. The study is based on 15 semi-structured in-depth interviews conducted among students from 10 universities in Poznań, Poland. The study extends research on the impact of COVID-19 on mental health, remote learning, and social isolation by focusing on students’ everyday relationships with urban space and their sense of place. The pandemic not only restricted students’ mobility and access to urban spaces but also presented an opportunity to reconfigure their daily relationships with the city. Students reported increased engagement with local and open urban spaces, a shift in preferences for public space use, and greater sensitivity to other users. While many participants described a return to pre-pandemic routines, some practices and perceptions of space developed during the pandemic have persisted. Mobility restrictions encouraged many incoming students to explore previously unknown urban landscapes, helping them gain a deeper understanding of the city, become more familiar with it, and strengthen their daily connections to urban places. The results highlight the role of universities as key facilitators of students’ daily mobility, social interactions, and their engagement with urban space, even during periods of crisis.

title: CSR Performance During COVID‐19 in France: The Moderating Role of CSR Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines the impact of the COVID‐19 pandemic on corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance among French SBF120 firms within a highly stringent regulatory environment. Based on stakeholder and risk management theories, we examine whether pre‐crisis CSR strategies act as a buffer or constraint during an exogenous crisis. Using a fixed‐effects panel of 93 firms over the 2017–2022 period, we introduce novel exposure measures to capture firms' pandemic intensity. Our results show a robust positive relationship between contamination rates and CSR performance, whereas pre‐crisis CSR strategies negatively moderate this relationship. Sub‐score analyses across environmental, social, and governance (ESG) pillars and extensive robustness checks—including difference GMM estimations and a difference‐in‐differences approach—confirm the consistency of these findings. Overall, we highlight that the COVID‐19 pandemic underscored the significance of CSR, particularly in an extremely stringent regulatory setting like France. Nevertheless, pre‐pandemic CSR strategies may have constrained French SBF120 companies' adaptability during an unprecedented crisis.

title: Universities In TÜRkiye During Covid-19 And The Red Tree Project
abstract: This chapter examines the transformative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on universities in Turkey, emphasising the adaptation of drama education to remote and hybrid learning environments. It discusses challenges faced by students and educators, highlighting creative pedagogical solutions through Ankara University&s;s Creative Drama in Education Society (EYAT). The chapter details “The Red Tree Project”, a drama-based initiative inspired by Shaun Tan&s;s illustrated book, which supported students emotionally and academically during this period. Drawing from student experiences and practical examples, the discussion concludes by reflecting on lessons learned and implications for future crisis-responsive educational practices.

title: Comorbidity Exposure-Window Definitions and Multidimensional Disparities in Long COVID Risk: Evidence from a U.S. National Cohort (2020-2024)
abstract: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of individuals worldwide, particularly those with preexisting comorbidities. However, when assessing comorbidity-related risk factors for LC, it remains unclear whether preexisting comorbidities should be defined prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection or LC diagnosis. This methodological choice may substantially bias estimates of LC risk. In this study, leveraging Electronic Health Records (EHR) from 6,130,413 adults with documented COVID-19 across 49 U.S. states in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) from 2020 to 2024, we evaluated the impact of different comorbidity exposure-window definitions on LC risk estimates. We developed ensemble cross-fitted double/debiased machine learning to adjust for individual- and county- level confounders. We found that defining comorbidities before infection rather than before LC diagnosis yielded 8%-314% higher adjusted attributable risks and 3%-34% higher adjusted relative risks across 16 major comorbidities. Comorbidity-associated risks generally declined from 2020 to 2024, while substantial demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and multimorbidity-related disparities persisted. Exposure-window specification can be a major source of bias in estimates of LC risk, particularly for comorbidities prone to delayed clinical recognition or underascertainment. More broadly, our results highlight how temporal misclassification of exposures in longitudinal EHR studies can distort risk attribution and population-level inference for risk stratification for LC and prioritization of prevention strategies in clinical medicine and public health, respectively.

title: Persistently activated virus-specific CD8 T cells indicate antigen-driven immune aberrations in long COVID
abstract: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of people worldwide, yet its driving mechanisms remain incompletely defined and no treatment has been approved. Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 and reactivation of herpesviruses have been implicated in LC, but direct detection of these viral antigens in blood and tissues has been challenging. T cells are exquisitely sensitive to viral antigens, survey organs throughout the body, and can be readily sampled in peripheral blood. Using high-dimensional spectral flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing approaches with multiplexed peptide/HLA tetramers, we profiled virus-specific T cells from hundreds of people with LC and recovered controls. We identified a subset of people with LC that maintained elevated activation of CD8 T cells targeting SARS-CoV-2 spike and/or lytic antigens from Epstein-Barr virus, but not other viral specificities. Spike-specific cells in LC expressed genes linked to TCR stimulation, terminal effector differentiation, and exhaustion and demonstrated reduced functionality upon cognate peptide stimulation ex vivo. Thus, T cells from a subset of people with LC are likely chronically stimulated by persistent SARS-CoV-2 antigens. These findings establish the use of T cells as biosensors of persisting antigen in LC and other disease settings and may help develop new therapeutic strategies for LC.

title: Associations Between Salivary HHV-6 And Long COVID Severity in a Cross-Sectional, Case-Control Analysis
abstract: Background Reactivation of human herpesviruses (HHVs), particularly EBV, is associated with more severe acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and the development of Long COVID (LC). Reactivation of HHVs has been previously implicated in hormonal dysregulation, which has also been observed in LC, suggesting a potential link. This study aims to examine the relationship between LC symptoms and salivary HHV DNA, cortisol, testosterone, and oestradiol levels. Methods Our cross-sectional, case-control study enrolled 45 participants with LC, and 45 age-sex-matched controls. Surveys and validated health questionnaires were used to collect demographics, medical history, and symptom profiles. Saliva was self-collected at waking, 15, 30, and 45 minutes, and 8 and 16 hours after waking, across two consecutive days. Salivary cortisol, testosterone and oestradiol were measured, and extracted nucleic acid was tested for EBV, HSV 1/2, HCMV and HHV-6 A/B using multiplex qPCR, and for SARS-CoV-2 and RNaseP using RT-qPCR. Findings Detection of salivary EBV and HHV-6 DNA copies was highest early in the morning. There were no significant differences in salivary cortisol, testosterone, or oestradiol, or in EBV or HHV-6 DNA between the LC and control groups. title: Multiple Sclerosis and Viruses: « Liaisons Dangereuses ».
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex, multifactorial neurodegenerative disease with an aetiology that is still partially elusive. Several risk factors are associated with MS development including genetic predisposition and various environmental stressors; however, recently, viral infections have gained significant attention as a crucial environmental trigger. Despite the well-established link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and MS susceptibility, a single-pathogen model fails to clearly characterise the molecular cascades driving the disease, suggesting that the transition from infection to autoimmune response involves more than one viral agent. In this review we examine the speculation that the interactions among different neurotropic viruses could serve a collective causative role in MS, which is under-researched in the literature at present. We summarise contradictory evidence on the role of different viral agents, including the Herpesviridae family (Human Cytomegalovirus, EBV, Herpes Simplex Viruses HSV-1 and HSV-2, and Varicella Zoster Virus), Paramyxoviridae family (Measles Virus and Rubella Virus), Influenza virus, SARS-CoV-2, and Human Endogenous Retroviruses (HERVs). Through interplay within shared molecular pathways, immune modulation, and activation of latent infections, these viruses may collectively influence the inflammatory and demyelinating processes that characterise MS. This review evaluates the etiological role of viral interplay in MS through the cumulative and interactive effects of these pathogens. The available epidemiological, immunological, and experimental data converge on the concept that viral co-exposures act synergistically to shape MS susceptibility in genetically predisposed individuals. Characterising these viral interactions presents a new research direction for the identification of novel biomarkers and the development of preventative strategies through the targeted control of viral networks.

title: Nanopore Sequencing for Chikungunya Virus: Principles and Application.
abstract: Nanopore sequencing is transforming viral genomics through real-time, portable, long-read analysis of RNA and DNA. Unlike traditional short-read platforms, it detects nucleotide sequences by measuring ionic current changes as nucleic acids pass through nanoscale pores, enabling direct single-molecule sequencing and base modification detection. Its simplicity, flexibility, and capacity for ultra-long reads make it ideal for resolving complex genomic regions, structural variants, and full viral genomes. These advantages have accelerated its use in pathogen surveillance and outbreak response, especially in resource-limited settings. For chikungunya virus (CHIKV), nanopore sequencing allows rapid, culture-independent recovery of complete genomes from clinical and vector samples, enabling real-time tracking of viral diversity, evolution, and spread. Experiences from Ebola, Zika, and COVID-19 have demonstrated the power of portable sequencing, now applied to CHIKV monitoring. Advances in tools such as Guppy, Dorado, Minimap2, and Medaka enhance read quality, consensus accuracy, and downstream analyses. Despite challenges in basecalling and error correction, robust quality control pipelines ensure reliable results. Ongoing improvements in chemistry, flow cell design, and machine learning will further enhance fidelity and throughput, establishing nanopore sequencing as a cornerstone of CHIKV genomic surveillance and epidemic preparedness.

title: Respiratory viral triggers and pediatric acute necrotizing encephalopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis of risk, clinical phenotype, and outcomes
abstract: Background Acute necrotizing encephalopathy is a rare but severe pediatric neurological disorder characterized by rapid neurological deterioration and characteristic bilateral thalamic lesions on neuroimaging. Increasing evidence suggests that respiratory viral infections, particularly influenza viruses and SARS-CoV-2, play a major role in triggering ANE. However, clinical evidence remains fragmented due to the rarity of the disease. This study aimed to systematically synthesize current evidence on respiratory viral triggers, clinical presentation, neuroimaging features, treatment strategies, and outcomes of pediatric ANE. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Electronic databases including PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase were searched for studies published between January 1, 2015, and March 31, 2026 involving pediatric patients (<18 years) diagnosed with ANE associated with respiratory viral infections. Observational studies, case series, and case reports with extractable clinical data were included. Pooled descriptive analyses were performed to summarize demographic characteristics, viral triggers, clinical features, neuroimaging findings, therapeutic interventions, and outcomes. Results Fifteen studies comprising 138 pediatric ANE cases were included. Most patients were previously healthy children, predominantly in early childhood. The most common viral triggers were influenza viruses (46.0%) and SARS-CoV-2 (42.3%), accounting for nearly 90% of cases. Clinically, fever (93.4%), altered consciousness (94.9%), and seizures (68.6%) were the most frequent manifestations. Neuroimaging consistently showed bilateral thalamic lesions (94.2%), often accompanied by brainstem (33.6%) or basal ganglia involvement (28.5%). Treatment commonly involved corticosteroids (75.9%) and intravenous immunoglobulin (51.8%), with some patients receiving targeted immunomodulatory therapies such as tocilizumab. Despite aggressive treatment, mortality remained substantial, with 54 deaths among 138 reported cases (39.1%). The random-effects pooled mortality estimate was 39.1% (95% CI: 29.8–49.8%). Conclusion Respiratory viral infections—particularly influenza and SARS-CoV-2 are major triggers of pediatric ANE. The disorder is characterized by rapid neurological decline and characteristic bilateral thalamic lesions, with substantial mortality and long-term neurological morbidity. Further multicenter prospective studies are needed to clarify immunopathogenesis and establish standardized therapeutic strategies to improve outcomes.

title: Mechanisms and Research Progress of LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Viral Infections
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), a class of RNA molecules whose transcripts exceed 200 nucleotides in length and typically lack protein-coding capacity, were once widely regarded as “transcriptional noise.” However, recent studies have shown that lncRNAs can encode small peptides and play critical roles in biological processes, including gene expression regulation, cell differentiation, and immune response. Viral infections, as a common disease, can reshape the transcriptome of host cells, in which the differential expression of lncRNAs is a core link in host–virus interactions. This review aims to deeply analyze the multidimensional regulatory mechanisms of lncRNAs in the host antiviral innate immune response. It elaborates in detail on how lncRNAs construct the host antiviral defense by regulating pattern recognition receptor (PRR) signaling pathways, the production and signal transduction of interferons (IFNs), as well as the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Additionally, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the complex functions of lncRNAs in regulating programmed cell death (PCD), including key processes such as pyroptosis, autophagy, and apoptosis, and integrated specific research cases in infections caused by multiple significant viruses, including influenza A virus (IAV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). We aim to provide novel strategies for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of viral diseases.

title: The Association between Vitiligo and Infections: A Systematic Review
abstract: ABSTRACT: Vitiligo is an acquired depigmentation disease with an unknown etiology. Several theories on its etiology have been proposed, including autoimmune mechanisms, oxidative stress, genetic factors, environmental factors, and lack of melanocyte growth factor. Recent studies have demonstrated a possible correlation between microbial infections and the development or consequences of vitiligo. This study aims to investigate the potential association between microbial infections and vitiligo, focusing on identifying any explainable correlations between these two. A systematic search was performed on all publications evaluating the effects of viral, bacterial, parasitic, and fungal infections on vitiligo using online databases such as PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 2010 up to June 2023 and followed the preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA) checklist. Viral infections, such as human immunodeficiency virus, varicella-zoster, and hepatitis C, are suggested triggers of vitiligo, potentially through immune dysregulation, cytokine imbalances, the Koebner phenomenon, and altered cellular immunity. Activation of MDA5 and vitamin D deficiency have also been proposed as mechanisms for virus-induced vitiligo. Infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) can dysregulate CD8+ lymphocytes and activate proinflammatory cytokines, disrupting immune tolerance and triggering or exacerbating vitiligo. Additionally, bystander activation triggered by coronavirus may cause an immune response against the host's melanocytes. Other factors such as Helicobacter pylori infection, endophytic bacterial and fungal infections, and vitamin D deficiency may also contribute to vitiligo pathogenesis by altering cellular immunity and systemic inflammation. Overall, a better understanding of the multiple factors that contribute to vitiligo may help inform more effective treatments and management strategies for this challenging condition.

source_records.title: The Association between Vitiligo and Infections: A Systematic Review.
source_records.abstract: ABSTRACT Vitiligo is an acquired depigmentation disease with an unknown etiology. Several theories on its etiology have been proposed, including autoimmune mechanisms, oxidative stress, genetic factors, environmental factors, and lack of melanocyte growth factor. Recent studies have demonstrated a possible correlation between microbial infections and the development or consequences of vitiligo. This study aims to investigate the potential association between microbial infections and vitiligo, focusing on identifying any explainable correlations between these two. A systematic search was performed on all publications evaluating the effects of viral, bacterial, parasitic, and fungal infections on vitiligo using online databases such as PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from 2010 up to June 2023 and followed the preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis (PRISMA) checklist. Viral infections, such as human immunodeficiency virus, varicella-zoster, and hepatitis C, are suggested triggers of vitiligo, potentially through immune dysregulation, cytokine imbalances, the Koebner phenomenon, and altered cellular immunity. Activation of MDA5 and vitamin D deficiency have also been proposed as mechanisms for virus-induced vitiligo. Infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) can dysregulate CD8+ lymphocytes and activate proinflammatory cytokines, disrupting immune tolerance and triggering or exacerbating vitiligo. Additionally, bystander activation triggered by coronavirus may cause an immune response against the host's melanocytes. Other factors such as Helicobacter pylori infection, endophytic bacterial and fungal infections, and vitamin D deficiency may also contribute to vitiligo pathogenesis by altering cellular immunity and systemic inflammation. Overall, a better understanding of the multiple factors that contribute to vitiligo may help inform more effective treatments and management strategies for this challenging condition.

title: [THE STRUCTURAL AND DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF THE DISEASES OF BLOOD CIRCULATION ORGANS IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The diseases of circulatory system continue to occupy leading positions in structure of morbidity and mortality of population, remaining one of key public health problems. The purpose of the study is to investigate dynamics of primary morbidity and prevalence of diseases of circulatory system by main nosological forms among adult and adolescent population of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2018-2024. The study used official data from the Center for E-Health Care that was analyzed using retrospective, statistical and comparative analytical methods. It was found that indicators of primary morbidity and prevalence were characterized by pronounced variability with greatest increase in 2022, against the background of decrease in 2020-2021, that may be due to changes in availability of medical care in period of COVID-19 pandemic. The highest levels of morbidity and prevalence were found for hypertension, coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular diseases. Some nosologies, including myocardial infarction and other peripheral vascular diseases, demonstrated sharp increase in indicators, suggesting changes in disease detection and health care seeking behavior of population. The obtained results confirm necessity to improve system of monitoring, prevention and early detection of cardiovascular diseases, especially among high-risk groups.

title: Genomic investigation of an Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K outbreak in a secondary school in Burundi, 2026
abstract: Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) are an important public health concern, particularly in settings where identification of the causative pathogen can be challenging. Testing of patients with unexplained SARI (SARI surveillance) and characterization of causative pathogens also is seen as an important pillar of emerging disease preparedness. Therefore, we applied targeted viral enrichment sequencing as a tool for understanding a broad range of disease etiologies. In January 2026, an increase in respiratory illness cases was reported in a secondary school in Bujumbura, Burundi, raising concerns about a possible resurgence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). However, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) testing of symptomatic individuals was negative, suggesting the involvement of another respiratory pathogen. To identify the causative agent, nasopharyngeal samples collected from symptomatic students were investigated using targeted viral enrichment sequencing. Eight SARS-CoV-2-negative samples were sequenced using the Illumina Viral Surveillance Panel v2 on the iSeq 100 platform. Sequencing reads were quality-checked and analysed for viral identification, followed by genome reconstruction, clade assignment, and phylogenetic analysis of the identified viruses. Influenza A virus (IAV) was detected in seven of the eight analyzed samples. Four samples yielded near-complete IAV genomes, allowing detailed genomic characterization. All characterized genomes were identified as Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K, representing the first genomic detection and characterization of this subclade in Burundi. Phylogenetic analysis showed that Burundian sequences clustered into two distinct groups, suggesting the circulation of at least two viral lineages during the outbreak. No neuraminidase inhibitor resistance-associated markers were detected. Influenza sequences were shared through GISAID to support global influenza surveillance. This study shows the usefulness of targeted viral-enrichment sequencing for investigating acute respiratory outbreaks when the cause is not known, particularly when initial testing is negative and routine testing for other respiratory viruses is limited. We provide the first genomic characterization of Influenza A(H3N2) subclade K in Burundi. The identification of different viral lineages highlights the value of genomic approaches to complement routine laboratory testing and support outbreak investigation and respiratory pathogen surveillance in Burundi.

title: A helminth-microbiota metabolic relay promotes disease tolerance.
abstract: Persistent infection by helminths requires limiting inflammatory damage despite incomplete pathogen clearance, yet how helminths mobilize resident microbiota to establish this state remains unclear. Here we identify a cross-kingdom metabolic relay through which Trichinella spiralis promotes systemic disease tolerance. Infection selectively expanded Ligilactobacillus murinus and redirected microbial tryptophan metabolism toward indole-3-lactic acid (ILA), a direct ligand of the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). Antibiotic perturbation abrogated ILA production, AhR activation and Treg-Th17 remodeling, whereas transfer of helminth-conditioned fecal preparations or supplementation with L. murinus or ILA restored these responses. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic deletion of AhR eliminated the protection conferred by T. murinus and ILA against endotoxin-induced lung injury. In lethal SARS-CoV-2 infection, oral ILA improved survival and limited pulmonary immunopathology without reducing viral burden, thereby uncoupling host protection from pathogen control. In a human COVID-19 cohort, ILA relative abundance remained inversely associated with IFN-γ after adjustment for available clinical covariates. These findings reveal that helminths can reprogram commensal metabolism to govern systemic immune tolerance and identify microbial ILA production as a tractable postbiotic strategy for limiting inflammatory tissue damage.

title: [THE TRENDS OF DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM OF PROTECTION OF REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH OF GIRLS-ADOLESCENTS OF ST. PETERSBURG].
abstract: The article presents results of comprehensive analysis of gynecological morbidity of girls-adolescents 15-17 years old in St. Petersburg in 2019-2024. It is established, on the basis of preventive examinations data, that average level of pathological affect made up to 105.04‰ and had pronounced trend to decreasing (β=-4.07; p=0.048). The comparative historical analysis demonstrated improvement of reproductive health indicators by 1.9 times as compared to basic data for 1996-1997. The characteristic of structure of gynecological morbidity of modern girls-adolescents in megalopolis is predominance of menstrual disorders (90.7% of newly diagnosed cases). At that, low medical activity of girls-adolescents continues that is proved by high percentage of newly diagnosed diseases detected only during preventive examinations (29.0%) and as well as significant prevalence of general morbidity over primary one. It is established that in St. Petersburg indicators of morbidity are 2.3-2.6 times higher than the National average indicators that is related to better accessibility of medical care and more efficient system of preventive examinations in the megalopolis. The analysis of the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on gynecological morbidity of girls-adolescents revealed significant decreasing of appealability in 2020 and subsequent incomplete reestablishment of indicators that testifies structural changes in pattern of medical activity of girls-adolescents. The study confirms efficiency of the system of protection of reproductive health of girls-adolescents in St. Petersburg but at the same time indicates at necessity to further enhance medical activity of girls-adolescents and to develop target preventive programs.

title: [THE MODERN DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGES IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The article presents results of analysis of medical demographic indicators of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2016-2024. The study was carried out concerning dynamics of population size, natality, mortality and migration processes based on statistical data from the National Statistical Committee and the Center of E-Health Care. The regional differences in demographic trends were revealed. The high natality is specific for Southern regions, while in Northern regions its steady decreasing was fixed. It is established that COVID-19 pandemic had short-term impact on mortality growth in 2020. Despite positive natural increase, its pace is decreasing that requires elaboration of state demographic policy and mechanisms stimulating natality, population health promotion and development of regional health care infrastructure. In 2022-2023 migration flows demonstrated positive balance that reflects changes in social economic priorities of population. The main motives for migration remain low wages, limited career opportunities and uncertainty about future. The obtained results confirm necessity of systematic approach to prognostication of demographic processes and development of measures stabilizing medical demographic situation in the Republic.

title: SUMOylation of Viral Proteins: A Promising Host-Directed Antiviral Strategy
abstract: Infectious viruses pose significant health concerns globally. In the recent decade, numerous pandemics and outbreaks have emerged, costing millions of lives and immense financial burdens. The World Health Organization (WHO) has highlighted the need for pandemic preparedness, with a list of WHO priority pathogens including high-priority viruses such as severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) and ZIKA virus (ZIKV). Antiviral drug resistance remains a major challenge due to the evolving nature of viruses, diminishing direct-acting antivirals over time. To overcome drug resistance, host- directed antivirals (HDAs) are key in preparing for the next pandemic. As viruses rely on the host's protein synthesis machinery, many viral proteins undergo post-translational modifications (PTMs) to facilitate infection. PTMs are covalent alterations to proteins after biosynthesis and are essential for cellular functions such as growth, metabolism, and cell signaling. SUMOylation is a ubiquitination-like PTM that regulates various host processes, including cellular localization, transcription regulation, and protein-protein interactions. This pathway involves the covalent attachment of a small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) polypeptide to a lysine residue on the target protein. Recent studies have highlighted that numerous viruses, including ZIKV and SARS-CoV-2, exploit the SUMOylation pathway to suppress host immune responses and facilitate infection. ZIKV manipulates SUMOylation to stabilize viral proteins, thereby enhancing replication, while SARS-CoV-2 modifies its nucleocapsid protein (SARS2-NP) to disrupt innate immunity. Both viruses alter interferon-beta (IFN-β) production, a critical component of antiviral defense, allowing for viral immune evasion. Beyond ZIKV and SARS-CoV-2, other WHO-priority viruses have shown to interact with SUMOylation to inhibit antiviral responses and support viral replication. The growing evidence of SUMOylation's role in viral pathogenesis highlights its potential as a novel therapeutic target. SUMOylation inhibitors, which were initially developed for cancer treatment, have demonstrated potential in disrupting SUMOylation and exhibiting antiviral capacities. TAK-981, a SUMO E1 inhibitor currently in Phase I/II clinical trials, has shown safety and tolerability in patients. SUMOylation inhibitors could be repurposed against emerging viral threats. Understanding how these viruses manipulate the SUMOylation pathway can allow for the development of HDA strategies, which can ultimately streamline processes for the next pandemic.

TAK-981, a SUMO E1 inhibitor currently in Phase I/II clinical trials, has shown safety and tolerability in patients. SUMOylation inhibitors could be repurposed against emerging viral threats. Understanding how these viruses manipulate the SUMOylation pathway can allow for the development of HDA strategies, which can ultimately streamline processes for the next pandemic.

title: Genetic Variation Shapes MECP2-Dependent Vulnerability to Stress-Related Adverse Mental Health Trajectories in Women
abstract: The multi-factorial origin of stress vulnerability remains incompletely understood, hampering the implementation of targeted prevention. As interplays between genes and environment lie at the basis of individual variability, epigenetic mechanisms are considered important mediators of adverse mental health trajectories following stressful experiences. We have previously demonstrated that the X-linked epigenetic factor Methyl-CpG binding protein 2 (MECP2) plays a role in stress susceptibility, with dysfunctional variants in transgenic mice and its downregulation in human populations being associated with a lower ability to cope with adverse events. By leveraging a study of the Italian Twin Registry on mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic, the present study explored whether a genetic component that accounts for individual variability in MECP2 expression may shape risk of developing stress-related mental health deterioration. We report an association between homozygosity for the minor allele of the rs2734647, a single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the MECP2 3’-untranslated region (UTR) that has been linked to allele-specific MECP2 downregulation, and increased symptoms of COVID-19 pandemic-related depression, anxiety and distress in women. Our findings provide additional evidence to the emerging role of MECP2 in stress vulnerability, unveiling the contribution of genetic variation within the MECP2 locus to adverse mental health outcomes in women.

title: Enhancing Scientific Validity by Integrating EHR and Claims Data in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative
abstract: Purpose: Accurately capturing a patient's health journey is essential for ensuring the validity of scientific and public health studies. Electronic health records (EHR) and administrative claims are commonly used in healthcare research, albeit separately. Previous research has demonstrated that EHR and claims capture different aspects of patient history and care, potentially introducing bias when used alone. In this study, we leveraged the largest public US EHR resource, the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C), alongside Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) claims data to compare their information coverage and agreement. Methods: We integrated N3C EHR and CMS data to create one cohesive dataset and quantified the proportion of key variables present in EHR alone, CMS alone, and the overlap present in both data sources. Overlap in information coverage was quantified pre- and post-landmark diagnosis of COVID-19. To evaluate the impact of data coverage differences, we conducted a case study evaluating the effect of COVID-19 vaccination on ischemic stroke using both data sources alone and in combination. Results: CMS data helped identify many individuals that were duplicated among EHR identifiers. Examination of the overlap showed that CMS data more completely captured conditions, while EHR data more completely captured medications after COVID-19 diagnosis. Some variables exhibited marked differences over time after landmark COVID-19 diagnosis. Using target trial emulation and self-controlled case series methods, we found that data capture variations altered effect estimates: EHR data alone yielded lower risk of ischemic stroke after vaccination in the target trial emulation (odds ratio 0.47, 95% CI 0.28-0.79), with a smaller, non-significant reduction in the self-controlled case series (incidence rate ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.64-1.02), whereas analyses using CMS data alone or both sources combined yielded estimates close to the null in both designs. Conclusions: Results indicated that when using either a national database combining multiple EHR sources, or CMS claims data alone, patients' medical histories are less completely captured compared to when these data sources are combined. Case study results highlighted the value of combining data sources for not only yielding fuller patient health histories and valid scientific results, but for identifying and explaining biases that may emerge in research studies that rely on a single data source.

title: Narrative Numbing and the Politics of Public Health Emergencies.
abstract: We examine how political polarization and prolonged crisis governance contribute to narrative numbing in public health emergencies and explore how these dynamics reshape executive emergency powers in the United States. Using Google Trends data, we assess changes in public attention to the opioid epidemic. We follow this with an explanatory case study of Pennsylvania's opioid state of emergency and a comparative review of national legislative reforms to state emergency powers. Prolonged emergency governance during COVID-19 coincided with narrative numbing, weakening the agenda-setting power of emergency declarations. In Pennsylvania, this shift was associated with legislative reforms that constrained executive authority with downstream effects on the opioid emergency. Nationally, state legislatures adopted time-limit, legislative termination, and scope constraints that reallocated authority from executives to legislatures. Narrative numbing is reflected in legislative reforms and has reshaped public health governance by limiting states' capacity to sustain emergency responses to prolonged or recurring public health crises. These changes carry implications for regional health equity and population health outcomes, demonstrating the need to maintain political legitimacy for sustained public health action. ( Am J Public Health . 2026;116(11):1719-1726. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308730).

title: Targeting TMEM16F‐Driven Membrane Remodeling: A Promising Strategy for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development
abstract: With the continuous rise of epidemics with potential for global threats, the need for antiviral drug development continues to be essential. Most drugs approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are direct-acting agents (DAAs), targeting specific viral proteins, thus restricting the range of applications of the antiviral. Due to the constant evolution of viruses, DAAs regularly have to be optimized or modified to maintain their inhibitory effect against emerging resistant variants. An alternative therapeutic approach to DAAs are host-directed agents (HDAs) which instead target host processes to inhibit viral infection. They offer more potential for broad-spectrum use if the targeted host processes are conserved across viral families. They are also more resistant to viral mutations. However, research has to be done to identify such strategic host targets. Previous work done on TMEM16F, a cell membrane Ca2+-activated scramblase, has identified it as an interesting candidate for host-directed antiviral strategies. TMEM16F’s role in phosphatidylserine (PS) translocation from the inner leaflet of the cell membrane to the outer leaflet is essential for microvesicle secretion. However, research has shown TMEM16F can be hijacked by viruses, such as Ebola virus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), for viral apoptotic mimicry and for cell fusion, respectively. By activating TMEM16F for PS translocation, membrane-derived viral envelopes may contain this phospholipid, enabling glycoprotein-independent viral entry and dissemination into a host. The extent to which different virus families utilize this scramblase for viral spread and immune evasion remains to be elucidated. Niclosamide, an FDA-approved anthelminthic drug, was found to inhibit TMEM16F scramblase activity. Drug screening also revealed antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2. While niclosamide has shown antiviral, antibacterial and anticancer potential, it has low bioavailability and can cause severe side effects at high dosage. Since TMEM16F’s 3D structure was resolved with cryo-electron microscopy along with niclosamide’s binding pocket, AI-driven drug analog design may be used to optimize the drug’s efficacy and minimize cytotoxicity. Thus, in this paper, we will consider whether targeting TMEM16F scramblase activity offers broad-spectrum antiviral potential and whether niclosamide can be repurposed and optimized as a pan-viral HDA.

title: The socioeconomic value of adult respiratory vaccination in Australia: a benefit-cost analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pneumococcal disease, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza and COVID-19 cause a major burden of illness and death among adults, much of which is vaccine-preventable. We estimated the societal value of adult vaccination against these four pathogens in Australia. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We developed disease-specific static life table cohort models and conducted a societal-perspective benefit-cost analysis of adult respiratory vaccination, approximating those recommended by the Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunization, relative to no vaccination. Mortality risk reductions were monetized using value of a statistical life (VSL) and value of a statistical life year (VSLY); avoided morbidity and productivity losses were also captured. Main outcomes were benefit-cost ratios (BCRs) and net monetary benefits (NMBs). RESULTS: Over ten years, age and risk-based vaccination generated gross returns of $11.24 (VSL) and $5.69 (VSLY) per Australian dollar invested (net returns $10.24 and $4.69), with NMBs of $64.97 billion and $29.76 billion, averting 234,187 hospitalizations and 13,890 deaths. BCRs remained well above 1 across all scenarios. CONCLUSIONS: Adult respiratory vaccination shows strong societal returns. Improving coverage and extending eligibility offer the potential for further societal gains. Some simplifications in the model are likely to understate the value of vaccination while others may overstate it.

title: The PTP4A3 Inhibitor KVX-053 Disrupts STAT3 and NF-κB Signaling to Preserve Endothelial Barrier Integrity in Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Acute Lung Injury
abstract: Abstract Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) remains a devastating clinical condition with limited pharmacologic interventions capable of modifying disease progression. We have recently demonstrated that Protein Tyrosine Phosphatase Type IVA (PTP4A3 aka PRL3) is a key mediator of the inflammatory cascade that drives ALI following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Here, we investigated whether pharmacological inhibition of PTP4A3 with the small molecule inhibitor KVX-053 could attenuate Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute lung injury (ALI) in C57BL/6J mice and LPS-induced endothelial barrier dysfunction in human lung microvascular endothelial cells (HLMVEC). C57BL/6J mice were intratracheally instilled with LPS (1 mg/kg) and treated with KVX-053 (10 mg/kg, intraperitoneally) beginning 1-hour post-instillation and every 24 hours thereafter for 72 hours. LPS-challenged mice exhibited significant weight loss, increased bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) white blood cell and protein concentrations, elevated lung injury scores, and impaired pulmonary mechanics. Treatment with KVX-053 attenuated weight loss, reduced BALF cytosis and proteinosis, diminished histological evidence of lung injury, and reduced the activation of key inflammatory signaling mediators, including phosphorylated STAT3 (p-STAT3), NLRP3 inflammasome, HSP70, and MMP8 in lung tissue. In HLMVEC, KVX-053 pre-treatment abolished LPS-induced phosphorylation of STAT3 and IκBα, restored VE-Cadherin expression and phospho-Cofilin levels and preserved endothelial monolayer integrity as assessed by immunofluorescence microscopy. Genetic silencing of PTP4A3 by RNA interference protected HLMVEC barrier function against LPS, and the combination of silencing and KVX-053 was not additive, confirming that the compound acts specifically through PTP4A3. Collectively, these findings define a PTP4A3 dependent signaling axis, converging on STAT3, NF-κB, NLRP3, and Cofilin, that governs endothelial barrier integrity in LPS induced acute lung injury, and demonstrate that its pharmacological interruption by KVX-053 attenuates pulmonary inflammation and barrier disruption, supporting the broader therapeutic potential of PTP4A3 inhibitors in ARDS and ALI.
