title: Testing structural interpretations beyond goodness-of-fit in a phenomenological epidemic model: A reproducibility-oriented case study
abstract: Simulation models are widely used to support counterfactual inference in settings where direct experimental validation is difficult or infeasible. However, for phenomenological models calibrated to observational time series, goodness-of-fit does not necessarily establish that the structural assumptions underlying such inferences are uniquely supported by the data. Here, we examine this issue using a published COVID-19 transmission model for Japan that incorporates empirical inputs including human mobility, variant prevalence, and vaccination and has been used to estimate the effects of alternative vaccination scenarios. Using the publicly archived code together with a reconstructed substitute for a restricted-access input file required by the released implementation, we first reproduced the published model behaviour. We then performed two complementary computational stress tests. First, the vaccination-related input was suppressed and the remaining parameters were re-estimated against the original epidemic trajectory. Second, as a complementary test of trajectory-level flexibility, the model was refitted to synthetic target series with qualitatively different temporal structures while retaining the empirical mobility and variant inputs. The model retained substantial fitting capacity in both tests: suppression of the vaccination-related input caused only a limited deterioration in fit to the original trajectory, while qualitatively different synthetic trajectories could also be reproduced through parameter adjustment. Variation in fitted parameters across these conditions was also consistent with compensatory parameter behaviour. These results do not imply that vaccination had no effect or that the original model is invalid. Rather, they provide empirical evidence that, in this case, goodness-of-fit to the observed epidemic trajectory alone does not uniquely support the structural interpretation required for vaccination-related counterfactual inference. The study illustrates the value of reproducible computational stress testing as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, formal identifiability or model-comparison analyses.

title: An inspectable Grover algorithm-based amplitude-amplification workflow for k-mer discovery and motif scanning with genomic coordinate traceability
abstract: Motif discovery and motif scanning remain core primitives in genomics, but both tasks face combinatorial growth as k-mer length increases and as mismatch-tolerant searches expand the candidate space. In this work, we present MotifQu, a Python package and command-line tool that maps two common motif-analysis workflows—(i) scanning a genome for a user-specified consensus motif and (ii) de novo discovery of recurrent k-mers above a user-defined count threshold—onto Grover-style amplitude amplification circuits executed reproducibly via Qiskit Aer statevector simulation. We evaluate MotifQu on the SARS-CoV-2 reference contig (29,903 bp) and S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome, where the classical census identifies strongly non-uniform motif frequencies dominated by A/T-rich 5-mers and returns explicit coordinate lists across the full genome span. We further execute the same logical 10-qubit search on IBM hardware showing that while end- to-end execution is feasible, transpilation-induced circuit depth and entangling-gate volume produce a diffuse measurement distribution whose probabilities remain close to the uniform 1/1024 scale, limiting observable amplitude concentration under current NISQ constraints. Finally, we demonstrate the full discovery workflow on the S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome (12,157,105 bp) to illustrate search results (ranked motifs, probability summaries, circuit diagrams, and position plots) and to highlight the regime where a large, marked set reduces the sharpness of Grover amplification.

In this work, we present MotifQu, a Python package and command-line tool that maps two common motif-analysis workflows-(i) scanning a genome for a user-specified consensus motif and (ii) de novo discovery of recurrent k-mers above a user-defined count threshold-onto Grover-style amplitude amplification circuits executed reproducibly via Qiskit Aer statevector simulation. We evaluate MotifQu on the SARS-CoV-2 reference contig (29,903 bp) and S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome, where the classical census identifies strongly non-uniform motif frequencies dominated by A/T-rich 5-mers and returns explicit coordinate lists across the full genome span. We further execute the same logical 10-qubit search on IBM hardware showing that while end-to-end execution is feasible, transpilation-induced circuit depth and entangling-gate volume produce a diffuse measurement distribution whose probabilities remain close to the uniform 1/1024 scale, limiting observable amplitude concentration under current NISQ constraints. Finally, we demonstrate the full discovery workflow on the S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome (12,157,105 bp) to illustrate search results (ranked motifs, probability summaries, circuit diagrams, and position plots) and to highlight the regime where a large, marked set reduces the sharpness of Grover amplification.

title: The Unified Systems Theory of PASC: Resolving the Ferroptosis-Replication Loop and the Bioenergetic Lock
abstract: Abstract Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) is defined by a systemic failure of homeostatic resolution, manifesting as a state of "pathological suspension." We propose a Unified Systems Theory wherein SARS-CoV-2 exploits a multi-layered molecular hijack: a "Ferroptosis-Replication Loop" coupled with a "Bioenergetic Lock." Mechanistically, the viral N-protein induces the lncRNA NEAT1, while chronic inflammatory hypoxia stabilizes CASC15, collectively functioning as a "microRNA vacuum" that sponges p53/NRF2-regulated transcripts (miR-145-5p, miR-214-3p, and miR-101-3p). This landscape facilitates the pathological upregulation of ACSL4, MMP-9, and TLR2, driving iron-catalyzed necrosis. Specifically, MMP-9 acts as a central executioner by suppressing GPX4 and silencing the NRF2 protective shield. Concurrently, viral-mediated degradation of WT1 collapses mitochondrial integrity and NAD+ salvage via the WT1-AS/NAMPT/PGC-1α axis, a failure further "locked" by CASC15-mediated suppression of biogenesis. Clinical data identifying low baseline SLC7A11, GPX4, and miR-145 levels in PASC cohorts validate this state of systemic ferroptotic suspension. By integrating the newly discovered noncanonical GPX1-OSBPL8 cardiac shield, we provide a definitive blueprint for p53/NRF2-based therapeutic restoration. We identify pharmacological inhibitors—including Nimodipine, Eugenol, and Quercetin—as agents capable of breaking the CASC15/NEAT1 vacuum, restoring bioenergetic flux, and achieving systemic resolution of Long COVID.

title: ScateClave: software complex for analysis and tracking of evolutionary changes in large amounts of viral genomes
abstract: As of June 2026, more than 18.5 million SARS-CoV-2 genomes have been collected and sequenced worldwide, creating a viral dataset of unprecedented scale. Such collections provide exceptional opportunities for studying viral evolution, including the dynamics of nucleotide substitutions, deletions, insertions, recombination-related patterns, and the emergence and spread of new variants across geographic regions. Although several web resources provide access to genome repositories and online analytical tools, many research problems still require local computation with custom algorithms, user-defined workflows, and private or unpublished sequences. In these settings, computational efficiency depends critically on how genomic data are loaded, represented, stored, and processed. Here we present ScateClave, an open-source software complex for local analysis and tracking of evolutionary changes in large viral genome collections. The system was developed and practically validated on SARS-CoV-2. Its computational core is implemented in C++, whereas static and interactive visualization is provided in Python. ScateClave is designed for efficient loading, sparse in-memory representation, and scalable downstream analysis of annotated genomes on a single workstation. The complex produces several coordinated analytical outputs, including a time-distance landscape, position-specific change matrices across the coding region, sliding-window profiles for Pango lineages, graphs of locally plausible transitions, and reconstructed paths between genome states. Although the current implementation and validation are specific to SARS-CoV-2, the underlying algorithms rely on general operations over sparse genomic events, temporal indices, and metadata, making the approach extensible to other viruses and suitable as a foundation for developing new large-scale genomic analysis methods.

title: Relationship of post COVID syndrome with blood type, sex and diseases in young people
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has affected over 700 million individuals worldwide, with a substantial number of confirmed cases still ongoing. A significant proportion of patients (10% to 77.7%) continue to experience symptoms associated with post-COVID syndrome (PCS). However, research concerning the incidence and progression of PCS has predominantly focused on older patients with comorbidities, leaving a knowledge gap regarding its effects in young, relatively healthy adults. To evaluate the relationship between the incidence of post-COVID syndrome and blood type, gender, and comorbidities in relatively healthy adults. Materials and methods. A total of 115 participants were surveyed to detect signs of PCS; the respondents were young (20–45 years old), healthy or with comorbidities, and had no ongoing therapy. Data collected included gender, age, blood group (according to the ABO system and Rh factor), the presence of comorbid conditions, smoking status, and COVID-19 vaccination history. Among the participants, COVID-19 was confirmed in 95.6% (n=110). Of these, 67% exhibited symptoms consistent with PCS, with incidence higher among women (85%) than among those without PCS (64%; p=0.03). Notably, among participants with PCS, those with blood group A (II) were more prevalent, constituting 47.3% in the PCS group vs. 22.2% in the non-PCS group (OR, 2.42; 95% CI, 1.39-4.2). In contrast, blood groups B (III) and AB (IV) were less common among those with PCS, with prevalence rates of 16.2% and 5.4%, respectively, compared to 44.4% and 16.7% in the non-PCS group (p=0.0008). Additionally, individuals with digestive system conditions were more frequently observed in the PCS group (20.3% vs. 5.6%; OR 7.14, 95% CI 1.23-50.0; p=0.03). The findings indicate that post-COVID syndrome occurs more frequently in women, individuals with blood type A (II), and those with concurrent digestive system diseases. It is plausible that these groups have higher susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 persistence, or that men and individuals with blood group B (III) or AB (IV) have protective mechanisms that mitigate the effects of infection.

title: The Heart Under Viral Attack: From Infection and Vaccination to Myocardial Injury
abstract: Chronic heart failure remains a major global burden, with respiratory viral infections frequently precipitating hospitalisation and mortality.Viral myocarditis has emerged as a significant contributor to cardiac dysfunction, driven by both direct cytopathic effects and immune-mediated pathways.This review synthesises contemporary experimental and clinical evidence on the molecular mechanisms by which cardiotropic viruses-including Coxsackievirus B, herpesviruses (HHV 6, EBV, CMV), parvovirus B19, influenza viruses and SARS CoV 2damage the myocardium, with particular emphasis on the roles of Toll like receptors, viral proteases and the pro inflammatory cytokines TNF α, IL 6 and IL 1β.These cytokines exert negative inotropic actions, promote cardiomyocyte apoptosis and disrupt extracellular matrix homeostasis, thereby contributing to adverse ventricular remodelling and heart failure progression.The review also examines the veterinary legacy of coronavirus vaccine development, which has been largely overlooked in human cardiology.For over half a century, veterinary medicine has confronted coronaviruses as devastating livestock pathogens, accumulating extensive knowledge of vaccine platforms, viral mutation and immune escape mechanisms that proved instrumental in expediting the creation of mRNA vaccines against COVID 19.Importantly, the review appraises the cardiac safety profile of these vaccines, concluding that the incidence of vaccine associated myocarditis-predominantly observed in young males after the second dose-is substantially lower than the risk of myocarditis following natural SARS CoV 2 infection.Although rare, post vaccination cardiac complications warrant ongoing surveillance and mechanistic research.Overall, this comprehensive overview underscores the convergence of infectious disease, immunology and vaccinology in shaping our understanding of virus related heart disease, while highlighting the translational value of veterinary research.Future investigations should focus on identifying individual susceptibility factors and developing targeted strategies to mitigate both viral and vaccine induced myocardial injury, thereby improving outcomes for patients with or at risk of heart failure.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Trends and Disparities in Respiratory Failure Mortality with Co-Listed Atrial Fibrillation and Flutter Among U.S. Adults Aged ≥ 65 Years, 1999 to 2024, with AAMR Forecasts Through 2035: A CDC Wonder Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background: Respiratory failure (RF) and atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF/AFL) often occur together in older adults, but long-term national mortality trends for the two conditions combined have not been described. We examined trends and disparities in deaths with co-listed RF and AF/AFL among U.S. adults aged 65 years and older from 1999 to 2024, and projected rates through 2035. Methodology: We used the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to identify deaths with ICD 10 codes J96 (RF) and I48 (AF/AFL) listed together. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 were standardized to the 2000 U.S. population and stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, census region, urbanization, state, and place of death. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Forecasts for 2025 to 2035 were generated with an exponential smoothing (ETS) model. Results: A total of 433,598 deaths were recorded. The overall AAMR rose from 12.8 in 1999 to 66.7 in 2024 (AAPC 8.11%; 95% CI, 7.35 to 8.87; P < 0.0001). Three segments were identified: an increase from 1999 to 2018 (APC 7.73%), a sharp rise from 2018 to 2021 (APC 18.10%), and a decline from 2021 to 2024 (APC -5.25%). Males had a higher AAMR and a steeper increase than females (AAPC 8.44% vs 7.81%). Non-Hispanic White adults had the highest mean AAMR, Hispanic adults had the largest relative increase (AAPC 8.72%), and Non-Hispanic Asian/Pacific Islander adults had the smallest (AAPC 6.23%). The Midwest had the fastest regional growth (AAPC 9.35%). From 1999 to 2020, non-metropolitan areas increased faster than metropolitan areas (AAPC 10.09% vs 8.21%). State AAMRs ranged from 24.7 in Ohio to 85.1 in Louisiana. Most deaths occurred in hospital inpatient settings (64.1%), followed by nursing homes (14.1%) and the home (11.9%). The model projects an AAMR of 122.96 per 100,000 by 2035 (95% prediction interval, 85.42 to 160.50). Conclusions: Mortality involving RF with AF/AFL among older U.S. adults increased more than fivefold over 25 years, with a marked surge during the COVID 19 period and only a partial decline afterward. Differences by sex, race/ethnicity, region, and urbanization point to groups that may benefit from earlier detection and coordinated cardiopulmonary care.

title: Generating Insights Into (Mis)Information About Measles Vaccination in Amsterdam Through Social Listening, the Netherlands, 2024
abstract: Background: HPV-vaccination prevents HPV-related cancers, but uptake remains suboptimal. In the Netherlands, a catch-up campaign invited 18-27-year-olds for an additional cost-free opportunity to initiate or complete their HPV-vaccination in 2023-2024, which led to 24% of this invited population getting vaccinated. As young adults increasingly seek health information online, understanding online questions, concerns and misinformation in response to the campaign may help improve future vaccination efforts. title: Comparison of three pangolin coronaviruses showing distinct pathogenicity, transmissibility and potential for cross-species infection
abstract: Pangolins harbor SARS-CoV-2–related coronaviruses (PCoVs). We isolate three PCoVs (P8V, P11V, P5V) from confiscated Malayan pangolins and analyzed their genomes, evolution and functional properties. Phylogenetic analyses place these viruses in two clusters within the PCoV-GX lineage, revealing spike mutations that later convergently evolve in SARS-CoV-2. All viruses replicate efficiently in Vero E6 cells, with variable replication in human cell lines and organoids. In hACE2-transgenic mice, P11V and previously isolated P2V cause rapid, severe disease, whereas P8V and P5V exhibit delayed pathogenicity. Direct-contact transmission in hamsters is efficient for all strains, with lung pathology reflecting strain-specific virulence. These results demonstrate that PCoVs possess substantial infectivity, pathogenicity, and transmissibility, illustrating their adaptability, and highlight the role of pangolins as reservoirs of coronaviruses with zoonotic potential. Comparative analysis of three pangolin coronaviruses reveals distinct pathogenicity and transmissibility profiles, demonstrates their potential for cross species infection, and highlights pangolins as potential reservoirs of zoonotic coronavirus threats.

title: Programmable design of functional RNAs through multimodal generative learning
abstract: RNA engineering is bottlenecked by the tight coupling among sequence, structure, and function, leaving the field reliant on heuristics or screening. We introduce RNAverse, a multimodal generative model that learns a conditionable design grammar from RNA sequences, experimental structural probing profiles, and functional annotations. Beyond setting a new state of the art across 16 predictive modeling tasks, RNAverse inverts into generative design across four distinct RNA classes through three regimes, requiring experimental testing of no more than 20 candidates per-task. Zero-shot in-painting generates snoRNAs that promote premature termination codon (PTC) readthrough, and chimeric aptazymes for ligand-controlled gene regulation, exceeding rational design or large-scale screens. In both settings, RNAverse outperforms family-adapted sequence-only baselines. Fine-tuned in-painting extends to an unseen functional class, yielding IGFBP3-binding aptamers with picomolar affinity that outperform SELEX winners. Iterative optimization engineers 5′ UTRs that outperform clinical benchmarks, enhancing protein production in cell-based assays for both the Zolgensma gene therapy and the BNT162b2 COVID-19 vaccine, and boosting antibody responses to BNT162b2 in mice. Together, these results establish multimodal generative learning as a route from predictive RNA modeling to programmable specification of functional RNAs.

title: Monitoring excess mortality among people with diagnosed HIV in Poland (2012–2024): insights from national claims data
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence on mortality trends among people with diagnosed HIV (PHIV-D) in Central European region is limited. We aimed to compare the mortality rates between general and HIV positive population and investigate the trends during 2012–2024 in Poland. Methods In this database study on the in the public payer, National Health Fund, claims data linked with census registry we applied an algorithm to identify PHIV-D, relying on the number of HIV-related and other claims. We estimated per year: number of PHIV-D aged 18+, mortality rate and standardized mortality ratio (SMR) for general population comparison. Kaplan-Meyer estimator and Cox proportional hazard model reporting adjusted hazard ratios (HR) were used for overall survival among newly diagnosed. Results PHIV-D population increased from 8.1 thousands in 2012 to 18.6 thousands in 2024, with proportion of females decreasing from 25% to 19%. In 2012–2024 there were 16,040 new diagnoses and 2621 deaths among adults aged 18 and older. The total number of deaths recorded in 18–64 age group was 2,386 and the mortality in this group group decreased from 2.66% in 2012 to 1.47% in 2024, and SMR, with respect to general population of comparable age, decreased from 18.2 to 8.8 in females and from 6.6 to 3.4 in males. Survival increased significantly with year of diagnosis and was lower in case of AIDS at diagnosis (HR 4.21, 95% CI 3.79–4.69) and during COVID-19 pandemic (HR 1.22, 95% CI 0.99–1.50) vs before pandemic. Conclusion The PHIV-D, in particular women with HIV, are at much higher risk of death than the general population. This difference is relatively large as compared to studies in other countries, which could be partially explained by frequent late presentation.

title: Integrating Citizen Perspectives into Table-Top Exercises: A Participatory Approach to Pandemic Preparedness
abstract: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic exposed deep social inequities in health crisis preparedness and response, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations in access to information, healthcare, and decision-making itself. These disparities expose a weakness in preparedness systems: the absence of participatory approaches that actively engage the populations most affected. The PREPSHIELD project ("Preparedness for Society in Health Crises and Disasters," HORIZON-CL3-2023-DRS-01-01) contributes to address this gap by embedding societal perspectives into health crisis preparedness, risk communication, and policy development, through three pilot sites spanning local, regional, and national scales. Methods This contribution presents findings from citizen involvement in a tabletop exercise (TTE) conducted in Piedmont, simulating a novel pandemic Influenza A variant, in which a Crisis Management Team (CMT) and a group of (vulnerable) citizens (MG) interacted through a continuous, facilitator-mediated feedback loop across successive rounds. Data were collected through observation checklists of the MG and CMT discussions, alongside pre- and post-exercise evaluation surveys for the MG and a post-exercise survey for the CMT. Results Citizens did not simply contribute experiential knowledge or a societal perspective on the unfolding scenario: they actively collaborated in shaping the decisions made by the CMT as the simulation progressed. Citizen input fed directly into each round of CMT deliberation, informing more inclusive response measures and shaping how economic support, healthcare access, and communication strategies were designed to reach vulnerable populations facing structural barriers, including vulnerabilities that the CMT had not initially considered. Citizens also surfaced original interpretive contributions, such as diagnosing institutional memory gaps and identifying a pattern of misinformed behaviour, that went beyond simply validating institutional plans. Conclusion This collaborative contribution of citizens moved beyond capturing lived experience toward influence over decision-making, demonstrating that even procedurally modest citizen involvement can generate substantively co-produced knowledge and inform the substance of crisis response. Beyond these findings, this work offers a replicable model, adaptable in duration, group composition, and facilitation structure, for translating citizen perspectives into decision-support processes, making health crisis governance more inclusive, equitable, and socially legitimate.

title: An in silico pipeline prioritizes candidate viral and bacterial mimics of hybrid insulin peptide autoantigens in type 1 diabetes
abstract: Abstract Hybrid insulin peptide (HIP) fusion junctions are not encoded in the germline proteome and may be absent during thymic negative selection, allowing microbial mimics to encounter T cells that escaped central tolerance. We present a structure-first screening pipeline for HIP mimics in type 1 diabetes, dataset-scoped negative results for motif yield and backbone RMSD, and ten peptides prioritized for experimental testing. Five reference HIP–TCR–MHC systems guided motif construction. The Swiss-Prot screen targeted ten taxa; a contemporary reconstruction contains reviewed sequences for nine. Of 1,092 motif hits, 55 passed predicted HLA-binding and AlphaFold 3 confidence filters and were modelled with TCRModel2 across five stochastic seeds. A composition-preserving shuffled-proteome control showed no aggregate motif-yield enrichment in the contemporary reconstruction (observed/null ratio 0.97). Candidate backbone RMSD had median 0.315 Å and interquartile range 0.274–0.389 Å; the three controls lay inside the candidate distribution at the 21.8th, 61.8th, and 81.8th percentiles. No single RMSD cutoff perfectly separated these sampled groups. A three-metric native-HIP gate using TCR–pMHC ipTM, interface-pLDDT, and ΔG retained 13 candidates; exclusion of three animal-associated Rotavirus A peptides left ten nominees. The nominated set was unchanged by dropping the redundant Kd criterion but was sensitive to the acceptance thresholds. Supporting comparisons found higher ipTM for 48 of 55 candidates, robust to nonparametric testing and multiple-comparison correction, but the candidate-only AlphaFold 3 pre-filter confounds that separation. RRNVATLQAENVTG from SARS-CoV-2 and SDLLKSVDSEEVRE from human rhinovirus 3 are co-priorities undergoing experimental testing: confidence and directional agreement favor the former, whereas interface energetics favor the latter. Their relative ordering is not statistically established. The pipeline supplies testable peptide–TCR–MHC combinations and documents the limits of motif-yield and backbone-similarity filters in these analyses.

title: Evolving infectious epidemiology in acute myeloid leukemia in the contemporary era: a 13-year retrospective, single-center analysis of induction therapies
abstract: Abstract We evaluated the 13-year (2012–2025) evolution of infectious epidemiology in a Polish acute myeloid leukemia (AML) induction cohort, contextualizing these findings within shifting antimicrobial resistance (AMR), the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, changing prophylaxis protocols (including fluoroquinolone cessation), and evolving diagnostic methodologies. Secondarily, we compared historical standard induction therapy (SIT) and novel targeted induction (NIT) regimens. This exploratory, retrospective, single-center study assessed induction-related infections in 219 newly diagnosed AML adults. We observationally evaluated temporal shifts in etiology and AMR, utilizing an interrupted time series approach to assess the 2018 cessation of universal fluoroquinolone prophylaxis, alongside a secondary comparison of SIT (n=189) and NIT (n=30) cohorts. The evolving infectious etiology in AML is driven by temporal, diagnostic, and ecological transitions rather than novel agents. Halting fluoroquinolone prophylaxis was clinically safe. Integrating contemporary therapies requires continuously adapting supportive frameworks to local epidemiology.Overall 30-day mortality was 8.2%. Comparing the pre-2018 (active fluoroquinolone) and post-2018 (discontinued) eras, proportional bloodstream infections (BSI; 40.6% vs. 34.7%) and multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) rates (77.2% vs. 68.6%) decreased, without a compensatory Gram-negative surge. Concurrently, 30-day mortality dropped from 11.9% to 5.1%. Between NIT and SIT, incidences of microbiologically documented infections (53.3% vs. 51.3%), invasive fungal diseases (6.7% vs. 13.2%), and BSI (33.3% vs. 38.1%) were comparable. title: Wildfire smoke leaves a large five-year imprint on mortality in the United States
abstract: Wildfire smoke poses a growing health risk worldwide, yet the magnitude and temporal evolution of mortality after episodic exposure remain poorly resolved, limiting burden assessment. Using monthly county-level wildfire PM2.5 and mortality data from the United State, we exploit episodic exposure contrasts to deconvolve overlapping mortality responses and recover the impulse-response function. The excess mortality response peaks approximately three years after an exposure pulse and subsides by five years. We estimate 1.7 (95% uncertainty interval: 1.1-2.3) million smoke-associated deaths during 2011-2023, approximately ten times estimates using long-term ambient PM2.5 mortality relative risks. Circulatory and respiratory diseases contribute comparably and dominate this burden. Responses are markedly greater among adults [≥]65 years; during the COVID-19 pandemic, population-wide cumulative responses are significantly higher over at least the first seven months after exposure. Reducing wildfire smoke exposure can thus yield substantial health benefits over multiple years, particularly when population vulnerability is heightened.

title: Effect of Cryopreservation of Perıpheral Blood-Derıved Cells on Transplant Outcomes in Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation
abstract: Background: and Objectives: The use of cryopreserved hematopoietic cells in allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) has become widespread all over the world and in our country, especially after the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. This situation has increased the importance of the effect of cryopreservation on engraftment, the incidence of transplantation-related complications, and the survival of patients. This study aimed to compare the transplant results between the patient group receiving peripheral blood-derived cryopreserved cells and the patient group receiving fresh products in patients over the age of 18 who had hematological diseases and underwent allogeneic HCT. Materials and Methods: A total of 222 patients over the age of 18 with hematological diseases who underwent allogeneic HCT were included in the study. Neutrophil engraftment time, platelet engraftment time, disease-free survival, overall survival, graft versus host disease incidence, cytomegalovirus reactivation/infection and transplant-related mortality rates were retrospectively compared between the cryopreserved and fresh product groups. Results: No significant difference was found between the cryopreserved and fresh product groups in terms of median age, gender, body weight, hematological disease subtype, disease status before HCT, Sorror comorbidity index, blood group compatibility, and preparation regimen intensity. On the other hand, the haploidentical HCT count was higher in the fresh cell group. The number of CD34+ stem cells received by patients receiving cryopreserved products was lower than the number of CD34+ stem cells received by patients receiving fresh products. No significant difference was found between the cryopreserved and fresh product groups in terms of platelet and neutrophil engraftment time, engraftment failure rate, cytomegalovirus reactivation/infection rate in the first 100 days after HCT, development of graft versus host disease, transplant-related death, disease-free survival and overall survival. Conclusions: Cryopreservation and cell storage is very important in order to prevent complications such as delays in the patient's transplantation process due to donor-related problems, prolonged hospital stay, and related complications. When done properly, cryopreservation can produce HCT outcomes similar to those obtained with fresh products.

title: Institutional Environment and Corporate Leverage in Latin America
abstract: Abstract This study examines how corruption control and financial freedom are associated with total leverage in Latin America. The analysis uses a panel of 729 listed non-financial firms from Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru over 2014–2024, totaling 7,241 firm-year observations. Firm fixed-effects models with year effects and standard errors clustered by firm show that financial freedom is negatively associated with total leverage, whereas the coefficient on corruption control is positive but not statistically significant. A ten-index-point increase in financial freedom is associated with a 2.95-percentage-point decrease in the debt-to-assets ratio. Additional analysis indicates that leverage was higher during and after the COVID-19 shock than in 2014–2019 and that the negative association between financial freedom and leverage weakened after 2019. A leave-one-country-out analysis identifies Argentina as an influential case: excluding it reverses the sign of the financial-freedom coefficient. Because this pattern was identified ex post, it is interpreted as exploratory evidence rather than a confirmed country effect. Overall, the results indicate that financial freedom is associated with firms' reliance on debt, while the relationship between corruption control and leverage is not stable at the regional level.

title: Online Group antenatal care: reaching out to Eritrean refugees. A mixed method study
abstract: Abstract Background Eritrean refugee women in the Netherlands face multiple barriers to accessing equitable antenatal care, including language barriers, limited health literacy, and cultural differences. Group antenatal care (gANC) has been shown to improve knowledge, empowerment, and care experiences, and was therefore introduced for Eritrean-born women, facilitated by an experienced gANC midwife and Tigrinya speaking cultural mediator. Prompted by the COVID-19 pandemic, this model was adapted to an online format. This study evaluated online gANC tailored to Eritrean-born women. Methods A mixed-methods evaluation was conducted of eighteen online gANC groups delivered nationwide between April 2022 and November 2023. Data were collected using facilitator diaries documenting attendance, topics discussed and group interactions. Questionnaire-guided telephone interviews were conducted six months postpartum (n = 40) by Tigrinya-speaking interviewers. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively, and qualitative diary data were analysed thematically. Results Participants reported improved understanding of pregnancy, childbirth, and maternity care system, increased confidence to communicate with healthcare providers, and greater awareness of their rights. Group discussions facilitated exploration of culturally embedded beliefs and sensitive topics, including lifestyle practices, female genital mutilation, and domestic violence. The presence of a cultural mediator supported culturally safe care and trust-building. While short-term peer connection was fostered, sustained community building appeared limited in the online format. Following completion of the study, adjustments were implemented, including focus on postnatal care and parenting, in response to participants’ expressed need for opportunities to meet each other. Facilitators report an increase in social interaction after these adjustments. However, overall impact remains to be evaluated in future research. Conclusion Online gANC offers a promising, culturally sensitive approach to improving access to, engagement with, and equity in antenatal care for Eritrean refugee women. Further research is needed to optimise model fidelity and examine its impact on empowerment, social connectedness and perinatal outcomes.

title: Respiratory Viruses in the Air of Shared Indoor Environments: Multi-Country Molecular Surveillance Across Europe (TwinAIR)
abstract: Indoor environments are the dominant setting for human exposure to respiratory viruses, yet routine molecular surveillance of indoor air remains rare outside single-site studies. Within the Horizon Europe TwinAIR project, a single harmonised workflow was applied to 102 indoor air samples (2000 L each) collected between October 2024 and February 2026 at ten pilot settings in Germany, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain, Greece and Sweden, covering university teaching rooms, school classrooms and staff rooms, healthcare-associated offices, workplace offices, an elderly care facility and public transport vehicles. Air was collected onto gelatine membrane filters with a Sartorius MD8 Airport sampler, total nucleic acid was extracted with the QIAamp Viral RNA Mini kit, and five targets—SARS-CoV-2, human adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus A/B, influenza A and rhinovirus—were quantified against target-specific standard curves as genome copies per cubic metre (GC/m3). At least one target was detected in 84 of 102 samples (82.4%; 95% CI 73.8–88.5). SARS-CoV-2 was the most frequent and most abundant target (64.7%; up to 8.36 × 106 GC/m3) and adenovirus was the second most frequent though consistently low in concentration (33.3%); both were recovered from all six countries. Rhinovirus (14.7%, five countries), RSV A/B (8.8%, four) and influenza A (6.9%, four) were detected less often yet reached high concentrations when present, showing that detection frequency alone substantially understates airborne viral burden. Detection of viral genome does not establish infectivity.

title: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I for post-COVID cardiovascular risk stratification: A three-year longitudinal cohort study from a South Indian tertiary care centre
abstract: Background: COVID-19 is associated with persistent cardiovascular complications beyond acute infection. SARS-CoV-2 induces myocardial injury through direct viral invasion, systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and microvascular thrombosis. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI), interpreted using sex-specific thresholds, enables detection of subclinical myocardial injury and may improve cardiovascular risk stratification. The present study evaluated hs-cTnI-based cardiovascular risk across different COVID-19 illness severities in a South Indian tertiary care population.Materials and Methods: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study included 2,063 RT-PCR-confirmed COVID-19 patients treated at AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad (June 2020–June 2023). Patients were classified as having mild (n = 436), moderate (n = 820), or severe (n = 807) disease according to WHO criteria. Peak hs-cTnI was measured using the Abbott ARCHITECT i2000 and interpreted using sex-specific HUNT study thresholds. NT-proBNP, D-dimer, CRP, ferritin, and IL-6 were measured concurrently. Patients were reassessed at six months. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, odds ratios, and logistic regression.Results: Elevated hs-cTnI was observed in 52.3% of patients at baseline. Among troponin-negative patients, 31.8% were classified as high risk and 28.3% as moderate risk using sex-specific thresholds. Men had significantly greater odds of high-risk classification than women (OR 4.07, 95% CI 2.50–6.60; p < 0.001). Six-month follow-up demonstrated progression to higher-risk categories across all illness severities, including patients with initially mild disease. D-dimer was elevated in 88.7–92.4% of patients, indicating persistent thromboinflammatory activity.Conclusion: Sex-specific hs-cTnI thresholds identify clinically important subclinical cardiovascular risk after COVID-19 and support structured long-term cardiovascular surveillance.

title: Molecular detection of respiratory viruses from breath samples: Evaluation of nucleic acid extraction systems and PCR panels
abstract: Background Reliable and scalable molecular testing is essential for risk assessment and monitoring of respiratory viruses with epidemic or pandemic potential. The AveloMask Kit (Avelo) is a non-invasive sampling device that collects exhaled breath aerosols (XBA) using a high-performance filter, which can be released into a stabilizing buffer for nucleic acid preservation. Detection of viral nucleic acids in breath samples remains challenging, as viral loads are typically lower than in conventional upper-respiratory swabs. Therefore, optimizing extraction and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) workflows is critical to maximizing analytical sensitivity. Methods In this proof-of-concept study, we compared the nucleic acid extraction efficiency of ELITe InGenius® (ELITech) and QIAsymphony (Qiagen) automated platforms in combination with an in-house real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) panel and a commercial PCR panel (RespiFinder® 2Smart, Pathofinder). Using synthetic ribonucleic acid (RNA) standards, we determined the limit of detection (LOD) for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) as a performance indicator for both extraction platforms and PCR panels. As proof-of-concept, we analyzed seven XBA samples from infected individuals, eight from healthy controls, and one from a person recovering from a cold. Results Our results demonstrate that ELITe InGenius and QIAsymphony provide comparable extraction efficiencies without negatively impacting downstream RT-qPCR. The combination of QIAsymphony and RespiFinder 2Smart achieved LODs below 100 viral copies/mL and detected all pathogens in clinical XBA samples (7/7) that were also detected in matched swabs. Conclusions These initial findings suggest the compatibility of high-throughput extraction systems and PCR panels with XBA samples collected using AveloMask and warrant further investigation of XBA sampling as a non-invasive method for respiratory virus detection.

title: Mass cytometry of early immune remodeling after mRNA booster vaccination reveals exploratory CD4 naive T-cell associations with documented breakthrough infection
abstract: Background Messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines rapidly engage innate and adaptive immunity, but the systemic immune changes occurring within 24 h of vaccination remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether early cellular and global H3K27ac/m6A changes were associated with subsequent documented breakthrough infection (BTI). Methods We performed an exploratory longitudinal systems-immunology analysis of an outcome-balanced subset of 124 participants from a randomized trial of COVID-19 mRNA booster vaccination (62 BTI and 62 non-BTI). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells collected at Day 0 and Day 1 were profiled by high-dimensional mass cytometry. Seventeen major immune-cell populations were assessed for changes in relative abundance, marker profiles, and global H3K27ac/m6A signals. Neutralizing-antibody responses were measured through Day 180. Results Within 24 h, booster vaccination induced rapid lineage-specific remodeling of circulating immune composition. Classical and intermediate monocytes showed positive shifts in CLR-transformed relative abundance, whereas pDCs, NK cells, and selected CD8 and unconventional T-cell populations showed negative shifts. CD4 T-cell populations remained comparatively stable on this relative-composition scale. Early H3K27ac and m6A changes correlated with abundance changes in selected innate and T-cell populations. Associations with later humoral immunity were limited: after exclusion of antibody measurements obtained on or after documented BTI, no association between early H3K27ac/m6A changes and Day 14 or Day 180 neutralizing-antibody responses remained significant after multiple-testing correction. Major-cell abundance trajectories did not differ significantly by subsequent BTI status. In contrast, BTI was associated with smaller Day 0-to-Day 1 changes in CD4_Tn IFN–Th1 chemokine, cytotoxic–Th1-associated, and CCL2–CCR2-associated marker scores and in the m6A readout. Conclusions mRNA booster vaccination induces rapid, cell-type-specific immune remodeling within 24 h. Major-cell abundance changes were broadly shared across BTI groups, whereas early CD4_Tn marker-associated and m6A signal changes were associated with subsequent documented BTI. These findings support further evaluation of dynamic early immune states as correlates of heterogeneity in vaccine responses.

title: Delayed Informalisation in India’s Post-COVID Labour Market: Evidence from Pooled Repeated Cross-Sections of the Periodic Labour Force Survey, 2017-18 to 2023-24
abstract: Abstract COVID-19 disrupted India’s labour market, where informal employment was already widespread. This study tests whether recovery restored pre-pandemic employment levels and quality. It also checks whether informal employment grew further after the pandemic. The study separates employment quantity from quality, protection, social security, and earnings. It uses unit-level Periodic Labour Force Survey data for 2017-18 to 2023-24. Pooled repeated cross-sectional regressions estimate effects on employment and informal employment. Additional models test differences by gender, education, social group, and rural-urban location. The study also examines industry differences, employment benefits, and earnings. Robustness checks use logit models, placebo tests, and an event-study design. An extended post-COVID period also tests whether the results still hold. Pre-COVID state-level informal employment measures each state’s exposure to the shock. This tests whether effects were larger in states with more existing informality. The results challenge a simple shock-and-recovery interpretation of the pandemic. Aggregate informal employment did not rise significantly in 2020, though employment grew. Informal employment rose by about 1.55 percentage points during the 2021-23 recovery. Overall employment increased by a larger amount during the same period. Worker characteristics shaped the strongest differences in informal employment during the shock. Informal employment rose more among low-educated and socially disadvantaged workers. Paid-leave eligibility also fell significantly in 2020, which weakened employment protection. The negative COVID-female interaction needs care because estimates condition on employment. Selective exit from employment may explain this pattern for women. The positive earnings coefficients do not show pandemic-related earnings gains. The earnings sample includes only those workers who report their earnings. Survivorship and composition bias may also affect the earnings estimates here. Education and social disadvantage shaped informalisation more than initial state informality did. Recovery policies should address the quality, security, and protection of informal jobs. Low-educated and socially disadvantaged workers concentrate heavily in informal employment. Policymakers should therefore design targeted interventions for these vulnerable groups of workers. The immediate 2020 period shows no statistically significant aggregate increase in informal employment , although measured employment increased. In contrast, informal employment increased by approximately 1.55 percentage points during the 2021–23 recovery period , alongside a larger increase in overall employment. JEL code: E24, J21, J46, J48.

title: Cardiovascular complications as a consequence of coronavirus infection in pregnant women managed in ambulatory settings
abstract: Background SARS-CoV-2 has been linked to cardiovascular complications in the general population. However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. In this retrospective population-based matched cohort study, we evaluated whether COVID-19 infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular complications among pregnant women managed predominantly in outpatient settings. Methods We conducted a retrospective population-based matched cohort study using electronic health record data from pregnant women between 2020 and 2025. Women with COVID-19 during pregnancy were matched 1:1 to women without documented COVID-19 during pregnancy according to demographic, obstetric, and clinical characteristics. The final analytical cohort included 4,068 women in each group. Cardiovascular outcomes during pregnancy and within a year since last menstrual period were assessed. Baseline demographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the COVID-19 and control groups. No significant differences were observed between the groups in the incidence of major cardiovascular complications, either when analyzed individually or as a composite endpoint (0.15% vs. 0.15%; OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.27–3.74). Specifically, there were no significant differences in the occurrence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, or deep venous thrombosis. In contrast, cough and backache were significantly more frequent among women with COVID-19 than among matched controls (6.88% vs. 4.87%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.19–1.75; 13.8% vs. 11.8%; OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05–1.37; p = 0.007 respectively). Conclusions Our findings suggest that among pregnant women in ambulatory community settings, COVID-19 infection is not associated with an increased risk of major cardiovascular complications.

title: Computationally Guided Discovery of Cannabinoid Derivatives for Antiviral and Anticancer Applications: From Chemical Space to Experimental Validation
abstract: Cannabinoids represent a chemically diverse and structurally tunable class of natural and synthetic compounds that have attracted growing interest as molecular scaffolds for therapeutic discovery. However, their extensive chemical diversity, polypharmacology, conformational flexibility, and complex pharmacokinetic properties make the systematic identification and optimisation of therapeutically useful derivatives challenging. Recent advances in computer-aided drug discovery (CADD), molecular simulation, quantum chemistry, quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) modelling, and artificial intelligence (AI) provide opportunities to interrogate the chemical space of cannabinoids in a systematic and mechanistically informed manner. This review examines computational strategies for the discovery and optimisation of cannabinoid derivatives with potential antiviral and anticancer applications, emphasising the integration of complementary computational approaches rather than reliance on isolated in silico predictions. A hierarchical computational workflow is described, progressing from cannabinoid chemical-space generation and ligand preparation to disease-relevant target identification, virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, binding free-energy estimation, quantum-chemical analysis, and ADMET/drug-likeness prediction. For antiviral discovery, computational investigations of SARS-CoV-2 targets, including the main protease (Mpro/3CLpro), papain-like protease (PLpro), spike protein, and spike–ACE2 interface, are discussed alongside emerging host-directed targets. For anticancer applications, computational studies involving EGFR, HER2, VEGFR, PI3K/AKT, MAPK, apoptosis, autophagy, oxidative stress, and cell-cycle regulation are evaluated. Particular emphasis is placed on the complementary roles of docking and MD simulations in characterising binding modes, interaction persistence, conformational stability, and molecular recognition, while MM-PBSA/MM-GBSA and related approaches provide additional energetic criteria for candidate prioritisation. QSAR and AI/ML-assisted approaches are further considered as complementary tools for expanding chemical-space exploration, predicting biological activity and ADMET properties, and enabling multi-parameter candidate prioritisation. Importantly, computational affinity scores are not treated as sufficient evidence of target inhibition or therapeutic efficacy. Instead, the review emphasises a progressive validation framework in which computationally prioritised candidates are evaluated through biochemical target-engagement studies, cellular assays, and, where appropriate, in vivo models. Experimental observations can subsequently inform structure–activity relationship analysis, lead optimisation, and iterative computational rescreening, establishing a closed-loop strategy for integrating molecular recognition, dynamic behaviour, binding energetics, pharmacokinetic properties, toxicity, and biological activity during cannabinoid lead development. The review critically examines key limitations of current computational approaches, including incomplete treatment of ligand flexibility, scoring-function limitations, protein conformational heterogeneity, limited experimental validation, dataset bias in AI/ML models, and translational challenges associated with cannabinoid solubility, bioavailability, metabolism, receptor promiscuity, psychoactive liabilities, and off-target effects. Collectively, current evidence indicates that computationally guided cannabinoid discovery is a promising but predominantly preclinical strategy. Further progress will depend on integrating CADD, molecular simulation, AI-assisted molecular design, uncertainty-aware prediction, and experimental validation into iterative multi-objective optimisation frameworks that jointly address potency, selectivity, pharmacokinetics, toxicity, and translational relevance.

title: Vaccination and Economic Recovery
abstract: ABSTRACT The COVID‐19 pandemic severely hampered human mobility and disrupted a series of economic activities. In this study, I examine the impacts of vaccine coverage on mobility and several other economic indicators in the US. I construct a novel shift‐share instrument that leverages the strong correlation between vaccination rates and demographic composition by sex and age group to address endogeneity concerns. Using high‐frequency data, I find strong evidence that higher vaccine coverage increased mobility, reflected in more trips taken and a lower likelihood of staying at home. I then assess the effects of vaccination on multiple economic indicators. I find modest evidence that higher vaccine coverage increased labor market participation and employment rate, while the effects on new business applications and home mortgage applications are limited.

title: Computationally guided side chain optimization of nirmatrelvir for lead discovery against coronavirus main proteases
abstract: To optimize Nirmatrelvir as an inhibitor of the MERS-CoV main protease (Mpro), we developed an automated RDKit-based iterative scaffold optimization framework that integrated fragment replacement, combinatorial library enumeration, and chemical feasibility filtering to generate 15,744 drug-like analogs through systematic substitutions at six positions on the Nirmatrelvir scaffold. Structural similarity to Nirmatrelvir was assessed using complementary 2D fingerprint and 3D shape-based analyses of the 15,953 designed analogs and a separate set of 13,090 molecular weight-matched ChEMBL compounds to examine the binding potency in both the modified and randomly selected compound cohorts. Based on the correlation between structural similarity and docking score of the modified molecules, a binding score (BS) approach was advanced to rapidly identify and rank promising lead compounds. Several top candidates exhibited improved binding characteristics compared to that of Nirmatrelvir. To assess the robustness of the BS approach, multiple computational methods were employed, including K DEEP , molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, molecular mechanics/generalized Born surface area (MM/GBSA) free energy calculations, and Boltz-2. The BS ranking showed strong agreement with all computational validation methods, consistently identifying compounds with enhanced binding affinities and stable protein-ligand interactions. The top-ranked compounds, M1, M3, M5, and M6, identified by high Binding Score (BS) values (9.1–10.2), exhibited favorable MM/GBSA binding free energies ranging from − 31.7 to − 42.9 kcal/mol, K DEEP -predicted binding affinities of − 9.5 to − 10.6 kcal/mol, and Boltz-2 predicted pIC50 values of 10.0–11.8. Furthermore, for SARS-CoV-2 Mpro, BS scores also correlated well with available experimental half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) data and Boltz-2 predictions for Nirmatrelvir analogues. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the BS approach may serve as an efficient strategy for screening, prioritizing, and accelerating the discovery of next-generation coronavirus Mpro inhibitors.

title: Gut–lung axis in respiratory viral infections: Linking dysbiosis to immune dysfunction
abstract: The gut–lung axis is a critical immunological interface linking intestinal microbiota composition with respiratory health. During viral infections such as influenza and COVID-19, gut dysbiosis—marked by reduced microbial diversity and depletion of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing taxa—has emerged as a determinant of disease severity and immune dysfunction. This narrative review critically evaluates current mechanistic and clinical evidence connecting intestinal microbial alterations with immune dysregulation in respiratory viral infections and explores microbiome-targeted therapeutic strategies. Literature from 2005–2025, including clinical studies, experimental animal models, meta-analyses, and high-impact reviews, was analyzed. Evidence indicates that severe infections are associated with loss of beneficial commensals, including Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Bifidobacterium spp., alongside enrichment of opportunistic pathogens such as Enterococcus and Clostridium spp. Dysbiosis contributes to systemic inflammation via microbial translocation and endotoxemia, amplifying cytokine-mediated lung injury. SCFAs derived from gut bacteria modulate alveolar macrophage function, type I interferon signaling, and regulatory T-cell differentiation, balancing antiviral defense with immune tolerance. Experimental models demonstrate that depletion of SCFA-producing microbes impairs interferon responses and viral clearance, whereas restoration through dietary fiber, probiotics, or defined microbial consortia enhances antiviral immunity. Human studies largely provide associative evidence, highlighting the need for controlled trials to confirm causality and therapeutic efficacy. Integrating microbiome modulation into clinical management may serve as a host-directed strategy, reinforcing systemic immunity through intestinal homeostasis. Future research should focus on defining minimal protective microbial consortia, evaluating safety in immunocompromised populations, and expanding investigation to the virome and mycobiome. Such approaches could complement antiviral therapy, optimize immune resilience, and reduce disease burden in respiratory viral infections.

title: Antiviral and inflammatory immune signatures in anti-CD20-treated multiple sclerosis: a cross-sectional study
abstract: CD20-targeting monoclonal antibodies are highly effective therapies for relapsing multiple sclerosis (MS). We examined how anti-CD20 therapy reshapes antiviral T-cell immunity, innate inflammatory tone, and blood markers of neuroaxonal injury. In this cross-sectional study, adults with relapsing MS were enrolled at two neurological centers in Rome. An immunophenotyping cohort (45 untreated, 25 anti-CD20-treated, all receiving ocrelizumab) was profiled by high-parameter flow cytometry across more than 40 immune populations. A separate antiviral cohort (24 untreated, 13 treated, 19 healthy donors) was assessed for T-cell responses to Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), cytomegalovirus (CMV) and SARS-CoV-2 by activation-induced marker assay, for cytokine and chemokine release by multiplex assay, and for serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) by single-molecule array. Groups were compared by Kruskal–Wallis with Dunn’s correction; correlations used Spearman’s rank test. Anti-CD20 therapy depleted total and switched-memory B cells while sparing antibody-secreting cells and reduced absolute counts of follicular helper T cells and mucosal-associated invariant T cells. Untreated patients with MS (pwMS) showed elevated monocyte interleukin-1β and monocyte chemotactic protein-3 (MCP-3) and impaired pDC cell interferon-α production, whereas pDC IFN-α responses in ocrelizumab-treated pwMS were comparable to those in HD. EBV-specific CD4+ T-cell counts and stimulation index were selectively lower ocrelizumab-treated pwMS, whereas CMV- and SARS-CoV-2-specific responses were comparable across groups. sNfL was elevated in untreated pwMS and correlated with MCP-3 at baseline and after EBV stimulation. Anti-CD20 therapy acts on immune circuits beyond B cells, selectively contracting EBV-directed helper T-cell immunity while sparing other antiviral responses, and identifies MCP-3 as a candidate blood marker associated with neuroaxonal injury in pwMS. report that B-cell-depleting therapy in multiple sclerosis favorably modifies immune activity beyond B cells, reducing Epstein–Barr virus-directed helper T-cell responses while preserving responses to other viruses. They also identify MCP-3 as a candidate blood signal linked to nerve injury.

title: MDL-001: an Oral, Direct-Acting Broad-Spectrum Antiviral for Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) and Chronic Hepatitis In Vivo
abstract: Background/Objectives Endemic viral respiratory illnesses caused by influenza, RSV, and coronaviruses impose a global disease burden of hundreds of millions of infections and hundreds of thousands of deaths annually. Chronic hepatitis B and C infections persist in 254 million and 58 million people worldwide, respectively. No approved therapy addresses these viruses simultaneously. MDL-001 is an oral, direct-acting, broad-spectrum antiviral targeting the Thumb-1 allosteric site of viral polymerases. Methods Here we evaluated the antiviral activity of MDL-001 in vitro in influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, endemic human coronaviruses, and hepatitis B/C/D. We next evaluated MDL-001 antiviral activity in vivo in H1N1, SARS-CoV-2, HCV, and HBV. MDL-001’s in vivo efficacy was compared head-to-head versus standards of care including oseltamivir, remdesivir, sofosbuvir, and tenofovir alafenamide, or through literature comparison with nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Lastly, we evaluated the pharmacokinetics, metabolism, tolerability, and safety profile of MDL-001. Results Here, we report MDL-001 inhibits influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2, endemic human coronaviruses, and hepatitis B/C/D viruses with nanomolar EC90 potency in vitro. MDL-001 demonstrated equivalent in vivo efficacy to oseltamivir against mouse-lethal influenza A virus infection, reducing lung viral load by 2.6 log10 and preventing weight loss and mortality. MDL-001 demonstrated equivalent symptom reduction to subcutaneous remdesivir after SARS-CoV-2 infection. MDL-001 reduced SARS-CoV-2 lung viral titers by 2.9 log10, superior to literature reported 1.4 log10 and 1.0 log10 reductions for nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir, respectively. MDL-001 reduced HCV viremia by 3.3 log10, equivalent to sofosbuvir. Oral MDL-001 reduced plasma HBV surface antigen by 2.5 log10, superior to tenofovir alafenamide from Day 8 through Day 21. MDL-001 demonstrated an in vitro EC50 of 79.4 nM against infection with RSV strain A2, a 416-fold improvement over literature-reported ribavirin. Oral pharmacokinetics studies demonstrate MDL-001 is rapidly absorbed and partitioned into Lung (Kp=39-52) and Liver (Kp=71-104) tissues. MDL-001 produced no treatment-related tolerability adverse events across 376 animals and showed no hERG, Ames genotoxicity, or micronucleus safety issues. Conclusions These findings support MDL-001 as a broad-spectrum, direct-acting non-nucleoside antiviral clinical candidate.

title: More Cases, Less Autonomy? The Paradox of Modern Orthopaedic Residency Training.
abstract: Orthopaedic residents may be logging more operations than prior generations, but concerns regarding their readiness for independent practice persist. This apparent contradiction reflects a limitation of case counts: participation does not measure autonomy, clinical ownership, judgment, or the ability to manage complications. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed the vulnerability of surgical training, but declining operative autonomy predates the pandemic. Simultaneously, reimbursement pressure, throughput demands, expanding team-based care, and increasing subspecialization have changed how residents encounter patients and operations. A consequence is increasingly apparent in fellowship, where faculty may need to teach foundational surgical skills before they can teach the intended nuances of subspecialty practice. These changes are not inherently harmful, but without deliberate educational design, they can remove experiences that convert exposure into competence. Case counts should be supplemented by competency-based measures of entrustment, autonomy, and longitudinal clinical ownership. Residency should ultimately be judged by whether graduates can independently evaluate, operate on, and longitudinally care for appropriate orthopaedic patients, with fellowship reserved for subspecialty refinement rather than completion of core surgical training.

title: Identification and Determination of the Main Active Ingredient of Aspen Bark as a Functional Ingredient for Novel Phytocomplexes
abstract: The article presents the results of the development of innovative functional forms of dietary supplements (DS), such as "Populin with Dihydroquercetin" and "Tremulacin," created based on aspen bark extract (Populus tremula).The study aimed to identify and quantify salicin as a key biologically active component ensuring the therapeutic efficacy of the products.The paper describes in detail the technological production scheme, including stages of extraction, standardization, pasteurization, and filtration to obtain a product with specified physicochemical parameters.The authors established strict regulated quality indicators, storage periods, and regimes, ensuring composition stability during industrial scaling.Comprehensive production testing was conducted, confirming the technological feasibility of implementing these supplements into serial production.Particular attention is paid to evaluating the clinical efficacy of the preparations in the therapy of inflammatory and viral pathologies, including infections caused by SARS-CoV-2.The data obtained indicate the high potential of aspen bark extract as a natural corrector of metabolic disorders.The scientific and practical significance of the work is confirmed by a Russian Federation patent for the invention.The research results substantiate the possibility of using these phytocomplexes as specialized products for systemic prevention and supportive therapy in nutrition science, making them a promising tool in modern evidence-based medicine.
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology

title: Growth Failure and Delayed Puberty in an Adolescent with Previously Undiagnosed Advanced HIV Infection: A Case Report
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Longstanding human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) may remain clinically unrecognized until adolescence. Growth failure, delayed puberty, and recurrent or atypical infections may represent manifestations of underlying immunodeficiency but can initially be attributed to other conditions. Case Presentation: A 16-year-old male, adopted at 4 years of age, was admitted with prolonged low-grade fever, chronic productive cough, and recurrent sinonasal symptoms. Marked growth retardation and absent pubertal development were also present. No perinatal or early-childhood medical records were available, and maternal HIV status could not be established. Laboratory investigations demonstrated severe CD4+ T-cell depletion, hypergammaglobulinemia, and elevated liver enzymes. Repeated SARS-CoV-2 antigen/PCR tests were positive, while anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibodies were undetectable. CT demonstrated chronic pansinusitis and hepatosplenomegaly. HIV infection was confirmed by positive ELISA and Western blot, with a plasma HIV RNA level of 127,721 copies/mL. The findings were consistent with advanced HIV infection with severe immunosuppression. Although the clinical history suggested longstanding infection, the timing and route of HIV acquisition could not be established. Similarly, the available SARS-CoV-2 results did not allow definitive differentiation between persistent infection and separate infection or reinfection episodes. Previous CMV IgG positivity had contributed to an earlier attribution of the hepatic abnormalities to CMV, although active CMV disease was not documented. Conclusions: Severe growth failure, absent pubertal development, recurrent or atypical infections, and profound CD4+ T-cell depletion should prompt consideration of underlying immunodeficiency, including HIV. In patients with incomplete medical records, previous diagnoses should be reassessed, especially when the clinical course remains unexplained.

title: Evaluation of Physics-Based Pose Prediction and the Role of Receptor Flexibility in a Community Antiviral Blind Challenge
abstract: Prediction of protein–ligand binding modes is a key step in computer-aided drug design, since incorrect pose prediction inevitably limits the achievable accuracy of downstream physics-based affinity predictions. The ASAP-Polaris-OpenADMET antiviral competition was launched in 2025 as a means to prospectively test computational methods across a range of measurements that guide early prioritization during a drug discovery campaign including pose prediction. Here, we describe our two open-source, physics-based entries to the pose prediction challenge, which are based on templated molecular growth with hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics interatomic potentials. We show that our approach was among the top-performing physics-based methods, and with a retrospective change to the workflow to make greater use of the training data as templates, we obtain a success rate of 74% across SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV main protease target protein structures. Finally, we investigate the importance of receptor side-chain flexibility on retrospective performance. We find that building poses against an ensemble of feasible side-chain conformers is useful in generating improved binding poses but that the tested scoring functions are unable to successfully pick out native structures from the generated ensemble.
journal: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: ARE-Wochenbericht des RKI KW 41
abstract: Die ARE-Aktivität liegt auf Bevölkerungsebene und im ambulanten Bereich auf einem moderaten Niveau, im stationären Bereich auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Das ARE-Geschehen wird momentan hauptsächlich durch Rhino-/Enteroviren und Parainfluenzaviren bestimmt. Die Aktivität von SARS-CoV-2, Influenzaviren und RSV ist derzeit in allen Systemen noch niedrig, jedoch zeigte sich in den letzten Wochen bereits in verschiedenen Systemen ein allmählicher Anstieg der SARS-CoV-2- und Influenza-Aktivität. Es gibt Hinweise, dass SARS-CoV-2 bereits flächendeckend bundesweit zirkuliert.

title: 11 million days of longitudinal Fitbit data reveal novel future health insights
abstract: Abstract Wearable devices offer a scalable, objective measurement of physical activity, but most studies reduce these data to a single metric over 7-days. Here, we compare wearable-derived phenotyping approaches to understand their impact on activity-disease associations, analyzing 11 million days of Fitbit data from 29,303 All of Us Research Program participants. We derive four daily activity metrics (step count, peak 1-min cadence, peak 30-min cadence, and heart rate per step) across five time-windows (1-day, 1-week, 1-month, 6-months, 1-year), then run phenome-wide analyses across > 700 incident and >1,400 prevalent disease outcomes. Though all phenotypes are highly correlated, longer measurement windows yield stronger, more stable associations: 1-year step count was associated with 389 prevalent and 61 incident outcomes (versus 271 and 33 for 1-day step count) after Bonferroni-correction, including novel links to chronic pain syndrome and SARS-CoV-2. Differences between prevalent and incident associations suggest that activity metrics may act as both early markers of disease and risk factors. These findings highlight how large-scale, longitudinal wearable data can advance understanding of health and disease.

title: Development of a highly sensitive photometric readout platform technology using SPAAC-modified HRP liposomes.
abstract: Liposome-based bioassays take advantage of liposomes' immense signaling power and easy surface modification. Photometric, electrochemical, and fluorescent detection methods dominate their application in bioassays. Here, it is studied how covalent modification of the liposome surface with proteins affects the functionality of entrapped enzymes. Horseradish peroxidase (HRP) was selected as a model for entrapment while streptavidin served as a model surface ligand. Several coupling reagents negatively affected the functionality of entrapped HRP. In the case of EDC-sNHS chemistry, membrane-permeable reagents inactivated HRP. Similarly, when applying copper-free click chemistry, in particular strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition (SPAAC), azide-functionalized lipids caused enzyme inactivation probably through coordination with the prosthetic heme iron of HRP. In contrast, the inverse approach employing DBCO-functionalized lipids fully preserved HRP activity. Under optimized conditions with coupling times of only 24 h at room temperature, streptavidin coupling efficiencies reached standard levels. Entrapped HRP was stabilized with 310 mM trehalose and 2 mg/mL HSA enabling storage for up to 6 months after streptavidin modification. HRP-loaded liposomes were evaluated by adapting an assay for the detection of SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies in serum. Therefore, the liposome surface was modified with the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. The RBD-modified liposomes with simple photometric detection demonstrated a similar sensitivity as fluorescent sulforhodamine B (SRB) liposomes, with a strong correlation of both methods (Pearson's r = 0.987). HRP liposomes are hence a reliable platform for visual or photometric bioassays providing similar limits of detection as fluorescent approaches making them ideal for routine lab and point-of-care applications.

title: Analytical Method Development for the Estimation of Molnupiravir: A Review
abstract: Molnupiravir, also known as Lagevrio, is a small-molecule antiviral prodrug of β-D-N4-hydroxycytidine (NHC) that is taken orally and was created to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults who are at risk of developing the illness. Numerous research organizations throughout the world have independently developed and validated a wide range of analytical procedures as a result of this regulatory and analytical gap. These reported methods, which include chromatographic techniques Chromatographic techniques (RP-HPLC, HPTLC, UPLC, LC-MS/MS, and UPLC-MS/MS), spectrometric techniques (direct UV and derivatized/extractive visible spectrophotometry), and electroanalytical techniques (differential pulse voltammetry), are systematically compiled, categorized, and critically compared in this review with regard to important validation parameters such as linearity, sensitivity (LOD/LOQ), accuracy, precision, and stability-indicating capability, as well as emerging green analytical chemistry metrics. While LC-MS/MS and UPLC-MS/MS methods offered better sensitivity appropriate for bioanalytical and pharmacokinetic applications, RP-HPLC methods were found to offer a suitable mix of sensitivity and practicality for routine quality control. Differential pulse voltammetry brought a sensitive, low-cost electrochemical option with a wide linearity range, while spectrophotometric techniques, especially oxidation-complexation procedures, provided straightforward and affordable alternatives with reasonably low detection limits. Overall, this review emphasizes the variety and technical value of current molnupiravir analytical techniques while highlighting the ongoing need for a pharmacopeial method that is validated, standardized, and environmentally sustainable in order to support regulatory compliance and consistent quality control for this clinically important antiviral drug.

These reported methods, which include chromatographic techniques Chromatographic techniques (RP-HPLC, HPTLC, UPLC, LC-MS/MS, and UPLC-MS/MS), spectrometric techniques (direct UV and derivatized/extractive visible spectrophotometry), and electroanalytical techniques (differential pulse voltammetry), are systematically compiled, categorized, and critically compared in this review with regard to important validation parameters such as linearity, sensitivity (LOD/LOQ), accuracy, precision, and stability-indicating capability, as well as emerging green analytical chemistry metrics. While LC-MS/MS and UPLC-MS/MS methods offered better sensitivity appropriate for bioanalytical and pharmacokinetic applications, RP-HPLC methods were found to offer a suitable mix of sensitivity and practicality for routine quality control. Differential pulse voltammetry brought a sensitive, low-cost electrochemical option with a wide linearity range, while spectrophotometric techniques, especially oxidation-complexation procedures, provided straightforward and affordable alternatives with reasonably low detection limits. Overall, this review emphasizes the variety and technical value of current molnupiravir analytical techniques while highlighting the ongoing need for a pharmacopeial method that is validated, standardized, and environmentally sustainable in order to support regulatory compliance and consistent quality control for this clinically important antiviral drug.

title: Mecanismos de acción y eficacia de los antisépticos bucales más utilizados
abstract: Objetivo: analizar la evidencia sobre los mecanismos de acción, la eficacia y los efectos adversos de los antisépticos bucales más utilizados. Métodos: revisión de la literatura con síntesis narrativa en PubMed, SciELO y la Biblioteca Cochrane; se seleccionaron 15 documentos. Resultados: la clorhexidina, catiónica, altera la membrana bacteriana; reduce la placa con certeza alta, causa tinción y disminuye la neumonía asociada a la ventilación mecánica (RR 0,67). Los aceites esenciales redujeron la placa un 27,7 % y la gingivitis un 16 %, y el cloruro de cetilpiridinio aportó un beneficio pequeño. El triclosán redujo la placa y la gingivitis un 22 %. El flúor actúa sobre todo por vía tópica. Los enjuagues mostraron actividad in vitro contra el SARS-CoV-2, pero no redujeron la carga viral en ensayos clínicos. Conclusión: los antisépticos son complementos útiles de la higiene mecánica, con indicaciones específicas.
